docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Item LDM is the standard, governed logical interface for eBay item-domain data, abstracting fragmented underlying physical sources to enable self-service consumption on GDS platform to support business use cases such as data engineering, analytics, and ML feature engineering.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
Understanding Item domain fundamentals:

  • Item, Variation, Product

    Core entity hierarchy: listings (item), SKUs (variation), and catalog references (product/ePID)

  • Attributes vs Aspects

    Two ways to describe items: seller-provided attributes vs SAP-processed aspects with higher quality

  • Variation Traits

    SKU-level differentiators like Color, Size, Network that distinguish variations

Learn core concepts in detail →

docs.title: LDM Relationships and Lifecycle
docs.text:
The catalog contains two LDM types:

  • Governed LDMs provide the consumer-facing item and variation models.
  • Raw LDMs represent source data and behavior. They are grouped according to the source and site application model design.

The relationships below explain how the raw-LDM groups support the listing lifecycle, rather than describing relational-table joins.

docs.title: Current Listing State
docs.text: The governed item and variation entities represent a listing and its SKU-level variations. Their raw current-state data is held in ItemKeyspace. ItemRoot contains the identity and broad state for one item or variation. ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemPriceAndQuantity, ItemDetails, and ItemBusinessPolicies are separate raw LDMs, allowing those portions of the listing to be read and updated independently. ItemLock records one or more inventory reservations for the item. ItemUUIDMapping is a seller-and-UUID lookup that resolves a listing.

docs.title: Shared MSKU State
docs.text: ItemGroupKeyspace holds data shared by the variations in an MSKU listing. ItemGroupRoot identifies the group and references its member items, while ItemGroupDescription and ItemGroupBusinessPolicies hold the shared description and policies. The group does not replace the current state of its member variations: their sellable price, quantity, lifecycle, and other item-specific data remain in ItemKeyspace.

docs.title: Draft Listing State
docs.text: ListingDraft is an independent working-state group used before or during publication. ListingDraftRoot stores draft-session state. An SSKU draft contains ListingDraftItem and can include ListingDraftItemCompatibility. An MSKU draft contains ListingDraftGroup, ListingDraftGroupDescription, and optionally ListingDraftGroupCompatibility, plus one ListingDraftItem for each variation. Draft LDMs do not imply that a corresponding live ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace record exists.

docs.title: Active Draft Discovery
docs.text: UserListingDraftMap is a user-scoped index of active drafts. It connects a user and a draft identifier to summary metadata used to find the draft, but does not contain the full ListingDraft content. Its lifecycle is separate from the draft content: creating, updating, or deleting one does not automatically change the other.

docs.title: Listing Revision History
docs.text: ListingRevisionKeyspace stores historical changes by listing identifier, separately from current state. ListingRevisionRoot is optional retention state. Each ListingRevision records a revision summary and can have multiple ListingRevisionDetail children for listing-property changes and ListingVariationRevisionDetail children for variation-property changes. These LDMs are history records and do not replace the latest ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace data.

docs.title: Access Methods
docs.text:
Spark SQLDDF Python

Query via Spark SQL on DLS:

-- Example: Query active US listings in a specific category
SELECT 
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    slr_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 9355
  AND bin_price_lstg_curncy > 100
LIMIT 100;

Programmatic access via Declarative Data Flow (DDF): Examples to be added.

Migrating from Legacy Hive Tables?

Currently using DW_LSTG_ITEM, DW_ATTR_DETAIL_VALUES, or other legacy tables? See the Migration Guide for step-by-step instructions to migrate your queries to Item Domain LDM.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text: Understanding the foundational concepts in the Item domain.

docs.title: Item
docs.text:
Item

Definition: A listing on eBay's platform. In the data warehouse, item_id (also known as listing_id) uniquely identifies each item.

Characteristics:

  • Can be single-SKU (SSKU) or multi-SKU (MSKU)
  • Contains seller-provided metadata (title, price, description, category)
  • Has attributes (seller input) and aspects (SAP-generated)

Example:

"Apple iPhone 17 Pro for (AT&T or Cricket) - New Open Box, Never Used"

  • Item ID: 227255267188
  • Price: $1,029.99

  • Attributes: Brand=Apple, Condition=Open Box, Processor=A19 Pro, Style=Smartphone, etc

docs.title: Variation
docs.text:
Variation

Definition: A specific SKU within a multi-variation listing, reflecting different product configurations.

Characteristics:

  • Only exists for MSKU items
  • Has variation traits (characteristics that differ across SKUs)
  • Each variation has its own price, quantity, SKU

Example:

For the iPhone listing above, variations might include:

  • Variation 1: Network=AT&T, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue
  • Variation 2: Network=T-Mobile, Storage=512GB, Color=Silver
  • Variation 3: Network=Verizon, Storage=1TB, Color=Orange

Variation Traits: Network, Storage Capacity, Color

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
Product

Definition: Product catalog reference (ePID - eBay Product ID) that groups items representing the same physical entity.

Types:

  • Seller-tagged (PROD_REF_ID): Seller manually assigns ePID during listing creation
  • Auto-tagged (AT_PROD_REF_ID): eBay's Structured Data Adoption team assigns ePID

Relationship:

  • Multiple items (different sellers, conditions, prices) → Same product (ePID)
  • Enables cross-listing analysis and product catalog mapping

Example:

ePID 285507661 = "iPhone 15 Pro" → Links all iPhone 15 Pro listings regardless of seller

docs.title: Entity Relationships
docs.text:
• One item can have 0 to many variations (1:N)
  • Multiple items reference the same product via ePID (N:1)

docs.title: Attributes vs Aspects
docs.text:
Two ways to describe item characteristics. The core difference lies in data source and quality:

Attribute vs Aspect Comparison

Dimension Attribute Aspect Data Source Seller input Processed from attributes by SAP (Search Annotation Platform) Data Quality Raw data, inconsistent format Cleaned, standardized, enriched Generation Seller provides when creating listing SAP extracts, normalizes, and standardizes from attributes Primary Use View Item Page display, basic filtering Search indexing, recommendations, high-precision classification Visibility Buyer-facing (shown on product page) Internal eBay systems (search, recommendation) Example Brand=apple, Storage=256 GB, Color=dark blue Brand=Apple, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue, Screen_Size=6.3" Storage EAV pattern Structured taxonomy with namespace/classifier IDs Tables dw_attr_detail_values, dw_attr_lstg_dtl, dw_attr_shpmt_dtl item_aspct_clssfctn_sap, vrtn_aspct_clssfctn_sap

Why do we need Aspects?

Seller-provided attributes have inconsistent quality (typos, format variations, missing information), which cannot meet the precision requirements of search and recommendation systems. SAP generates high-quality aspects through:

  • Normalization: apple → Apple, 256 GB → 256GB (via UNS - Unified Normalization Service)
  • Enrichment: Extract missing attributes from title/description (e.g., Screen Size, OS)
  • Standardization: Map to unified names/values using UMS (Unified Metadata System)

Real-world Example

Seller-provided Attributes: 

Brand=apple, Storage=256 GB, Color=dark blue

SAP-generated Aspects: 

Brand=Apple, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue, 
Screen_Size=6.3", Operating_System=iOS, Camera_Resolution=48MP

Notice how aspects are standardized and include additional information extracted from the listing.

docs.title: Variation Traits
docs.text:
Traits

Definition: Variation-level characteristics that differentiate SKUs within the same multi-SKU item.

Characteristics:

  • Only exist for MSKU items with variations
  • Describe the specific features that differ across variations
  • Common trait types: Color, Size, Style, Capacity, Network, Material

Purpose:

  • Enable SKU differentiation within the same listing
  • Support variation-level analysis (e.g., which color/size sells better)
  • Help buyers select the specific variant they want

Examples:

For a clothing item with multiple variations:

  • Traits: Color (Red, Blue, Black), Size (S, M, L, XL)
  • Variation 1: Color=Red, Size=S
  • Variation 2: Color=Blue, Size=M
  • Variation 3: Color=Black, Size=L

For a smartphone listing:

  • Traits: Network (AT&T, Verizon, Unlocked), Storage (128GB, 256GB, 512GB), Color (Blue, Silver, Gold)
  • Variation 1: Network=AT&T, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue
  • Variation 2: Network=Unlocked, Storage=512GB, Color=Silver

Key Distinction:

  • Attributes/Aspects describe the item as a whole (e.g., Brand=Apple applies to all variations)
  • Traits describe differences between variations (e.g., Color=Blue vs Color=Silver)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Concept Level Definition Primary Use Item Listing A listing on eBay (SSKU or MSKU) Core entity for product analysis Variation SKU Specific SKU within MSKU item SKU-level inventory/pricing Product Catalog eBay Product ID (ePID) grouping Cross-listing analysis Attribute Item metadata Seller-provided properties Product filtering, classification Aspect Item metadata SAP-processed standardized properties Search indexing, recommendations Trait Variation metadata Variation-level differentiators SKU differentiation

docs.title: Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This guide explains how Core Listing Service (CLS) produces and changes the listing information used by the Item LDM. It uses a small set of canonical business events so users can understand the data without learning every endpoint or storage document. The canonical names are documentation labels; the repository event names are retained as evidence where CLS publishes them.

CLS records accepted listing state. It does not by itself decide final buyer eligibility, checkout price, search or View Item rendering, policy outcomes, delivery promises, orders, refunds, or payments. The Item LDM can also combine CLS state with catalog, classification, warehouse, search, and other downstream sources.

docs.title: Event overview
docs.text:
Canonical business event Action Business description Representative CLS evidence Listing created Produce A seller or authorized workflow submits a new listing and CLS accepts its identity, seller context, and initial listing information. Core item/listing create flows Listing revised Update A seller or authorized workflow changes listing content or configuration, such as title, category, condition, media, shipping, payment, tax, returns, or policies. ITEM.CATEGORY.UPDATED; item/listing update flows Offer or availability changed Update Price, quantity, auction terms, offers, promotions, or inventory availability changes. ITEM.AVL.UPDATED, ITEM.LOCK.EXPIRED Listing lifecycle changed Update A listing is scheduled, activated, renewed, ended, finalized, or relisted. LISTING.RENEW, LISTING.END Listing control changed Update A hold, restriction, administrative action, safety control, or privacy-related control changes the accepted state. ITEM.HOLDSTATUS.UPDATED; administrative and PII operations Listing reconciled Operational signal A migration, dual-write, repair, or consistency process asks other systems to reconcile listing state. LISTING.RECONCILE, ITEM.DUALWRITE.FAILED Listing data removed or privacy-cleared Clear/remove Supported personal information is cleared or anonymized, or a supported entity is removed. Privacy clearing is not the same as ending a listing. PII removal and deletion processors Draft changed Produce/update/remove A seller creates, revises, reconciles, or deletes working draft information. A draft is not a live listing. DRAFT.CREATE, DRAFT.UPDATE, draft dual-write failure signals Derived or exposed state Derived/expose CLS exposes current state and revision history; downstream systems may derive, standardize, or enrich additional Item LDM values. Current-state reads, revision-history reads, downstream Item LDM sources

An event is not necessarily a complete listing snapshot. Some events are facts about a state change, some tell consumers to re-read current state, and some are repair or failure signals.

docs.title: Listing created
docs.text: When a seller or authorized eBay workflow submits a listing, CLS validates and records the listing identity, marketplace and seller context, application or channel information, and initial seller-provided content. Consumers can use this event category to understand when listing state was first accepted, but creation alone does not prove that the listing is live, buyer-visible, or successfully sold.

docs.title: Listing revised
docs.text: When a seller or authorized workflow changes what is being offered or how it is presented, CLS accepts and records the revised content or configuration, including categories, condition, media, shipping, payment, tax, returns, and other listing settings. Consumers can use this category to understand the latest seller-configured listing state, while standardized or enriched values may be supplied by other processes.

docs.title: Offer or availability changed
docs.text: When an inventory or listing workflow changes price, quantity, auction or offer terms, promotions, or availability, CLS records the accepted commercial state and may publish an availability signal. Consumers should treat an availability signal as a prompt to refresh the listing state, not as a complete price or quantity snapshot; listing-currency price is not the final buyer price or checkout total.

docs.title: Listing lifecycle changed
docs.text: When a seller, scheduler, or authorized eBay operation schedules, activates, renews, ends, finalizes, or relists a listing, CLS records the resulting status, dates, duration, end reason, auction outcome, or relist relationship. Consumers can use this category to understand the lifecycle state recorded by CLS, but lifecycle state alone does not establish search visibility, purchase eligibility, checkout availability, or order outcomes.

docs.title: Listing control changed
docs.text: When eBay operations or a safety, administrative, or privacy workflow places a hold, applies a restriction, ends or reinstates a listing administratively, or changes a supported control, CLS records the resulting state. Consumers can use this category to identify controls recorded by CLS, but one control value does not represent the complete policy, fraud, visibility, or buyer-eligibility decision.

docs.title: Listing reconciled
docs.text: When migration, dual-write, repair, or consistency work detects that listing state may need correction, CLS can publish a reconciliation or failure signal for other systems. Consumers can use this category to identify operational coordination, but it should not be interpreted as a seller revision or as proof that every downstream copy has already been corrected.

docs.title: Listing data removed or privacy-cleared
docs.text: When a supported privacy or deletion operation removes personal information, CLS clears or anonymizes the supported values and may remove supported entity state. Consumers must distinguish privacy clearing from listing ending and from physical deletion; the resulting record may continue to exist with specific values removed.

docs.title: Draft changed
docs.text: When a seller saves, revises, reconciles, or deletes a draft, CLS records the seller's working state and maintains draft associations where supported. Consumers can use this category to understand saved seller work, but a draft does not prove publication, buyer visibility, or purchase eligibility.

docs.title: Derived or exposed state
docs.text: After CLS accepts a business event, consumers can retrieve the latest recorded listing state and, where supported, revision history. The Item LDM may also derive or enrich values from catalog, classification, warehouse, search, or dimensional sources. These values should be interpreted using their field definitions and source lineage rather than assumed to be direct CLS writes.

docs.title: Consumer contract
docs.text: Consumers can use the Item LDM to understand listing information accepted by CLS, the recorded commercial and lifecycle state, seller working drafts where applicable, and changes or signals that CLS records or publishes. They must combine it with other data before concluding what a buyer will pay, whether a buyer can complete checkout, how policy or fraud rules were applied, what View Item will display, how an order or payment completed, or what delivery outcome occurred.

docs.title: Source and repository boundary
docs.text:
The Item LDM documentation is broader than the CLS source model. Some fields are derived, standardized, historical, dimensional, financial, or search values from sources other than CLS. The mapping marks those fields as Derived or exposed rather than attributing them to a CLS event without evidence.

During migration between legacy and current listing paths, the same business change can reach different consumers at different times. Current state, revision history, event signals, and downstream LDM values may therefore have different availability timing.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
LDM Name: item

Description: The core listing entity in the Item Domain. Each record represents one eBay listing, containing comprehensive information about title, pricing, category, seller, listing lifecycle, and more.

Primary Key: item_id

docs.title: Fields (228)
docs.text:
item_id LONG

A unique identifier for the listing, generated upon successful creation.

auct_titl STRING

Listing title shown to buyers in search results and on the item page.

subtitle STRING

The listing’s full subtitle text; it can be null if the seller did not provide one

item_desc STRING

Seller-provided item description content encoded in Base64. Decode before displaying or analyzing the description text.

item_desc_lgth_num INTEGER

Length of the encoded item description content.

bin_price_lstg_curncy DOUBLE

Buy It Now price in listing currency in View Item page.

More context

Producer Knowledge

  • Producer Ownership — The team and application that owns and maintains the source data

    • Team Name: SX Inventory Mgmt - Listing Platform Core Services
    • Notification Email: DL-eBay-ListingRedesign@ebay.com
    • OnCall Service: https://ebay-cpt.pagerduty.com/service-directory/$PZMGJDA
    • Service Link: https://cloud.ebay.com/app/detail/crlstngsv/overview

  • Producer Process — How producer applications write data to the source system.

    • Service Name: Core Listing Service
    • Source Code: https://github.corp.ebay.com/SellingDomain/crlstngsv
    • Processes: Core Listing Service produces the listing's Buy It Now price when a seller or authorized eBay workflow creates a fixed-price offer, and updates it when the listing price, promotion, offer configuration, or relist information changes. CLS accepts and stores the resulting listing-currency amount for downstream Item LDM publication. This process does not establish localized buyer pricing, tax, checkout total, or final paid amount.

  • Source Storage — Physical storage information of source data, such as NuDoc keyspace, Oracle db.

    • NuDoc Keyspace Name: ItemKeyspace, ItemGroupKeyspace
    • NuDoc Link: https://qa.cloud.ebay.com/cloud-data/databases/nudocument/keyspaces/ItemKeyspace
    • NuDoc Fields: itemkeyspace.ItemQtyPrice.price.fixedPrice

  • Source Model Design — The data structure written by producer applications, such as source classes.

    • Class: Item.class, ItemGroup.class
    • Field: fixedPrice

  • Change Process — How producer-side changes are released, such as PRs, release notes, schema changes, or standard CI/CD process.

    • 8 releases: https://cloud.ebay.com/app/detail/crlstngsv/ecd?pipelineId=48317243&count=10&pageSize=10&current=1
    • 10 PRs in last month: https://github.corp.ebay.com/SellingDomain/crlstngsv/pulls?q=is%3Apr+

Semantic Knowledge

  • Schema — Entities, fields, data types, primary keys

    • Data Type: double

  • Semantics — Entity and field business definitions

    • Description: Buy It Now price in listing currency in View Item page.

  • Data Lineage (Source → LDM) — How data from source systems is extracted, transformed, and mapped into Logical Data Model (LDM) fields, including key transformation and data-cleaning decisions that turn raw inputs into consumption-ready outputs.

    • Data Flow Summary: Extract itemkeyspace.ItemQtyPrice.fixedPrice from two NuDoc keyspaces (ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace) via ZeroETL, covering five docsets. Consolidate into SSKU and MSKU entities, then merge and transform into bin_price_lstg_curncy at the item level. [AI Summary]

    • Top 1 (~70%): Live inventory scoping filter. Use lstg_status_id = 0. (Use auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE for performance optimization.)
      • Fitment live-listing extract for sellers — defines "currently live."
      • FOD seller experiments — use lstg_status_id = 0 to count each experiment seller's active listings as a metric or feature.

    • Top 2 (~10%): Exclusion of not-yet-started listings. Uses lstg_status_id <> 4.
      • Historical seller listing summary — excludes scheduled (not-yet-live) listings while keeping live, ended, and admin-ended listings for trend statistics.

docs.title: Get US Listings in a Category
docs.text:
SELECT
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    qty_avail,
    item_cndtn_id         AS condition_id,
    slr_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0          -- US site
  AND leaf_categ_id = 9355      -- Cell Phones & Accessories
  AND lstg_status_id = 0        -- Live listings
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Filter by Condition and Price Range
docs.text:
-- New items within a price range
SELECT
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    item_cndtn_id         AS condition_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0          -- US site
  AND item_cndtn_id = 1000      -- 1000 = New
  AND bin_price_lstg_curncy BETWEEN 100 AND 500
  AND lstg_status_id = 0        -- Live listings
ORDER BY bin_price_lstg_curncy ASC
LIMIT 100;

docs.text:
LDM Name: variation

Description: The SKU-level variation entity in the Item Domain. Each record represents one SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) variation of a multi-SKU listing, containing variation-specific pricing, quantity, condition, media, shipping, payment, and policy information.

Primary Key: item_vrtn_id

Relationship Type: Child Entity (belongs to Item via 1:N relationship — gds.variation.item_id = gds.item.item_id)

docs.title: Fields (159)
docs.text:
item_vrtn_id LONG

A unique SKU(stock keeping unit) identifier which stands for each variation of multi-SKU listing. only multi-SKU listing will have item_variation_id.

item_id LONG

A unique identifier for the listing, generated upon successful creation. FK to ITEM.item_id

item_vrsn_id LONG

This column will be populated in the revise process, and will contain a unique identifier for a specific version of an item listing

slr_prdct_id_txt STRING

The SKU (stock-keeping unit) product identifier text defined by a seller.

price_amt DOUBLE

Price for the SKU variation in the listing currency. individual SKUs can have different prices from the listing price in ITEM

orgnl_price_amt DOUBLE

Original Price for the SKU variation when a sale happens. This value will be set by the Mark Down Manager flow.

qty INTEGER

Number of quantity available for this SKU.

sold_qty LONG

Number of sold quantities for this SKU.

dlt_sts_yn_ind STRING

To identify the status of the SKU. The SKU could be soft deleted by the seller. Value of 'Y' would mean the SKU has been soft deleted by the seller.

glry_url_txt STRING

Single gallery image URL for the SKU, usually the first picture URL, shown as extenal picture URL + ";"+ eBay picture URL

auct_end_dt DATE

This is the date that the SKU ended on or is scheduled to end on.

mfo_price_lc_amt DOUBLE

The discount price for "made for outlet" items

map_price_lc_amt DOUBLE

The discount price for "minimum advised price" items

stp_price_lc_amt DOUBLE

The discount price for "strike thru price" items

price_trtmnt_cd INTEGER

the discount price treatment type (1-STP, 2-MAP, 3-MFO, 0-None)

upc_num STRING

UPC(Universal Product Code) code of the SKU

isbn_num STRING

ISBN(International Standard Book Number) number of the SKU.

ean_num STRING

EAN(European Article Number) number of the SKU.

gtin_num STRING

GTIN(Global Trade Item Number) number of the SKU.

incebyprdtdtail BOOLEAN

Indicates whether eBay product details are included for the SKU. Possible values: True = eBay product details are included, False = eBay product details are not included, Null = no value present / not populated.

incstkphtourl BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the stock photo URL is included for the SKU. Possible values: True = stock photo URL is included, False = stock photo URL is not included, Null = no value present / not populated.

bidsfl BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU BIN activity on the listing has concluded . Possible values: True = SKU BIN activity concluded, False = SKU BIN activity not concluded, Null = no value present / not populated.

buyerrstdsbld BOOLEAN

Indicates whether buyer restrictions are disabled for the SKU. Possible values: True = buyer restrictions are disabled, False = buyer restrictions are not disabled, Null = no value present / not populated.

cndidnum INTEGER

Stores the numeric condition ID for the SKU. This is the integer representation of the item condition and is used alongside conditionId and conditionDesc in the listing record.

conditiondesc STRING

Stores the condition description for the SKU. This field contains the human-readable description of the item condition when a textual condition description is present.

conditionid STRING

Stores the condition identifier for the SKU. This field contains the condition enum value used for the listing, such as NEW,USED ,LIKE_NEW,GOOD,VERY_GOOD etc..

creationmode STRING

Stores the creation mode for the SKU. This field identifies how the listing was created, such as Add, Relist, or SellSimilar.

ftmtid STRING

Stores the fitment ID associated with the SKU. This field is used in the listing's fitment/compatibility context and relates to parts compatibility or fitment data.

gblidentifiers ARRAY

Stores the global product identifiers for the SKU. This field is modeled as a list of name/value pairs and can contain identifiers such as UPC, EAN, and ISBN.

invntrytrkmthd STRING

Specifies the inventory tracking method for the SKU. This field determines whether inventory is tracked by SKU or by ItemID

isbuyerresponsibleforshipping BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the buyer is responsible for shipping for the SKU. This field is used for Motors shipping scenarios where the buyer pays or arranges shipping. Possible values: True = buyer is responsible for shipping, False = buyer is not responsible for shipping.

iscreatedbysellsimilar BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU was created using the Sell Similar flow. Possible values: True = created via Sell Similar, False = not created via Sell Similar.

islistedwithnocontactviaemailsupport BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU was listed in a format that does not support contacting the seller by email. Possible values: True = no contact-via-email support, False = email contact support is allowed.

isrestrictedbidding BOOLEAN

Indicates whether bidding is restricted for the SKU. This field is used when the item requires pre-approved bidders. Possible values: True = restricted bidding is enabled, False = restricted bidding is not enabled.

isrestrictedtobusinessuser BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU is restricted to business users only. Possible values: True = restricted to business users, False = not restricted to business users.

isselleronvacation BOOLEAN

Indicates whether seller vacation hold applies to the SKU. This field is used to hide eligible items from buyer discoverability while the seller is on vacation. Possible values: True = seller vacation hold applies, False = seller vacation hold does not apply.

itmonsale BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU is on an active promotional sale. Possible values: True = the SKU is on an active promotional sale, False = the SKU is not on an active promotional sale, Null = legacy.

itmrevsndt LONG

Stores the item revision date for the SKU. This field is a bigint timestamp stored in epoch milliseconds.

mngbyinv BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU is managed by inventory. Possible values: True = managed by inventory, False = not managed by inventory.

onhold BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU is on hold. This field represents the listing's on-hold status. Possible values: True = on hold, False = not on hold.

outofstockdt LONG

Stores the out-of-stock date for the SKU. This field is a bigint timestamp stored in epoch milliseconds.

prgspprtd ARRAY

Stores the list of programs supported for the SKU.

vehpkgid STRING

Stores the vehicle package ID associated with the SKU. This field is used for Motors listings.

videos ARRAY

Stores the videos attached to the SKU listing. This field is modeled as an array of video structures, not a single value.

epr_ecofee DOUBLE

Specifies the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) eco fee for the SKU variation.

epr_prddocid STRING

Stores the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) product document identifier associated with the SKU.

epr_prdpkgid STRING

Stores the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) product package identifier associated with the SKU.

epr_prdcrid STRING

Stores the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) producer identifier associated with the SKU.

epr_shppkgid STRING

Stores the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) shipment package identifier associated with the SKU.

lifecycle_duration STRING

Specifies the listing duration for the SKU, it can be null. and the value 'GTC' means 'GOOD TILL CANCEL'

onfreeshipprtopromo BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU had standard free shipping before it was placed into a promotional free shipping sale. Possible values: True = the SKU was on standard free shipping prior to the promotional free shipping sale, False = it was not.

onfreeshipsale BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU is on a promotional free shipping sale. Possible values: True = the SKU is on a promotional free shipping sale, False = it is not.

aplcbltoshp BOOLEAN

Indicates whether sales tax is applicable to the shipping fee for the SKU/listing. Possible values: True = tax applies to shipping, False = tax does not apply to shipping.

tax_rcgnzbsnsslrvat BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU/listing is recognized as a business seller for VAT purposes.It is a boolean field with values true or false.

tax_thrdprttxctgcd STRING

Stores the third-party tax category code for the SKU/listing.

tax_vatpct DOUBLE

Specifies the VAT percentage for the SKU/listing as a numeric tax rate.

trdscp_intlstvsbl ARRAY

Stores the list of international site visibility targets for the SKU/listing.

autaccptenbld BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Best Offer auto accept is enabled for the SKU. Possible values: True = auto accept is enabled, False = auto accept is not enabled.

bestofrtrms_autacptthrshprc_currency STRING

Specifies the currency code for the Best Offer auto-accept threshold price for the SKU.

bestofrtrms_autacptthrshprc_value DOUBLE

Specifies the Best Offer auto-accept threshold price value for the SKU.

autdclnenbld BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Best Offer auto decline is enabled for the SKU. Possible values: True = auto decline is enabled, False = auto decline is not enabled.

bestofrtrms_autdclnthrshprc_currency STRING

Specifies the currency code for the Best Offer auto-decline threshold price for the SKU.

bestofrtrms_autdclnthrshprc_value DOUBLE

Specifies the Best Offer auto-decline threshold price value for the SKU.

buyerrstrctns_minfdbkscore INTEGER

Specifies the minimum feedback score a buyer must have to be eligible to purchase the SKU when buyer restrictions are applied.

buyerrstrctns_prchsrate_qntylmtperbyr INTEGER

Specifies the maximum quantity of the SKU that a single buyer is allowed to purchase when buyer purchase-rate restrictions apply.

qntylmtperbyr INTEGER

Specifies the maximum quantity of the SKU that a single buyer is allowed to purchase. This field is used to enforce per-buyer quantity limits for the listing.

rstrctbid BOOLEAN

Indicates whether bidding is restricted for the SKU.

rstrcttobsnsusr BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU is restricted to business users only. When enabled, the listing is intended for business-buyer contexts rather than general consumer purchase.

rstrctndate LONG

Specifies the date associated with a restriction for the SKU. This field can be used to capture the effective, recorded, or applicable date of a buyer or listing restriction for downstream processing.

unpaidtranthrsh_count INTEGER

Specifies the unpaid-transaction count threshold used for the SKU.

byrrstrctdsbld BOOLEAN

Indicates whether buyer restrictions are disabled for the SKU. When enabled, buyer-restriction rules are not enforced for the listing.

cashondlvryfee_currency STRING

Specifies the currency used for the cash-on-delivery fee applied to the SKU. This field identifies the monetary denomination for the COD fee amount.

cashondlvryfee_value DOUBLE

Specifies the cash-on-delivery fee amount applied to the SKU. This field stores the fee charged when the buyer selects cash on delivery as the payment method.

dgtdlvlgsplsprt BOOLEAN

Flag to determine if the item can be delivered as a digital good

ebaymgdshpng BOOLEAN

Indicates whether eBay Managed Shipping is enabled for the SKU.Possible values: True = eBay Managed Shipping is enabled, False = eBay Managed Shipping is not enabled, Null = no value present / not populated.

freeshipavail BOOLEAN

Indicates whether free shipping is available for the SKU.Possible values: True = free shipping is available, False = free shipping is not available.

gsplgstcplnsprtd BOOLEAN

Flag to indicate if the item is listed using an Intermediated Shipping enabled business profile

ispulgstcplsprt BOOLEAN

Flag to determine if an item is eligible for pickup in store or not

mfulfillmentsprt BOOLEAN

Indicates whether managed fulfillment is supported for the SKU.Possible values: True = managed fulfillment is supported, False = managed fulfillment is not supported, Null = no value present / not populated.

mgdshpngcstpdby STRING

Specifies who(Buyer vs Seller) pays the managed shipping cost for the SKU. It can be null. This field is part of the managed shipping or fulfillment terms and is stored as a managed-shipping-cost-paid-by .

mgdshpngoptin BOOLEAN

Indicates whether managed shipping is opted in for the SKU.Possible values: True = managed shipping is opted in, False = managed shipping is not opted in, Null = no value present / not populated.

ovrridshipoptn ARRAY

Stores the list of override shipping options for the SKU. It is used when the seller overrides the flat shipping costs in the Business Policies shipping profile for domestic or international shipping services.

pkgspec_depth DOUBLE

Specifies the package depth for the SKU. This field stores the depth component of the shipping package dimensions associated with the SKU and is part of the package-dimension structure used to define a shipping package.

pkgspec_length DOUBLE

Specifies the package length for the SKU. This field stores the length component of the shipping package dimensions associated with the SKU and is used together with width and depth to define the full package size for shipping-related processing.

pkgspec_width DOUBLE

Specifies the package width for the SKU. This field stores the width component of the shipping package dimensions associated with the SKU and is used together with length and depth as part of the package specification for shipping.

irregularpackage BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the shipping package for the SKU has an irregular or non-standard shape. Possible values: True = the package has an irregular shape, False = the package does not have an irregular shape.

unitofmeasure STRING

Specifies the unit of measure associated with the SKU. This field identifies the measurement unit used to interpret related quantity, weight, dimension, or package-specific values stored for the SKU.

pkgspec_majorweight DOUBLE

Specifies the major weight component of the package specification for the SKU. This field stores the higher-order weight value used in package definition, typically representing the primary weight unit for shipment calculation.

pkgspec_minorweight DOUBLE

Specifies the minor weight component of the package specification for the SKU. This field stores the lower-order weight value used along with the major weight component to represent the complete package weight for the SKU.

pymtplcyid_plcyvrsn STRING

Stores the version of the payment business policy used for the SKU. This helps identify which version of the payment policy was associated with the listing record.

pymtplcyid_policyid STRING

Stores the identifier of the payment business policy associated with the SKU.

rtrnsplcyid_plcyvrsn STRING

Stores the version of the returns business policy used for the SKU. This helps identify which version of the returns policy was associated with the listing record.

rtrnsplcyid_policyid STRING

Stores the identifier of the returns business policy associated with the SKU.

shipplcyid_plcyvrsn STRING

Stores the version of the shipping business policy used for the SKU. This helps identify which version of the shipping policy was associated with the listing record.

shipplcyid_policyid STRING

Stores the identifier of the shipping business policy associated with the SKU.

galldurtn STRING

Specifies the gallery duration for the SKU listing. This captures how long the gallery enhancement is applied; example values may include Days_7,Lifetime etc..

application_id INTEGER

Application identifier used by external consumers for the SKU. It identifies the application or listing tool associated with creation of the original listing and can be used to derive the application name from application metadata. Common examples include 219527 = BOLT, 290356 = BOLT B2C, 384352 = HELIX, 2828 = File Exchange, 114100 = Auto Relist, 161592 = Webinterpret (3rd-party international listing/repricing tool), this is the FK to DW_APPLICATIONS

bold_title STRING

Indicates whether the SKU variation item title is displayed in boldface. Valid values are 0 = not bold, 1 = bold, and blank = legacy historical records not tracked. Does not affect the item subtitle. Not applicable to eBay Motors.

category_prmry LONG

Primary category ID for the SKU listing.

category2_scndry LONG

Secondary category ID for the SKU listing.

country_id INTEGER

Unique identifier of the country where the SKU is physically located, as declared by the seller. This reflects the item location country, not the seller registration country.

created_ts TIMESTAMP

Date and time the SKU variation row was created.

customer_reference_code STRING

Universally unique constraint tag for the SKU. Use UUID to ensure that you only list a particular SKU once, particularly if you are listing many SKUs at once.

end_code INTEGER

The code that identifies why the SKU ended. Potential values are 0 = NONE, 1 = LOST, 2 = NOT_AVAILABLE, 3 = ERROR_IN_PRICE, 4 = ERROR_IN_LISTING, 5 = END_AUCTION_AND_SELL, 9 = SOLD_ON_PROSTORE, 10 = SOLD_VEHICLE, 11 = END_ITEM_ON_ZERO_QUANTITY, 12 = PRODUCT_DELETED, and 99 = GTC_ENDED.

gallery_type_id INTEGER

Indicates the type of gallery image for the SKU. Potential values are 0 = NONE, 1 = GALLERY, 2 = FEATURED, 3 = UNGALLERY, 4 = UNFEATURED, 5 = HOMEPAGE_FEATURE, 6 = STOCK_PHOTO, 7 = PLUS, 8 = UNPLUS, and -99999999 = INVALID.

item_title STRING

Name of the SKU as it appears in the search results.

last_modified_ts TIMESTAMP

Date and time the SKU was last modified.

location STRING

Seller-provided textual geographical location of the SKU item.

lot_size LONG

Indicates the number of items in the lot for the SKU. A lot is a set of two or more similar items included in a single listing that must be purchased together in a single order line item.

owner LONG

Seller's Oracle user ID associated with the SKU. This is the internal user identifier for the seller and can be used as a foreign key to user LDM.

package_size_package_type_id INTEGER

Shipping package type code for the SKU. It identifies the package format used to ship the item(s). Values are 0 = None/not specified, 4 = Package/Thick Envelope, 1 = Letter, 26 =PaddedBags, 5 = USPSLargePack, 2 = Large Envelope, 19 = ParcelOrPaddedEnvelope, 29 = MailingBoxes, 27 = ToughBags, 21 = MediumCanadaPostBox, 22 = LargeCanadaPostBox, 24 = MediumCanadaPostBubbleMailer, 17 = ExtraLargePack 30 = Winepak, and 7 = UPS Letter.

photo_display_type INTEGER

Photo display mode code for the SKU variation. Valid values are -99999999 = invalid, 1 = Slide Show, 2 = Large Photo Show, 3 = Picture Pack, 4 = EPS Picture Show, 5 = Self Hosted Picture Show, and 6 = SuperSize Picture Show.

picture_url STRING

URL(s) of the View Item pictures for the SKU. Multiple URLs may appear semicolon-delimited.

private_sale_ind STRING

Indicates whether the SKU is a private listing where bidder identities are hidden. Values are 0 = not private and 1 = private.

sale_end_ts TIMESTAMP

Timestamp when the SKU actually becomes ended on eBay.

sale_sched_end_ts TIMESTAMP

Timestamp when the SKU is scheduled to end on eBay.

sale_start_ts TIMESTAMP

Timestamp when the SKU becomes active on eBay.

seller_product_id STRING

Seller-defined product identifier text for the SKU.

site_id INTEGER

Site ID where the SKU is listed.

sku_num STRING

Seller's custom, application-specific data associated with the SKU. This data is stored by eBay for the seller and is not used by eBay in any way.

storefront_category2 LONG

Unique identifier for the secondary custom Store category for the SKU. Set this field to a root-level custom category or a custom category that has no child categories (subcategories).

storefront_flags LONG

Unique identifier of the primary custom Store category for the SKU. This represents the primary custom category associated with the store listing; sellers can associate each listing with up to two custom Store categories.

subtitle STRING

Contains the full text of the subtitle for the SKU. This value can be null if not supplied by the seller.

super_featured STRING

Indicates whether the SKU is a super-featured (top-of-category) listing upgrade. Values are 0 = not super-featured, 1 = super-featured, and empty string = legacy records.

tax_new DOUBLE

Seller-provided sales tax percentage for the SKU.

tax_new_state STRING

State or jurisdiction for which sales tax is collected for the SKU.

gtc BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU is a Good 'Til Cancelled (GTC) listing.Possible values: True = GTC listing, False = not a GTC listing.

relist BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU was created using the Relist flow.Possible values: True = created via Relist, False = not created via Relist.

weight LONG

Item weight for the SKU in the unit specified by WEIGHT_UNIT_TYPE.

weight_unit_type INTEGER

Indicates the unit of weight for the SKU. Valid values are 1 = Ounces and 2 = Grams.

sale_type LONG

Appropriate SaleTypeEnum code for the SKU. Only fixed_price listings can have SKU variations

prcguarantee BOOLEAN

Indicates whether the SKU has a price guarantee. This boolean field identifies whether the SKU is enrolled in a price-guarantee or price-protection condition. Possible Values True , False .

itemqtypriceid STRING

Stores the identifier for the item quantity pricing associated with the SKU.

currency_id INTEGER

Specifies the currency identifier for the SKU. It indicates the currency in which the SKU value is expressed and maps to supported currency codes such as 1 = USD, 2 = CAD, 3 = GBP, 5 = AUD, 6 = JPY, and 7 = EUR. FK to dw_currencies.

bin_price_lstg_currency DOUBLE

Specifies the Buy It Now price of the SKU variation in the listing currency. This field stores the fixed-price amount associated with the variation in the currency used for the listing.

original_price DOUBLE

Specifies the original price of the SKU variation before any promotional or markdown sale discount is applied. This field stores the pre-discount price used as the reference value for comparison against the discounted selling price.

reserve_price_lstg_currency DOUBLE

Lowest price at which the seller is willing to sell the SKU in an auction listing. START_PRICE must be lower than RESERVE_PRICE. Value 0 indicates that no reserve price is set.

start_price_lstg_currency DOUBLE

Start price for the SKU in listing currency. For fixed-price SKU, this is the Buy It Now price; for auction or Dutch listing, it is the opening bid price.

daystofulpmt STRING

Specifies the number of days allowed for full payment for the SKU. This field defines the payment window within which the buyer is expected to complete the full payment after the purchase or commitment. It is used to enforce or track payment timing requirements for the listing.

pmttrms_depamt_currency STRING

Specifies the currency code for the deposit amount required for the SKU. This field identifies the currency in which the deposit amount is defined, ensuring that the deposit value is interpreted correctly in the payment terms. It should align with the currency used for the related payment or listing context.

pmttrms_depamt_value DOUBLE

Specifies the deposit amount required for the SKU as part of its payment terms. This field stores the monetary amount that must be paid upfront as a deposit. It is used together with the deposit currency and deposit timing fields to define the complete deposit requirement.

deprqd BOOLEAN

Indicates whether a deposit is required for the SKU. This boolean flag identifies whether the listing requires the buyer to pay an upfront deposit as part of the payment terms. A value of true means a deposit applies, while false means no deposit is required.

hrstodep INTEGER

Specifies the number of hours allowed to make the deposit for the SKU. This field defines the deadline for the buyer to submit the required deposit after purchase or commitment. It is used along with the deposit amount and deposit-required flag to control deposit payment terms.

pmtmthd ARRAY

Stores the list of payment methods accepted for the SKU. This field is part of the payment terms in the business policy and is modeled as an array of PaymentMethod values, so it can contain multiple accepted payment methods for the same SKU rather than a single flag. Downstream boolean payment fields such as COD, CashInPerson, Discover, LoanCheck, MOCC, OtherOnlinePayments, PaymentSeeDescription, PersonalCheck, and VisaMC are derived by checking whether those values are present in pmtMthd.

amex BOOLEAN

Indicates whether American Express is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = American Express is accepted, False = American Express is not accepted.

cod BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Cash on Delivery is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. When this option is enabled, the buyer pays for the item at the time of delivery instead of paying in advance through an online payment flow. This field is used to identify whether the SKU supports COD as one of its available payment methods. Possible values: True = COD is accepted, False = COD is not accepted.

codprepaydelivery BOOLEAN

Indicates whether COD pre-pay delivery is enabled for the SKU. This field identifies whether the SKU supports the CODPrePayDelivery payment method as part of its listing payment terms. Possible values: True = COD pre-pay delivery is enabled, False = COD pre-pay delivery is not enabled.

discover BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Discover is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = Discover is accepted, False = Discover is not accepted.

loancheck BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Loan Check is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = Loan Check is accepted, False = Loan Check is not accepted.

mocc BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Money Order or Cashier's/Bank Check is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = MOCC is accepted, False = MOCC is not accepted.

other BOOLEAN

Indicates whether other forms of payment are accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = other forms of payment are accepted, False = they are not accepted.

otheronlinepayments BOOLEAN

Indicates whether other online payments are accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = other online payments are accepted, False = they are not accepted.

paymentseedescription BOOLEAN

Indicates whether PaymentSeeDescription is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = PaymentSeeDescription is accepted, False = PaymentSeeDescription is not accepted.

paypal BOOLEAN

Indicates whether PayPal is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = PayPal is accepted, False = PayPal is not accepted.

postaltransfer BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Postal Transfer is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. Possible values: True = Postal Transfer is accepted, False = Postal Transfer is not accepted.

prepaydelivery BOOLEAN

Indicates whether PrePayDelivery is accepted as a payment option for the SKU.Possible values: True = PrePayDelivery is accepted, False = PrePayDelivery is not accepted.

visamc BOOLEAN

Indicates whether Visa or MasterCard is accepted as a payment option for the SKU. This field maps to the VisaMC payment method in listing/payment policy terms, and internal payment method definitions describe VisaMC as "Visa/Mastercard." Possible values: True = Visa or MasterCard is accepted, False = Visa or MasterCard is not accepted.

payment_cc STRING

Indicates whether credit card payment is accepted as a payment method for the SKU. Values: "0"=no, "1"=yes, empty string=legacy records.

payment_moneyxfer STRING

Indicates whether direct money transfer is accepted as a payment method for the SKU. Values: "0"=no, "1"=yes, empty string=legacy records.

docs.title: Get Active SKUs for a Listing
docs.text:
SELECT
    item_vrtn_id,
    item_id,
    price_amt,
    qty,
    sold_qty,
    item_title
FROM gds.variation
WHERE item_id = 123456789
  AND dlt_sts_yn_ind <> 'Y'  -- exclude soft-deleted SKUs
ORDER BY item_vrtn_id;

docs.title: Aggregate SKU Inventory for Multi-SKU Listings
docs.text:
SELECT
    item_id,
    COUNT(item_vrtn_id)    AS sku_count,
    SUM(qty)               AS total_qty,
    SUM(sold_qty)          AS total_sold,
    MIN(price_amt)         AS min_price,
    MAX(price_amt)         AS max_price
FROM gds.variation
WHERE dlt_sts_yn_ind <> 'Y'
GROUP BY item_id
HAVING COUNT(item_vrtn_id) > 1;

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: How to migrate from legacy Hive tables to Item Domain LDM.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Item Domain LDM consolidates multiple fragmented Hive tables into unified logical entities. This guide helps you migrate existing queries to the new LDM interface.

Benefits of migrating:

  • Simpler queries: Query by business concepts instead of physical table names
  • Better performance: Optimized materialized views on DLS
  • Unified interface: Consistent access pattern across all item-related data
  • Governed data: Standardized, quality-controlled data models

docs.title: Step 1: Identify Your Legacy Sources
docs.text: List the legacy Hive tables and fields used by your current query. Use the reference below to find the corresponding Item Domain LDM entity.

docs.title: Step 2: Check Fields and Replace with LDM Entities
docs.text: Confirm the required fields exist in the target LDM entity, then replace legacy table and field references with the corresponding gds.* LDM entity and LDM fields. Most migrations are table or field substitutions.

docs.title: Step 3: Test and Validate
docs.text: Compare results between legacy and LDM queries to ensure row counts, filters, and key business metrics remain consistent.

docs.title: Basic Item Query
docs.text:
Migrate from DW_LSTG_ITEM to gds.item.

Before (Legacy)After (LDM) 
SELECT 
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    slr_id,
    item_site_id
FROM DW_LSTG_ITEM
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE
LIMIT 100;

SELECT 
    item_id,
    auct_titl             AS title,
    bin_price_lstg_curncy AS price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    slr_id,
    item_site_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE
LIMIT 100;

Changes: - ✅ Replace DW_LSTG_ITEM → gds.item - ✅ Column names remain the same - ✅ WHERE clause unchanged

docs.title: Migrating Flag Fields
docs.text:
In legacy DW tables, many item indicator attributes were packed into bit-level flag columns such as flags, flags2, flags09, flags12, passwrd, passwordex, sale_status, and visitcount. In Item LDM, these decoded flags are exposed directly as individual 0/1 integer columns, so consumers should select the LDM column instead of repeating bitwise logic in every query.

Before (Legacy)After (LDM) 
SELECT
    item_id,
    CASE WHEN (CAST(flags AS BIGINT) & 262144) = 262144 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_seller_on_vacation
FROM DW_LSTG_ITEM;

SELECT
    item_id,
    is_seller_on_vacation
FROM gds.item;

Migration rule: replace each legacy bit extraction expression with the corresponding Item LDM 0/1 indicator column. If your downstream query needs boolean semantics, compare the LDM column to 1 (for example, is_seller_on_vacation = 1).

docs.title: Migration Checklist
docs.text:
Before migrating your queries:

  • Identify all legacy tables used in your current queries
  • Map each legacy table to its corresponding LDM entity
  • Update table references from legacy to gds.* schema
  • Test queries in development environment
  • Validate results match legacy query output
  • Update downstream dependencies (dashboards, reports, pipelines)
  • Document migration for your team

docs.title: Example 1: Basic Item Query
docs.text:
Get basic information for items in a specific category:

SELECT 
    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    item_quantity,
    seller_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0           -- US site
  AND item_cndtn_id = 1000       -- New condition
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Modeling Strategy
docs.text: This document explains the unified strategy for identifying entities, attributes, and relationships in Logical Data Model Design.

docs.title: 1. Entity
docs.text: A business object that satisfies the following identification principles:

docs.title: Principle 1: Unique Identifier
docs.text: Has unique identifier that represents individual instance.

docs.title: Principle 2: Independent Lifecycle
docs.text: Can be created, updated, or deleted independently of other entities.

docs.title: Principle 3: Referenced by Multiple Entities
docs.text:
Participates in relationships with multiple entities.

Examples: - ✅ Item - has item_id, independent lifecycle, relates to Variation/Product - ✅ Product - has product_id (ePID), exists independently, referenced by multiple items - ✅ Trait - individual instance referenced by multiple entities

docs.title: 2. Entity Attribute
docs.text:
A property that belongs to and describes a single entity. It has no independent existence outside the entity.

Examples: - item_title - describes Item

docs.title: 3. Relationship
docs.text: A connection between two or more entities. Relationships can be one-to-many (1:N), many-to-one (N:1), or many-to-many (M:N).

docs.title: 1:N (One-to-Many) / N:1 (Many-to-One)
docs.text:
One entity instance can be associated with multiple instances of another entity. Foreign key resides in the "many" side.

Example: Item → Variation 

Item (1) ─────< Variation (N)

One item has multiple variations

docs.title: M:N (Many-to-Many)
docs.text:
Multiple instances on both sides can be associated with each other.

Example: Item ↔ Attribute 

Item (M) >─────< Attribute (N)

An Item can have multiple Attributes
An Attribute can be used by multiple Items

docs.title: 4. Relationship Attribute
docs.text:
A property that belongs to the relationship between two entities, not to either entity alone. It describes the connection, not the entities themselves.

Examples: - photo_count - in Item ↔ Trait mapping, describes how many photos this item has for this trait

docs.title: Step 2: LDM Definition
docs.text: Based on Step 1 identification, define logical data models:

docs.title: Entity → LDM
docs.text:
• Create dedicated LDM for each entity
  • Primary key: entity's unique identifier
  • Fields: entity attributes

docs.title: Relationship → LDM Structure
docs.text:
• 1:N / N:1: Foreign key in the "many" side's LDM
  • M:N:
  • Long-term vision: Query entity LDMs directly, system auto-materializes joins
  • Short-term approach: Create mapping LDM (see Step 3 for details)

docs.title: Relationship Modeling and Querying
docs.text:
1. For 1:N / N:1 Relationships

Query from the "many" side entity:

-- Example: Get variations for an item (1:N)
SELECT 
    v.item_id,
    v.variation_id,
    v.variation_sku,
    v.variation_price
FROM gds.variation v
WHERE v.item_id = 123456789;

2. For M:N Relationships

Current Approach - Pre-joined denormalized mapping tables are modeled as LDM entities for direct consumption:

Relationship Mapping LDM Name Primary Keys Physical Sources Details Item ↔ Attribute Value (Common Attributes) item_common_attribute_value_mapping item_id, attr_id, value_id DW_ATTR_DETAIL_VALUES View Details → Item ↔ Attribute Value (Listing) item_listing_attribute_value_mapping item_id, gcs_id, vcs_id, lstg_attr_id, value_id, value_desc DW_ATTR_LSTG_DTL Item ↔ Attribute Value (Shipment) item_shipment_attribute_value_mapping item_id, gcs_id, vcs_id, shpmt_attr_id, value_id, value_desc DW_ATTR_SHPMT_DTL DW_ATTR_SHPMT_DTL_COLD Item ↔ Attribute Value (Fitment) item_fitment_attribute_value_mapping item_id, auct_end_dt, ftmnt_grp_id, ftmnt_name, ftmnt_value_text, src_ind, cmbntn_grp_id DW_LSTG_ITEM_FTMNT Item ↔ Attribute Value (Tags) item_tag_attribute_value_mapping item_id, gcs_id, vcs_id, lstg_attr_id, tag_name, tag_value_txt DW_ATTR_LSTG_TAG_DTL Item ↔ Attribute Value (Tax) item_tax_attribute_value_mapping item_id, sale_tax_rate, jrsdctn_cntry_id, jrsdctn_tx LSTG_SALE_TAX Item ↔ Picture item_picture_mapping item_id, trait_name LSTG_ITEM_PIC Item ↔ Aspect Value item_aspect_value_mapping item_id, aspect_name, aspect_value_name ITEM_ASPCT_CLSSFCTN_SAP Variation ↔ Aspect Value variation_aspect_value_mapping variation_id, aspect_name, aspect_value_name VRTN_ASPCT_CLSSFCTN_SAP Variation ↔ Trait variation_trait_mapping variation_id, trait_name LSTG_ITEM_VRTN_TRAIT 
-- Example: Get item attributes using mapping table
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.auct_titl AS title,
    m.attr_id,
    m.value_desc
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_id = 1000
LIMIT 100;

Future Vision - The long-term vision is to abstract M:N relationships into more intuitive entity-relationship models with dynamic materialization on DDF. This follows the modeling strategy described in this document.

docs.title: Step 3: Physical Source Mapping
docs.text: Map physical Hive tables to LDMs based on table granularity and type.

docs.title: 1. Granularity Analysis
docs.text:
Analyze physical table primary key structure to determine granularity:

  • Single entity key (e.g., item_id) → Entity table
  • Composite key with two entity FKs (e.g., item_id + attr_id) → Relationship table (M:N)
  • Composite key with entity FK + dimensions (e.g., item_id + snapshot_date) → Historical/SCD table
  • Aggregated dimensions (e.g., category_id + date) → Summary table

docs.title: Entity Tables → Entity LDM
docs.text:
Physical tables with entity-level granularity map to entity LDMs.

  • Single source: One physical table → One LDM (e.g., CTLG_PROD_FACT → product)
  • Multi-source: Multiple physical tables → One LDM (e.g., 11 tables → item)
  • Principle: One field has one source table (for given update frequency)
  • Merge complementary attributes from different sources

docs.title: Relationship Tables → Mapping LDM (M:N)
docs.text:
Short-term Approach: Physical M:N tables map directly to mapping LDMs with pre-denormalized attributes.

Mapping LDMs include not just foreign keys, but also denormalized entity attributes and relationship attributes.

Example: dw_attr_detail_values (physical table) → item_common_attribute_value_mapping (mapping LDM) 

-- Physical table structure
item_id, attr_id, value_id, attr_name, value_desc

-- Maps to: Item (M) ↔ Attribute (N)
-- Denormalized: attr_name, value_desc
-- Relationship attributes: none in this case

Benefits: Faster queries, simpler SQL (2-table join instead of 3-table join)

docs.title: SCD2 Tables → Entity/Relationship LDM with Temporal Filtering
docs.text:
Physical SCD2 tables track historical changes over time.

Mapping approach: - Map to corresponding entity or relationship LDM - Add temporal filtering logic in queries

Example: an entity history table with effective start/end timestamps 

-- Current state query
WHERE eff_end_dt IS NULL

-- Point-in-time query  
WHERE snapshot_date BETWEEN eff_start_dt AND eff_end_dt

docs.title: Summary Tables → Typically Not Modeled
docs.text:
Aggregated summary tables contain pre-computed metrics and typically are not modeled as LDMs.

Rationale: - Different granularity (aggregated vs entity-level) - Pre-computed views, not source of truth - Query directly from physical table when needed

Example: CTLG_BRWS_NODE_SD (browse node summary by date) - used as-is, not abstracted into LDM

docs.title: 3. Long-term Vision: DDF Dynamic Materialization
docs.text:
In the future, the platform's Declarative Data Flow (DDF) capability will enable:

  • Dynamic Materialization: Automatically optimize M:N joins based on query patterns
  • Transparent Performance: No manual denormalization needed
  • Simplified Queries: Users query entity LDMs directly, system auto-generates mapping tables

Note: DDF is a long-term roadmap item. For now, use the pre-denormalized mapping LDMs provided.

docs.title: Sample Data vs. Schema Alignment Report
docs.text:
This page documents the findings from cross-checking all 22 raw LDM JSON sample files (under data/sample-data/item-raw-ldm-samples/) against their corresponding schema definition pages in docs/entities/.

Each schema is rated:

  • 🟢 Aligned — data matches schema; no corrections needed
  • 🟡 Partially aligned — content matches but schema documentation has gaps or omissions
  • 🔴 Misaligned — documented field format or name is factually wrong in the schema

docs.title: Critical Corrections (🔴 Must Fix)
docs.text:
Three schemas document primary-key ID generation patterns that do not match actual data. The prefixes are condensed in production; underscores documented in the schema are absent in reality.

Schema Field Documented Format Actual Format itemkeyspace-business-policies.md plcsId BIZ_POL_<itemId> BIZPOL_<itemId> itemkeyspace-item-details.md itemDetailsID ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId> ITEMDET_<itemId> itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md ItemQtyPriceID QTY_PRICE_<itemId> QTYPRICE_<itemId>

Action: Update the "ID Generation" examples (and the existing review-notes table in ldm-review-notes.md) for these three pages to use the correct prefix strings.

Note: the GroupBusinessPolicies schema inherits its field shape from ItemBusinessPolicies; its plcsId values in sample data use BIZPOL_<groupId>, confirming the same prefix convention applies to the group-level counterpart.

docs.title: 1 — ItemGroupKeyspace / GroupBusinessPolicies
docs.text:
File: ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupBusinessPolicies.json Schema: itemgroupkeyspace-group-business-policies.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (plcsId, retTrms, pmtTrms, shipTrms) are present and correctly structured. The BIZPOL_<groupId> prefix convention used in plcsId is consistent but not explicitly stated in the schema text.

Gap: Schema does not document the BIZPOL_ prefix convention for plcsId.

docs.title: 2 — ItemGroupKeyspace / GroupDescription
docs.text:
File: ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupDescription.json Schema: itemgroupkeyspace-group-description.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

groupDescId, groupDesc, compDesc, and grpDescRevsnDt are all present in samples. Some records omit compDesc entirely (not present, not null); some records omit grpDescRevsnDt. Both are valid optional states.

Gap: Schema does not note that compDesc and grpDescRevsnDt can be absent when no compressed form or revision timestamp exists.

docs.title: 3 — ItemGroupKeyspace / ItemGroupKeyspace_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ItemGroupKeyspace/ItemGroupKeyspace_ROOT_.json Schema: itemgroupkeyspace-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (PK, owner, groupTitle, itemIds, itmsVryBy, imgVryBy, images, grpVrs, grpDrftId, mFulfillmentSprt, globalIdentifiers, httpsCmplt, createdDt, lastmodifiedDt, admEndDt, groupType, sellerGroupKey, compat, cmpCompat) are present and correctly typed.

Observation: Within imgVryBy.trtImg, some trait image entries contain only trtVal with no img key — meaning certain variation trait values have no associated images. This is valid but not called out in the schema description of ImagesVaryBy.

docs.title: 4 — ItemKeyspace / BusinessPolicies
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/BusinessPolicies.json Schema: itemkeyspace-business-policies.md Rating: 🟡 Partially aligned — plcsId prefix is wrong in docs (see Critical Corrections above)

Content fields (retTrms, pmtTrms, shipTrms) are fully aligned. Calculated shipping records correctly carry null for shpCost / addUnitCost with a non-null pkgHndlgCost — this pattern is not explained in the schema.

docs.title: 5 — ItemKeyspace / ItemCompatibility
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemCompatibility.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-compatibility.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All 10 sample records show compat, cmpCompat, and ftExempt as null. This is correct for non-automotive items that carry no fitment data. The ItemCompID prefix COMPAT_<itemId> is confirmed by the data.

docs.title: 6 — ItemKeyspace / ItemDescription
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemDescription.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-description.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

ItemDescID, desc, compDesc, and descRevsnDt are all present. Some records omit compDesc entirely; one record has descRevsnDt: null. Both are expected optional states.

Gap: Schema should note that compDesc and descRevsnDt are nullable/optional.

docs.title: 7 — ItemKeyspace / ItemDetails
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemDetails.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-details.md Rating: 🔴 Misaligned — see Critical Corrections above

Content-wise, itemDetailsID and hasRlxdRls match. Optional fields (fixedPriceHP, strtBidPriceHP, docs, srcLstId) are absent from all samples because the sample items do not require them — this is expected.

docs.title: 8 — ItemKeyspace / ItemKeyspace_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemKeyspace_ROOT_.json Schema: itemkeyspace-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

The rich schema (50+ fields) is well-represented in sample data. All major embedded objects (lifecycle, trmsAndPolicies, tax, category, rgltryInfo, vslEncmt, images, aspects, gblIdentifiers) are present and correctly structured.

Undocumented fields found in sample data:

Field in Data Notes pk (lowercase) Appears alongside PK (uppercase) in some records; appears to be a lowercase alias or legacy duplicate images[].extPicUrl External picture URL present in some image entries alongside eBayPicUrl; not in the schema's ImageMap description

docs.title: 9 — ItemKeyspace / ItemLock
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemLock.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-lock.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (pk, st, qty, expDt, cmtDt, cnclDt, extDt, extCnt, crtDt, modDt, uuid) are present. The summary lock record (LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$) uses the same schema with only the aggregate fields populated — consistent with schema documentation.

Observation: The qty field is encoded inconsistently across records: some use {"$numberLong": "1"} (MongoDB extended JSON), others use plain integer 1. Both represent the same value; the schema declares long which is correct in both forms.

docs.title: 10 — ItemKeyspace / ItemQtyPrice
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/ItemQtyPrice.json Schema: itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md Rating: 🔴 Misaligned — see Critical Corrections above, plus undocumented fields

Beyond the prefix error, two additional fields appear in sample data that are not documented in the schema:

Undocumented Field Observed In Notes lifecycle Ended items (e.g., QTYPRICE_110833294592) Contains endDt and schdldEndDt; represents lifecycle data on items that have ended crLstgDtVrs Some records Core listing data version string; documented in ItemRoot but not in this docset

docs.title: 11 — ItemKeyspace / UuidMap
docs.text:
File: ItemKeyspace/UuidMap.json Schema: itemkeyspace-uuid-map.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

listingId and listingAppId are present and correctly typed. The key shape ($UUIDMAP$_<sellerId>/<uuid> encoded in __key[0].string) matches the schema statement that seller ID and UUID are part of the key shape, not document fields.

docs.title: 12 — ListingDraft / ItemDraft
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemDraft.json Schema: listingdraft-item-draft.md Rating: 🟡 Partially aligned — undocumented fields

Content is broadly correct across the rich schema. Two fields present in sample data are absent from the schema's field table:

Undocumented Field Notes origItmId Original item ID from which a Relist or SellSimilar draft was created; critical provenance field invTrkMth Abbreviated form of invntryTrkMthd (inventory tracking method); same semantics as invntryTrkMthd in ItemRoot but with a shortened field name

docs.title: 13 — ListingDraft / ItemDraftCompatibility
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemDraftCompatibility.json Schema: listingdraft-item-draft-compatibility.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

DraftCompID, compat (full propertiesList entries with Car Make, Model, Variant, BodyStyle, Plat_Gen, Cars Type, Cars Year, Engine), and cmpCompat (absent when no compressed form) are all consistent with schema.

docs.title: 14 — ListingDraft / ItemGroupDraft
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemGroupDraft.json Schema: listingdraft-item-group-draft.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (PK, grpTtl, imgsVryBy, img, itmsVryBy, slrGrpKey, bizPol, grpId) are present. The grpId value of "0" for unpublished drafts is a valid sentinel value. The embedded bizPol.plcsId is null for drafts that have not yet been assigned a policy ID.

docs.title: 15 — ListingDraft / ItemGroupDraftCompatibility
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemGroupDraftCompatibility.json Schema: listingdraft-item-group-draft-compatibility.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

DraftCompID and compat (vehicle fitment entries) are present and correct. cmpCompat is absent in samples (expected when no compressed form is written).

docs.title: 16 — ListingDraft / ItemGroupDraftDesc
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ItemGroupDraftDesc.json Schema: listingdraft-item-group-draft-desc.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

PK, groupDesc are consistently present. cmpDesc and grpDescRevsnDt are absent in several records — valid when no compressed description or revision timestamp is stored.

docs.title: 17 — ListingDraft / ListingDraft_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ListingDraft/ListingDraft_ROOT_.json Schema: listingdraft-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields are present. usgHistDtl correctly carries an array of {name: "CREATE"/"UPDATE"/"PUBLISH", value: "<appId>"} entries. appCstmInfo carries an XML string. Flag fields (fl through fl12, scrtchFl through scrtchFl4) are present as documented.

Observation: itmId is typed List<String> in the schema but appears as null at the root level in some records (rather than an empty list). This is a nullable distinction the schema does not mention.

docs.title: 18 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / ListingRevision
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/ListingRevision.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-listing-revision.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (rvsdPrptyGrps, vrsnId, appId, sigRevCnt, vrsnCrtd, rvsdDate, updCrLstgVrs) are present and correctly typed. The GUID-style key ("guid": "AAdcK/x3...") for the ListingRevision collection is the NuDocument internal multi-key format, consistent with the schema note that no persisted key field exists on this class. updCrLstgVrs is absent on older revisions where no version was created — expected.

docs.title: 19 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / ListingRevisionDetail
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/ListingRevisionDetail.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-listing-revision-detail.md Rating: 🟡 Partially aligned — one undocumented field

All core fields (rvsdPrptyGrp, rvsdPrpty, chgTp, newVal, oldVal) are present. lbl is never observed in samples (optional and rarely populated).

Undocumented field:

Field Notes lstRvsnDtlId Appears as {"reference": "<id>"} in some records; appears to be a reference pointer used internally, not exposed as a Java property

docs.title: 20 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / ListingRevisionKeyspace_ROOT_
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/ListingRevisionKeyspace_ROOT_.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-root.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

lstgId and the TTL-maintenance expiredDate field ({"$date": ...}) are both present. The schema explicitly acknowledges expiredDate as an operational field not declared as a Java property, so its presence in sample data is expected.

docs.title: 21 — ListingRevisionKeyspace / VariationRevisionDetail
docs.text:
File: ListingRevisionKeyspace/VariationRevisionDetail.json Schema: listingrevisionkeyspace-variation-revision-detail.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

varId, rvsdPrptyGrp, rvsdVarPrpty, chgTp, and varTraitVals are all present and correctly structured. newVal and oldVal are absent for itmVarChg/add change-type records — expected, since an addition has no prior value. They are also absent for some binPrc/rvsd records, suggesting these fields are conditionally populated.

docs.title: 22 — UserListingDraft / UserListingDraftMap
docs.text:
File: UserListingDraft/UserListingDraftMap.json Schema: userlistingdraft-user-item-draft-map.md Rating: 🟢 Aligned

All documented fields (draftId, mktPlLstdOn, lstgAppId, primCatId, crtMd, eBGenTtl, ttl, imgUrl, stockImgUrl, crtDt, userId, lastModifiedDate) are present and correctly typed.

Undocumented field:

Field Notes ebayGeneratedTitle Appears alongside eBGenTtl in some records as an expanded-name alias (value is always null when present); not documented in the schema field table

docs.title: All Undocumented Fields Across the 22 Schemas
docs.text:
The table below consolidates every field observed in sample data that has no corresponding entry in the schema documentation.

Schema Field Type Notes itemkeyspace-root.md pk (lowercase) String Lowercase alias of PK; appears in same records as the uppercase PK field itemkeyspace-root.md images[].extPicUrl String External (non-eBay) picture URL inside ImageMap; present on some listings itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md lifecycle Object endDt + schdldEndDt; appears on ended/expired items in the ItemQtyPrice docset itemkeyspace-item-qty-price.md crLstgDtVrs String Core listing data version; documented in ItemRoot but also written to ItemQtyPrice on some paths listingdraft-item-draft.md origItmId String Original item ID for Relist / SellSimilar drafts listingdraft-item-draft.md invTrkMth String (enum) Abbreviated inventory tracking method; same semantics as invntryTrkMthd in ItemRoot listingrevisionkeyspace-listing-revision-detail.md lstRvsnDtlId Object ({reference}) Internal reference pointer; not declared as a Java property userlistingdraft-user-item-draft-map.md ebayGeneratedTitle String Expanded-name alias for eBGenTtl; always null in observed samples

Several schemas describe fields without noting that they can be absent or null in practice. The following table lists these, grouped by schema.
