docs.title: ULP Listing Data Reference
docs.text: This reference explains how Unified Listing Platform (ULP) data relates to Core Listing Service (CLS) NuDoc data. It is intended for consumers choosing the correct listing-data surface, not as a physical-storage contract.

docs.title: Scope and evidence
docs.text:
The analysis is based on the three repositories linked locally under .link/:

Repository Role proven by source Not proven by source crlstngsv CLS accepts, persists, reconstructs, and changes core listing state. Its converters map V2 listing objects to NuDoc document families. A complete public ULP API contract or post-listing provider calculations. unilistingsvc The ULP listing-read service supplies ListingV2 and Item, maps fields to groups, gates provider queries, reads cached group data, and refreshes groups from provider events. A provider's storage, calculation, or deployment enablement. fgql The Federated GraphQL Gateway composes the graph, validates and routes requests, and provides local schema snapshots. NuDoc writes, provider business logic, or a guarantee that a snapshot is the deployed graph.

The sources establish a set of related, but different, layers:

Seller or authorized listing workflow
  -> CLS V2 listing aggregate
  -> CLS NuDoc document families
  -> ULP current-listing projection and provider-group cache
  -> FGQL federated GraphQL response

Domain providers and derived-data jobs
  -> ULP provider groups
  -> FGQL federated GraphQL response

Use the following evidence labels throughout this page:

Label Meaning Directly mapped A CLS converter/reconstructor and a ULP field or generated mapping establish the relationship. Family correspondence The sources establish the same business concept at a document-family and API-family level, but not a safe one-to-one leaf-field mapping. NuDoc-only CLS persists or operates on the state, but the normal ULP current-listing contract does not establish an equivalent field. ULP-only ULP exposes the state through a provider or GraphQL contract, but CLS core NuDoc source does not establish it as core listing state. Conditional Availability depends on authorization, gateway exposure, requested group, runtime configuration, or data readiness. Unverified The repositories do not prove exact cross-system lineage or behavior.

Do not equate a GraphQL field with a NuDoc field

Similar names are not sufficient evidence of physical lineage. A ULP response may assemble multiple NuDoc documents, use cached state, add a provider result, transform a nested object, or omit an authorized field. Use the field-tracing procedure before recording an exact mapping.

docs.title: What CLS owns
docs.text:
CLS is the entity service for core listing data. It accepts seller or authorized-workflow state and records it in a producer-oriented NuDoc model. The model is organized by identity, lifecycle, mutation, payload, and lookup needs. It is not designed as a single consumer-facing listing row.

Core business action CLS-recorded state What a consumer must not infer Create listing Initial identity, seller context, product content, terms, price/quantity, and lifecycle configuration. That the item is buyer-visible, purchasable, or sold. Revise listing Seller-configured content and terms, including category, condition, media, policies, shipping, payment, and returns. That every derived, search, risk, or fulfillment value was recomputed synchronously. Change offer or availability Price, quantity, auction/offer state, promotions, locks, or other commercial state. A final buyer price, checkout quote, or fulfilled quantity. Change lifecycle or control state Scheduling, activation, renewal, ending, relisting, holds, administrative actions, and supported privacy controls. Search visibility, fraud outcome, buyer eligibility, or settlement. Save or change a draft Seller working state before or during publication. That a live item or group exists. Record revision history or reconcile state Historical change data, migration/repair, or consistency coordination. That the record is the current listing state or a seller revision.

CLS may dual-write during migration and has reconciliation paths. A reconciliation or failure signal is an operational coordination event, not a complete listing snapshot.

docs.title: Federated write and read boundary
docs.text:
The composed graph exposes seller-authorized createListing, updateListing, relistListing, and endListing mutations. The FGQL schema snapshot assigns those fields to the LISTAPI subgraph, not to FGQL or unilistingsvc. FGQL validates and routes the mutation; CLS source establishes the core listing-to-NuDoc persistence model, but neither boundary alone proves which storage path a particular deployed mutation completed.

ULP lookup operations are read contracts. listingV2ById, listingsV2ByIds, itemsByIds, and sellerListings expose accepted current state; they do not create or revise a listing. During the Oracle migration, core seller-managed data can be dual-written to NuData and Oracle. Availability is a notable cross-domain exception: quantity can change outside a seller revision, such as through a checkout flow moving to Central Availability Service (CAS).

docs.title: SSKU and MSKU data grain
docs.text:
ULP and NuDoc must both be interpreted at the correct grain.

Listing shape NuDoc owner Meaning Single SKU (SSKU) One ItemKeyspace item family, keyed by item ID. One sellable item holds its current item-level state. Multi-SKU (MSKU) shared state One ItemGroupKeyspace group family, keyed by group ID. Holds variation-group identity, member item IDs, variation dimensions, shared content, and shared policies. Multi-SKU sellable state One ItemKeyspace family for each member item, keyed by item ID. Each variation remains a separate sellable item with its own commercial and lifecycle state.

An MSKU ULP response is therefore not evidence that all shared and variation-level state originates in one document. In CLS, the group identifies the member item IDs; consumers must preserve the group-to-variation relationship rather than flatten it into duplicate listing facts.

docs.title: CLS NuDoc current-state families
docs.text:
CLS converters and reconstructors show these producer-side boundaries for live listing state:

NuDoc family Producer responsibility Consumer interpretation ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__ Broad item identity, seller/location, category, format, lifecycle, flags, media references, and listing metadata. Current broad item state; it is not necessarily the full customer-facing listing. ItemKeyspace.ItemQtyPrice Available and sold quantity, remnant rules, and price variants. Commercial state for one sellable item or variation. ItemKeyspace.ItemDescription Seller description and description revision time; stored expanded or compressed when beneficial. One description representation must be selected and decoded deliberately. ItemKeyspace.ItemCompatibility Vehicle/parts fitment and other compatibility payload. Optional, potentially large specialized content. ItemKeyspace.BusinessPolicies Payment, fulfillment, return, tax, and related policy content. Seller-selected terms, not a final buyer-specific decision. ItemKeyspace.ItemDetails High-precision prices, seller documents, and specialized item details. Optional supporting item state. ItemKeyspace.ItemLock Inventory reservations and lock-summary state. Operational reservation state, not a standard listing attribute. ItemKeyspace.UuidMap Seller-and-UUID lookup to item/listing/application identifiers. Operational lookup index, not a listing projection. ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__ Group identity, member item IDs, variation traits, shared images, and group metadata. Shared MSKU state that must be combined with member items. ItemGroupKeyspace.GroupDescription Shared group description. Shared MSKU description, separate from each variation's content. ItemGroupKeyspace.GroupBusinessPolicies Shared group policies. Shared policy state for the variation group.

DocumentConverter, ItemGroupDocumentConverter, and GetItemDocumentConverter provide the core evidence for the write and reconstruction boundaries. Their methods create or reassemble root, description, compatibility, quantity/price, policy, detail, and group documents rather than serializing one universal listing object.

For the full NuDoc hierarchy, primary-key shapes, and draft/history families, see NuData write-flow research and Listing NuData Design.

docs.title: ULP current-listing read contract
docs.text:
The ULP schema defines ListingV2 as the listing entity and Item as the sellable-item entity. The federated schema exposes these normal lookup operations:

Operation Use listingV2ById Retrieve one listing by listing ID. listingsV2ByIds Retrieve multiple listings by listing ID; the schema documentation sets a maximum of 100 IDs. itemsByIds Retrieve sellable item state by item ID. sellerListings Retrieve a seller-authorized listing view when the documented scopes are met.

itemsByVariationIds is deprecated in favor of item-ID lookup. ULP source also contains internal versioned and archived fallback calls; those implementation paths do not, by themselves, extend the normal public current-listing contract.

ListingV2 and Item organize core information into consumer-oriented families:

ULP family Examples in the GraphQL contract Consumer meaning Identity and lineage Listing, item, variation, seller-listing, and core-listing IDs; creation mode; source/relist relationships. Identifies a listing or sellable item and, when populated, its lineage. Seller product Title, description, categories, aspects, condition, images, videos, vehicle identifiers, seller SKU, and variation traits. Seller-defined offer content; it is not a guarantee of buyer-visible rendering. Listing terms Format, duration, buyer restrictions, fulfillment, payment, returns, tax, charity, regulatory content, and seller application data. Accepted or selected terms that may require marketplace and buyer context. Item commercial state Item price, quantity, sold quantity, item-level terms, and variation-specific product state. Recorded sellable-item state, not a checkout quote. Lifecycle state Created/revised times, listing dates and status, end reason, hold state, and relist information. Current or recorded lifecycle state, not a search, risk, or payment decision.

GraphQL type metadata also restricts fields by gateway and, for some fields, by the seller's principal. A field can be part of the source schema while being unavailable in a particular gateway or caller context.

docs.title: Federated response boundary
docs.text:
In normal gateway mode, FGQL validates an incoming request, creates a Federation query plan from the loaded supergraph, makes authenticated subgraph requests, and records the plan and participating subgraphs. The response is therefore a federated API result, not a physical NuDoc record or a transactionally current decision.

FGQL can also proxy requests to a router under static configuration or dynamic ramp rules. That routing mode changes how a federated request is executed; it does not change ownership of listing writes, CLS NuDoc state, or provider business logic.

docs.title: Core coverage: ULP projection versus NuDoc families
docs.text:
This matrix is deliberately at the documented business-family level. It identifies the required NuDoc assembly work and the ULP projection boundary without inventing leaf-field parity.

Business concept ULP surface CLS NuDoc source Coverage Important difference Listing/item identity, seller, category, format, lifecycle, broad metadata ListingV2 and Item identity, seller-product, term, and lifecycle families ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__; ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__ for shared MSKU state Family correspondence ULP is a graph projection; NuDoc divides current item and group state by key. SSKU and MSKU membership Listing/item/variation fields and identifiers Group root member itemIds plus member ItemKeyspace records Family correspondence Group and variation values have different grains and must not be duplicated. Seller description Seller-product/listing description and revision fields ItemDescription or GroupDescription Directly mapped at document purpose; leaf mappings are conditional NuDoc can use compressed content and has separate SSKU/group ownership. Price, quantity, and remnant rules Item commercial fields and seller-price objects ItemQtyPrice Directly mapped at document purpose; leaf mappings are conditional ULP presentation can nest amount/currency and aggregate listing/item context. Compatibility Listing/item compatibility fields ItemCompatibility; draft compatibility families Family correspondence Compatibility is optional and may be excluded from a default cache read until selected. Seller policies and terms Listing and item term/policy objects Item or group business-policy documents; root term fields Family correspondence ULP can restrict fields; API terms are not a buyer-specific outcome. Details, high-precision prices, and seller documents Specialized listing/item fields when exposed ItemDetails Family correspondence The ULP contract does not prove that every optional NuDoc detail is exposed. Locks and reservations No normal current-listing field established ItemLock NuDoc-only Reservation lifecycle is operational and may affect available quantity without being a listing attribute. UUID lookup No normal current-listing field established UuidMap NuDoc-only Lookup key and application association are operational indexes.

Current state is not a transaction

Price and available quantity can change outside a seller revision. ULP and its provider content may be cached and eventually consistent. For checkout, buyer eligibility, payment, delivery, or settlement, use the appropriate owning service rather than treating a listing read as the decision.

docs.title: Listing-event migration
docs.text:
ULP listing events identify a state change, not a full listing snapshot. Consumers should retrieve the current fields they need after receiving an event.

ULP BES2 event Meaning ULP.LISTING.NEW A listing was newly created for the corresponding ULP use case. ULP.LISTING.UPDATED Listing state changed. ULP.LISTING.ENDED The listing entered an ended state; this does not establish a sale or settlement outcome. ULP.LISTING.HOLDSTATUS.UPDATED Hold state changed; interpret detailed hold data only when authorized and available. ULP.LISTING.CATEGORY.UPDATED Listing category state changed.

Legacy BES1 item creation, revision, extension, closure, sale, scheduled-to-active, category, hold-status, and draft events are not payload-compatible with these ULP BES2 events even when they represent the same use case. A migration therefore needs deduplication and loss-avoidance logic rather than one-to-one field substitution. NuData CDC is described as an in-progress alternative for consumers whose need is change capture rather than one of the ULP event families; its delivery semantics must be confirmed with the owning platform.

docs.title: Why provider data is separate
docs.text:
Post-listing data is supplied, derived, or computed by a domain after core listing state exists. It can be updated by domain events or asynchronous jobs, and it does not necessarily share the seller mutation lifecycle or CLS storage.

Examples visible in the schema include derived listing attributes, visibility and searchability, deal state, inventory and shipping-program information, product tagging, regulatory enrichment, SEO image metadata, engagement, and purchase-view metrics. dalasEvaluation, for example, is documented as asynchronous plugin output triggered by backend events; it should not be treated as seller-written core state.

docs.title: Post-listing data families and freshness
docs.text:
The provider schemas complement the following wider post-listing categories. They are business groupings, not a physical-table mapping or a guarantee that every field is available to every client.

Data family Contract examples Consumer boundary Derived attributes and product enrichment dalasEvaluation, autoTagProduct, dynamic aspects, and calculated compatibility. Derived state can be absent or change without a seller revision. Policy, trust, and regulatory state Hold policies/details, regulatory content, country of origin, and energy-efficiency information. A returned value does not alone make the final policy decision for every buyer or marketplace. Search and visibility listingSearchabilityInfo, visibilitySummary, search suppression, and visibility flags. Search can have recovery behavior beyond a default-visible-site value; do not reduce this data to universal availability. Commercial and engagement Promotion state, purchase view, watch count, auction outcome, and deal data. Observed or derived commercial state is not payment, checkout, fulfillment, or settlement data. Inventory and fulfillment enrichment Warehouse locations, shipping-program eligibility, and seller-inventory flags. Mutable availability and fulfillment inputs can change outside a seller's listing revision.

ULP reads and provider state can be cached and eventually consistent. A missing field can mean an unavailable or disabled provider, authorization or gateway exclusion, asynchronous calculation, cache state, connection failure, or an actual empty value. Inspect field-specific GraphQL errors and the provider contract rather than treating absence as a general data-loss signal.

docs.title: Field-group retrieval model
docs.text:
ULP uses named field groups as an internal loading and cache boundary. A field group is not a public GraphQL type and is not proof that all of its fields have one physical store.

Requested ULP field path
  -> generated field-to-group mapping
  -> group-to-subgraph mapping
  -> enabled-provider check
  -> generated FGQL query section guarded by @include
  -> group-level cached response / current provider response

The ULP implementation applies the following rules:

  1. FieldOnDemandFieldGroupLookup loads generated field-to-group, group-to-subgraph, and group-classification JSON files. If an exact field path is not found, it walks upward through parent paths to find a group.
  2. A refreshable defaultFieldGroup configuration can classify a declared group as default; otherwise ULP treats it as on-demand. This runtime setting can override the schema-derived classification.
  3. ListingGraphQLQueryBuilder enables a group only when its mapped provider has queryEnabled=true in external configuration. Default groups are requested whenever enabled; on-demand groups require both enablement and selection.
  4. MonstorFieldMapper converts selected API paths to cache paths, requests an entire provider-group container rather than an independently cached provider leaf, and adds the minimum listing identity/lifecycle/seller context needed for the response.
  5. Provider-event handling maps an event application name through external configuration and refreshes the corresponding group. The source does not establish every production event-producer mapping or delivery guarantee.

The schema-level @onDemand directive is useful snapshot metadata, but it does not on its own prove default/on-demand behavior in a deployment. Similarly, @excludeGroupsInQuery describes exclusions, while the inspected ULP code consumes generated templates and lookup files rather than the directive abstract syntax tree.

docs.title: Snapshot scope and runtime enablement
docs.text:
The local schema snapshot declares 16 @onDemand field groups. The generated ULP lookup files map 24 service groups: 15 classified as onDemand and nine as default. CONNECTEDPRODUCTSULP is the difference: it is annotated on-demand in the schema but has no local generated field-to-group or group-to-service mapping. Therefore, 25 distinct provider-group identities are visible across these committed schema and mapping artifacts. The linked source set currently contains a corresponding repository for all 25. The schema also names 24 field groups in @excludeGroupsInQuery, while the FGQL supergraph snapshot contains 233 Federation subgraphs. These are schema-snapshot inventories, not production provider counts.

The active provider set depends on refreshable external configuration: unilistingcfg.defaultFieldGroup determines default versus on-demand classification, and unilistingcfg.provider.<group>.queryEnabled determines whether a mapped group is requested. Confirm a provider's deployment status from the active configuration and generated environment-specific query template, not from a schema declaration alone.

Fourteen declared groups have a local generated production-query path. DEFAULTULPPROVIDER and CONNECTEDPRODUCTSULP are discrepancies between schema declarations and locally generated artifacts. They are not evidence that a provider is disabled, unavailable, or stale in every deployment.

docs.title: SVLS
docs.text:
SVLS is the broad core-listing read provider, rather than a narrow post-listing enrichment. Its schema contains 104 output object/interface types and 726 output-field definitions, while ULP maps 683 paths to the default svls group. The root-level inventory below keeps this page readable; the core-listing section and svls/svlsService/src/main/resources/schema/SvlsGraphQLSchema.graphqls remain the authoritative detail for the nested contract.

Provider output field family Type and representative fields Description [ListingV2, SingleSkuListing, VariationListing] presentation photos: [Photo!], sellerProduct: SellerProduct, videos: [Video!], productGalleryFallbackURL: String, documents: ListingDocuments, promotionalDetails: PromotionalDetails Seller product and listing presentation data. Listing classification category: ListingCategory, itemCondition: ItemCondition, listingFormat: ListingFormat, listingLifecycle: ListingLifecycle, marketplaceId: ID, marketplace: ListingMarketplace Category, condition, selling format, lifecycle, and marketplace. Commercial and policy terms listingTerms: ListingTerms, totalQuantity: Int, lotSize: Int, autoRelistTerms: AutoRelistTerms, bestOfferTerms: BestOfferTerms, paymentTerms: PaymentTerms, taxInfo: TaxInfo, returnTerms: ReturnTerms, warrantyTerms: WarrantyTerms, buyerRestrictions: BuyerRestrictions, customPolicies: CustomPolicies Listing-level commercial, payment, tax, return, warranty, and buyer-policy data. Fulfillment and location fulfillmentTerms: FulfillmentTerms, itemLocation: ItemLocation, supportContact: SupportContact, tradingScope: TradingScope Shipping, pickup, logistics-plan, location, support, and trading-region data. Lifecycle, relisting, and inventory state draftId: ID, sellerListingVersionId: ID, coreListingVersionId: ID, relistId: ID, sourceListingId: ID, relistParentListingId: ID, endReason: EndReasonEnum, outOfStockDate: DateTime, inventoryTrackingMethod: InventoryTrackingMethod, managedByInventory: Boolean Current listing state, version/relist lineage, and inventory-management metadata. Specialized listing data regulatoryInfo: RegulatoryInfo, vehicleIdentifiers: [NameValuesPair], itemCompatibilities: [ItemCompatibility], visualEnhancements: VisualEnhancements, charity: Charity, ebayCommunity: EbayCommunity Regulatory, vehicle, compatibility, visual, charity, and community data. Item and variation structure items: [Item!]!; variation-only sku: String, minPrice: ConvertedPrice!, maxPrice: ConvertedPrice!, imagesVaryByAspect: ImagesVaryBy, itemsVaryByAspect: [NameValuesPair!]!, listingVariations: ListingVariations Sellable-item state and MSKU variation/group data. Item fields itemIdRestReference: ID, sku: String, itemTerms: ItemTerms, creationDate: DateTime, sellerPrice: ListingItemPrice, itemSellerProduct: ItemSellerProduct, quantityAvailable: Int, quantitySold: Int, extendedProducerResponsibility: ExtendedProducerResponsibility, documents: ListingDocuments Item-specific identity, price, quantity, terms, seller-product, EPR, and document data. Major nested families SellerProduct, ListingTerms, FulfillmentTerms, ShippingTerms, PaymentTerms, ReturnTerms, ListingLifecycle, ItemTerms, ListingItemPricingTerms, ListingCategory, ItemCondition, TaxInfo, RegulatoryInfo, ListingDocuments, and monetary/product types Nested fields provide the detailed product, price, shipping, payment, return, lifecycle, tax, regulatory, document, and identifier contract.

SVLS schema directives explicitly transform several source names and shapes: price to sellerPrice, tax to taxInfo, compatibilities to itemCompatibilities, versionId to sellerListingVersionId, and primaryCategoryId to ListingCategory.primaryCategory.
