docs.title: Provider implementation analyses
docs.text: The following analyses trace all 25 linked provider repositories. They describe provider-local behavior; ULP's group selection, cache container, and deployment-time enablement remain the responsibility of unilistingsvc configuration.

docs.title: basiclistingdata
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. basiclistingdata is a generic store for small application-owned listing and item attributes, not CLS seller-authored core state. Its checked-in federation schema adds watchCount to ListingV2, SingleSkuListing, VariationListing, and Item; it also offers basicListingData and counter mutations. The ULP generated query includes additional basic-listing fields, but their implementation is not established by this checkout.

Core logic and lifecycle. The write mutation validates a ListingV2Input, normalizes it to JSON, then invokes ListingDataService.upsertListingData. The service reads the existing NuData document, skips no-op updates, merges changes, persists through ListingDataDao, and emits an ITEM_REVISED ULP refresh event. Federation entity fetchers read the listing document; item lookup derives a listing ID and finds the requested entry in items.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The provider stores its owned document in NuData/Monstor. Single reads request strong consistency, while multi-get does not use that option. Database exceptions are mapped to typed provider errors; the refresh helper logs send failures without a local retry. Its data is ULP-only relative to CLS core NuDoc, even though this provider also uses NuData.

Evidence. basiclistingdata/src/main/resources/schema/basiclistingdata.graphqls, schema/watchcount.graphqls, graphql/mutation/ListingDataMutation.java, graphql/fetcher/ListingDataFetcher.java, service/impl/ListingDataServiceImpl.java, nudata/dao/ListingDataDaoImpl.java, and helper/ULPRefreshEventHelper.java.

docs.title: cmplregulatorysvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. cmplregulatorysvc provides country-of-origin (COO) and related compliance state. It exposes ListingV2.itemCountryOfOrigin.countryOfOrigin and confidenceScore, plus an itemCountryOfOrigin query that accepts listing/product/category/site and seller-cleared COO inputs.

Core logic and lifecycle. The direct query uses COOQueryHandler, which selects cache-first, vendor, seller-cleared, vector-search, or non-production mock paths. Federated listing reads are cache-only through COOEntityHandler. COOVendorService calls VMP when needed; COOVectorService embeds text, searches a NuDoc vector index, and calculates confidence from top similarity and consensus. Clearing COO writes an event and emits ULP ITEM_REVISED.

Storage, errors, and boundary. COO cache entries are stored in the CountryOfOrigin NuDoc keyspace with soft/hard deletion and a three-day expiry. Vendor rate-limit and authorization failures are explicitly handled, and the Zonos event producer retries once. This is provider-owned enrichment, not CLS core listing NuDoc; the source does not establish external VMP or vector-index behavior.

Evidence. cmplregulatorysvc/src/main/resources/schema/countryOfOrigin.graphqls, schema/listing.graphqls, graphql/countryoforigin/CountryOfOriginDataFetcher.java, COOQueryHandler.java, COOEntityHandler.java, service/COOVendorService.java, service/COOVectorService.java, service/COOCacheService.java, and util/NuDocHelper.java.

docs.title: connectedproductsulp
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. connectedproductsulp exposes Item.connectedProduct, which contains provider identity, warranty dates, and digital-authenticity status/image information. The field requires the parent item's listing ID.

Core logic and lifecycle. The entity fetcher validates item and listing identifiers and batches them through ConnectedProductItemLoader. ItemService reads connectedProduct.* from its NuDocument representation, maps it to ConnectedProductModel, and uses MapStruct to build the ULP response. REST POST, GET, and DELETE /v1/listing/{listingId}/item/{itemId} operations update, retrieve, or remove provider-owned modules. Modified updates and deletes synchronously send ITEM_REVISED through the ULP event producer.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The repository supports partial module updates and no-op detection before it persists the full provider document. It normalizes provider failures into typed GraphQL errors. This is provider-owned NuDocument data, not a CLS core docset. Its checked-in build-time GraphQL generation and runtime mapping explain that the source can expose the field even though the unilistingsvc generated mapping has no local CONNECTEDPRODUCTSULP entry; deployed availability still requires schema/configuration confirmation.

Evidence. connectedproductsulp/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, graphql/ConnectedProductItemFetcher.kt, graphql/ConnectedProductItemLoader.kt, service/ItemService.kt, database/ItemRepository.kt, database/utils/ConnectedProductModelMapper.kt, and ulp/cache/ULPCacheRefreshEventGenerator.kt.

docs.title: dealsgraph
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. dealsgraph contributes dealDetails to ListingV2, SingleSkuListing, and VariationListing. The output includes daily-deal status, permanence, quantity restrictions and quantity, plus deal start/end timestamps. It also provides a direct dealDetailsByListingId query with a 100-ID limit.

Core logic and lifecycle. Entity and direct-query resolvers load through DealFlagsDataLoader. When NuDocIntegrationEnabled is true, the loader reads __ROOT__ documents in the DealsULP Monstor/NuDocument keyspace and maps stored values, including epoch milliseconds, to GraphQL. When disabled, it uses FakeDealFetcher.

Storage, errors, and boundary. A missing document becomes isDailyDeal=false; other Monstor errors become retryable provider errors with listing and service context. The provider refreshes configuration from dealsgraphcfg; the inspected read path has no TTL, event publisher, or provider-local cache. Deal state is separate from CLS core listing NuDoc, although it is keyed by the core listing ID.

Evidence. dealsgraph/src/main/resources/schema/listingDailyDealDetails.graphqls, resource/DealsResource.java, dataloader/DealFlagsDataLoader.java, fetcher/NuDocFetcher.java, MonstorConfig.java, and exception/ProviderExceptionHandler.java.

docs.title: defaultulpprovider
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. defaultulpprovider is a provider scaffold and ULP directive/schema example, rather than a listing-data backend. It exposes the gateway-excluded defaultUlpProvider query and an illustrative DefaultULPProviderOutput with id, description, and test/example fields. otherGroupField demonstrates @fieldGroup; the repository also defines a shared Photo type.

Core logic and lifecycle. Its sole data fetcher returns a hard-coded URL. There is no listing entity resolver, data service, persistence adapter, cache, or event-generation implementation in the inspected path. A test verifies normal GraphQL subselection validation only.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The schema defines general directives such as principal authorization, fallback, and event-generation controls, but this repository does not implement those behaviors for a listing field. It has no NuDoc relationship. The scaffold nature and lack of a ListingV2 field explain why it cannot establish a generated production selection, without proving anything about deployment configuration.

Evidence. defaultulpprovider/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, src/main/java/com/ebay/app/DefaultULPProviderDataFetcher.java, and src/main/java/com/ebay/app/ResourceConfig.java.

docs.title: ebaypluseligibilitysvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. ebaypluseligibilitysvc adds FulfillmentTerms.shippingProgramEligibility.ebayPlus, an internal eligibility flag excluded from publicapi.

Core logic and lifecycle. The federation fetcher validates listingId, then a DGS loader batches FulfillmentTerms keys. For each listing it reads a precomputed NuKVListingEntity and maps isEligible() to ebayPlus; this layer does not calculate eligibility. A separate EligibilityListingProcessor can read the same entity for configured public-namespace program properties.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The provider reads the ebaypluslistingeligibilitynukvhost keyspace, warming up and cleaning up NuKV client state at application start/stop. Missing IDs and NuKV failures become ListingLogisticsDataFetcherException and emit monitoring counters. No TTL, invalidation, or event publisher was found in the GraphQL path. This is shipping-program enrichment, not a CLS NuDoc mapping.

Evidence. ebaypluseligibilitysvc/ebaypluseligibility-lib/src/main/resources/schema/ebaypluseligibility.graphqls, EbayPlusDataFetcher.java, EbayPlusDataLoader.java, NuKVListingEntityService.java, NuKVInitializer.java, and EligibilityListingProcessor.java.

docs.title: ItemVisibility (itmvzblit)
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. Item Visibility (IVF) provides cross-site listing visibility. ListingV2 exposes visibilitySummary with packed visibility, explicitly suppressed sites, and default-visible sites, as well as visibility.hasNativeBlock. The same extension applies to single-SKU and variation listings.

Core logic and lifecycle. Federation fetchers construct listing stubs and batch-load the two outputs using request-scoped user/site context. BatchAsyncVisibilityDataReader reads NuData and SaleBo, checks discrepancies, and maps the result to GraphQL DTOs. This establishes a consumer view of a visibility calculation, not a binary checkout decision.

Storage, errors, and boundary. IVF dual-writes Caty and NuData while Caty remains its source of truth. It uses eventual NuData read consistency, retries storage operations, handles not-found as empty, and can recover an optimistic-lock conflict when a reread matches. A visibility change, or a missing incoming ULP summary, can publish an ITEM_REVISED cache refresh. The source proves ULP core-data enrichment but does not identify a CLS NuDoc docset.

Evidence. ItemVisibility/ItemVisibilityService/src/main/resources/api-graphql/schema.graphql, graphql/DataFetchers.java, BatchVisibilityLoader.java, BatchAsyncVisibilityDataReader.java, IVFDataUpdateProcessor.java, UlpCacheRefreshEventGenerator.java, and NuDataStorageGateway.java.

docs.title: LC-ListingProvider (lclistingprovider)
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. The Live Commerce provider adds ListingV2.ebayLive. Its output includes live event IDs, a primary-event snapshot, listing intent, and purchasable, visible, and buyspotEligible flags for single-SKU and variation listings.

Core logic and lifecycle. Entity fetchers validate listingId, batch via LiveListingDataLoader, and read EbayLive JSON from NuKV using a configured key prefix. EbayLiveMapper makes the first live event the primary event, converts epoch milliseconds to UTC, and applies an orphan-listing compatibility rule to purchasable.

Storage, errors, and boundary. NuKV reads retry; not-found returns no provider data, while other response codes become retryable failures and typed GraphQL provider errors. primaryEvent is documented as eventually consistent cache data suited to high-throughput buyer-facing reads. The provider supports only single-SKU and variation listing types, and it has no CLS/NuDoc reference in the inspected source.

Evidence. LC-ListingProvider/schema/ebayLive_provider.graphqls, ListingDataFetcher.java, ListingDataLoader.java, NuKvClient.java, EbayLiveMapper.java, and ProviderExceptionHandler.java.

docs.title: locnmappingsvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. locnmappingsvc associates a listing or SKU with warehouse locations. It adds Item.inventoryLocations.warehouseLocations, where each location has a merchantLocationKey; the field requires SKU, listing ID, and seller ID context.

Core logic and lifecycle. The entity fetcher validates the item/listing/ seller context and batches items through LocationMappingDataLoader. LocationMappingService constructs a seller + listing + normalized-SKU key, reads ListingLocations from NuData, removes deleted documents, and maps each stored location to the GraphQL output. Batch reads are chunked at 100 keys on a dedicated executor.

Storage, errors, and boundary. REST writes and deletes upsert/delete NuData with up to five retries, publish an item-location BES event, and optionally publish ITEM_REVISED ULP cache refreshes. If a write fails, it rolls back the listing-extension flag; cache-refresh failures are fire-and-forget. This is provider-owned inventory-topology data keyed by ULP core identifiers; no CLS docset is identified.

Evidence. locnmappingsvc/src/main/resources/schema/locationMapping.graphqls, LocationMappingDataFetcher.java, LocationMappingDataLoader.java, LocationMappingServiceImpl.java, LocationMappingController.java, NuDataUtils.java, and UlpCacheRefreshPublisher.java.

docs.title: Marketplace Logistic Service (mpls)
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. MPLS adds FulfillmentTerms.shippingProgramEligibility.globalShippingProgram. The output contains Global Shipping Program eligibility, estimated weight/dimension sources, estimator version/mode, tariff information, domestic-leg cost/service, partner restrictions, and partner-hub postal code.

Core logic and lifecycle. The federation fetcher builds FulfillmentTerms from the listing entity; MplsDataLoader batches keys and uses DBFacade to strongly read ItemData from the GlobalShippingProgram Monstor keyspace. It normalizes the response for GraphQL, including a default GBP currency, two-decimal domestic-leg cost, and pipe-separated restricted country codes.

Storage, errors, and boundary. Missing store data returns a ShippingProgramEligibility object with a null GSP payload. Exceptions are logged and surfaced through the GraphQL exception handler. The inspected GraphQL path has no provider-local cache, TTL, or event publisher. It reads NuData keyed by core listing ID but does not identify a CLS NuDoc document.

Evidence. MarketplaceLogisticService/src/main/resources/schema/mpls.graphqls, graphql/MplsDataFetcher.java, graphql/MplsDataLoader.java, client/db/DBFacade.java, client/db/impl/DefaultDBFacade.java, client/db/impl/DefaultDbClient.java, and graphql/GraphqlExceptionHandler.java.

docs.title: purchaseviewgraphsvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. Purchase View adds ListingV2.listingPurchaseView to single-SKU and variation listings. It returns last-purchase time, a deprecated unique-buyer count, and last purchased unit cost; it requires the seller's legacy user ID and is excluded from publicapi.

Core logic and lifecycle. SaleSummaryDetailsDataFetcher creates a request context from the selected GraphQL subfields and delegates to SaleSummaryDetailsApplicationHandler. The handler executes only the needed COMS/Cosmos tasks: one counts unique counterparties over the configured lookback and another pages orders to find the latest qualifying purchase or a commitment-date fallback. The default lookback is 90 days, batch size is five, and the local retry limit is zero.

Storage, errors, and boundary. This is a request-time aggregation rather than a provider cache. COMS timeouts/failures become sentinel responses, and retryable cases become typed GraphQL provider errors. No CLS/NuDoc implementation is referenced in the provider source; QA test synchronization with other stores is not evidence of a production data path.

Evidence. purchaseviewgraphsvc/PurchaseViewGraphLib/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, PurchaseViewGraphService/.../SaleSummaryDetailsDataFetcher.java, SaleSummaryDetailsApplicationHandler.java, FetchUniqueBuyerCountTask.java, AggregateSaleSummaryDateTask.java, ComsContractErrorUtil.java, and PurchaseViewExceptionHandler.java.

docs.title: sapsvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. sapsvc extends Item with autoTagProduct and dfAnnotatedAspects, both excluded from publicapi. The provider turns search/classifier output into an auto-tagged product reference and a deduped set of dynamically annotated name/value aspects.

Core logic and lifecycle. SapItemDataFetcher validates and normalizes the item ID, then batches through SapItemDataLoader. SapMonstorClient calls /v1/monstorGetBulk, reads the ClassifierResult payload, obtains AutotagProdRefId from the adoption annotator, and reads configured dynamic-aspect names from the df namespace across annotators. The aspect configuration is refreshable through sapeventprocessorcfg.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The inspected provider uses a DGS batch loader but has no explicit TTL, cache invalidation, or event publisher. Invalid item IDs produce typed bad-request errors; client/parse failures are logged and return null or an empty map. It reads SAP/Monstor classifier results and contains no CLS/NuDoc lineage.

Evidence. sapsvc/src/main/resources/schema/sapitemdata.graphqls, graphql/datafetcher/SapItemDataFetcher.java, graphql/dataloader/SapItemDataLoader.java, client/SapMonstorClient.java, config/GlobalDependentLibConfig.java, and util/RequestValidatorUtil.java.

docs.title: sellerportalsvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. sellerportalsvc supplies Item.ebayInventoryStorageMetadata, derived from item-group authentication, consignment, and hub-fulfillment state. Its federated item resolver requires item ID, listing ID, and SKU.

Core logic and lifecycle. SellerListingDataFetcher batches listing/SKU pairs through ItemGroupDataLoader and ItemGroupDAO. The provider's REST listing workflows validate seller listing state, optionally enrich from catalog, create or synchronize inventory/offers, and map item-group data to listing responses. Its DAO has batch reads and atomic item-group/item updates.

Storage, errors, and boundary. Creation and synchronization update provider-owned state; creation rolls back offers, variation groups, and inventory items if it fails. ULP cache refresh can be synchronous or asynchronous with three attempts, while cache/IMS failures are logged and do not fail a completed creation. The checkout contains no explicit CLS or NuDoc reference, so its exact physical store and core-field lineage remain unverified.

Evidence. sellerportalsvc/src/main/java/com/ebay/sellerportal/app/graphql/SellerListingDataFetcher.java, ItemGroupDataLoader.java, dal/dao/ItemGroupDAO.java, resources/ListingResource.java, services/ListingService.java, and producer/CacheRefreshEventGenerator.java.

docs.title: sellerriskentitysvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. sellerriskentitysvc exposes the internal-only listingSearchabilityInfo on ListingV2, SingleSkuListing, and VariationListing. The risk-hold form supplies searchability start and modification times, a non-searchable reason, original start time, hold-log ID, allowance-window timings, used hours, and total hold hours.

Core logic and lifecycle. Federation entity fetchers validate listingId and invoke ListingSearchabilityRiskHoldDataLoader. The loader reads DelayedItem through DelayedItemEntityService and maps its index, modified, original-index, log, and delay-period fields into the GraphQL projection.

Storage, errors, and boundary. REST update paths whitelist the DELAYED_ITEM_KEYSPACE API, upsert NuDoc state through Monstor, and emit ITEM_REVISED for ULP refresh; deserialization and upsert errors are logged and surfaced. A null epoch is mapped to the loader's current time, so it must not be read as a source timestamp. This is provider-owned NuDocument risk state, not CLS core NuDoc.

Evidence. sellerriskentitysvc/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, ListingSearchabilityRiskHoldDataFetcher.java, ListingSearchabilityRiskHoldDataLoader.java, DelayedItemResource.java, DelayedItemEntityServiceImpl.java, and DelayedItemConstants.java.

docs.title: seocorelabsvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. seocorelabsvc adds photosWithAltText to ListingV2, SingleSkuListing, VariationListing, and Item. Each output contains the source Photo plus optional imageAltText, and is excluded from publicapi.

Core logic and lifecycle. Federation entity hydration creates listing/item stubs; PhotoAltTextFetcher batches listing IDs and maps each input photo's image GUID to cached alt text. PhotoAltTextLoader bulk-reads the NuKV SEO cache. The mapper retains the first alt-text value for a GUID collision and returns the original photos without alt text when mapping/data load fails.

Storage, errors, and boundary. A protected REST refresh endpoint is called after upstream alt text is written to NuKV. It emits ITEM_REVISED when the refresh feature and client allowlist permit it. The provider source has no explicit retry or persistence implementation beyond NuKV reads, and it does not establish a CLS/NuDoc source for the photo itself.

Evidence. seocorelabsvc/src/main/resources/schema/photo-alt-text-schema.graphqls, graphql/EntityFetcher.java, graphql/PhotoAltTextFetcher.java, graphql/PhotoAltTextLoader.java, cache/NuKVSeoCoreLabCacheImpl.java, cache/PhotoAltTextMappingMapper.java, and cache/CacheRefreshService.java.

docs.title: slrinvsvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. slrinvsvc supplies the internal ListingV2.hideFromSearch and availableForShipToHome flags for single-SKU and variation listings. The fields require seller context and are excluded from publicapi.

Core logic and lifecycle. The entity fetcher validates listingId and seller.legacyUserId; its DGS loader batches requests on a dedicated executor. ListingFlagsService groups requests by seller, reads SKUStatusDAO, decodes stored flags, merges duplicate rows using OR for ship-to-home and AND for search hiding, then fills absent listings with null flags.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The GraphQL path is read-through with no provider-local TTL/cache found. Invalid context and DAO errors become typed provider GraphQL errors. Separate inventory write paths can emit asynchronous, feature-flagged, fire-and-forget ITEM_REVISED cache refreshes; send failures are ignored after logging. The source has no CLS/NuDoc references, so only the federation relationship is established.

Evidence. slrinvsvc/src/main/resources/schema/listingflags.graphqls, ListingFlagsDataFetcher.java, ListingFlagsDataLoader.java, ListingFlagsServiceImpl.java, DefaultSKUStatusRepository.java, UlpCacheRefreshPublisher.java, and AppInventoryResource.java.

docs.title: svls
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. SVLS is the broad, read-only seller-view/core-listing provider. It reconstructs listing, item, seller-product, category, price, quantity, terms, fulfillment, lifecycle, variation, tax, regulatory, vehicle, and document data. It is the source-backed read boundary for the large default svls group, rather than a narrow provider enrichment.

Core logic and lifecycle. Listing and federation fetchers batch IDs using a DataLoader with caching disabled, then call ItemAndGroupProcessor and CLSClient.getItemsAndGroupForListing with the FULL field group. CLS responses are converted through item/group adapters and GraphQLConverter, which chooses SingleSkuListing or VariationListing based on whether CLS returns an item group. Separate loaders support archived and versioned reads. SVLS has no listing write path or ULP refresh publisher; its CLS clients have a configured maximum retry count of two.

Storage, errors, and boundary. SVLS reads CLS over authenticated HTTP and does not directly access a NuData/NuDocument DAO. Failed ordinary batch records can be omitted, while bulk reads retain typed GraphQL error data, including listing identity and retryability. The source proves a direct service-level CLS relationship, but it does not identify the individual CLS NuDoc document that supplies each GraphQL field. The lack of a dedicated _svls query branch is expected for this baseline group; the schema's 726 output-field definitions and ULP's 683 mapped paths are related inventories, not directly comparable counts.

Evidence. svls/svlsService/src/main/resources/schema/SvlsGraphQLSchema.graphqls, dgsgraphql/datafetcher/ListingDataFetcher.java, dgsgraphql/dataloader/ListingDataLoader.java, processors/ItemAndGroupProcessor.java, gingerclients/CLSClient.java, dgsgraphql/converter/GraphQLConverter.java, and service/SellerViewListingService.java.

docs.title: itemcompatibilitysvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. itemcompatibilitysvc supplies final motors compatibility data by marketplace, including notional-profile grouping and optional search configuration. listingCompatibilities is the preferred listing-level contract; the legacy Item.compatibilities path remains deprecated so MSKU compatibility does not fan out to every variation.

Core logic and lifecycle. The federation resolver reads the listing ID, marketplace, and primary category. The query service checks marketplace/category allowance, obtains cached or remotely fetched category compatibility, then reads the ItemCompatibility Monstor/NuData record. It filters rows to the listing marketplace, adds a configured search-config ID, and returns no object when no compatible row remains. Fitment refreshes can call Fitment Service, construct or update notional-profile groupings, and persist the result. The current item-entity ULP path intentionally returns an empty compatibility item; it does not populate compatibilityCatalogProduct.

Storage, errors, and boundary. Provider compatibility data, audit records, and listing history are separate from CLS core NuDoc. Category data uses an in-memory cache refreshed at the configured 24-hour interval; the compatibility documents have no local TTL. Successful changed fitment data can publish ITEM.REVISED or backfill events, with configurable sync/async send behavior and a two-second refresh timeout. The refresh consumer retries failed messages. Fitment timeout, throttle, and 5xx responses are retryable; an invalid compatibility type is retried only by mutation/refresh paths, not normal ULP reads.

Evidence. itemcompatibilitysvc/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, resolver/ItemCompatibilityResolver.kt, service/ItemCompatibilityQueryService.kt, service/CategoryServiceUtil.kt, service/ItemCompatibilityFromFitSvcUtil.kt, repository/ItemCompatibilityRepositoryImpl.kt, nudata/ItemCompatibilityDAO.kt, util/ULPCacheRefreshEventGenerator.kt, and task/RefreshItemConsumerTask.kt.

docs.title: vehentsvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. vehentsvc enriches vehicle listings with vehicle history, report-provider and purchase data, vehicle identifiers, and seller document-verification status. Report content can represent free, paid, or unavailable vehicle history, so a returned object does not guarantee every history subfield is available.

Core logic and lifecycle. The listing field fetcher batches selected vehicle history/identifier fields by listing ID and marketplace. It calls FGQL listingsV2ByIds to obtain seller ID, VIN, and year/make/model context, then reads the vehicle-history data by VIN, seller, site, and attribute ID. It prefers the MotorsVehicleHistoryReport NuDocument path when enabled and falls back to Oracle CATY for missing, unparsable, or NO_VHR data. The independently selected vehicleVerification field reads a VehicleVerificationDetails NuDocument child record by listing ID.

Storage, errors, and boundary. Vehicle-history writes can dual-write NuDocument and CATY, while vehicle verification writes a NuDocument record with a 90-day TTL. Both changed-write paths publish ULP refresh events. UlpCacheRefreshPublisher retries ULPException three times with a 500 ms delay; the core-context FGQL client retries only transport failures three times before returning no result. This is provider-owned vehicle data keyed from ULP core context, not a CLS document family. The source establishes the CATY fallback but not its external service semantics.

Evidence. vehentsvcService/src/main/resources/schema/VehicleHistoryReport.graphqls, graphql/VehicleHistoryReportDataFetcher.java, graphql/VehicleListingDetailsDataLoader.java, graphql/service/VehicleListingDetailsService.java, vehentsvcLib/.../helper/VehicleHistorySummaryHelper.java, fgql/FGQLServiceInvoker.java, dal/ebayvehicleattrinfo/MotorsVehicleHistoryReportNuDataServiceDao.java, dal/vehicleverification/VehicleVerificationNuDataDao.java, and events/UlpCacheRefreshPublisher.java.

docs.title: pickupeligibility
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. pickupeligibility computes whether a listing is eligible for a Pick Up/Drop Off (PUDO) program. It consumes seller offer status and a substantial federated listing context, but owns only the eligibleForPudo result.

Core logic and lifecycle. The entity fetcher converts ULP listing data to the legacy sale representation, reads seller pickup offer intent/eligibility through ULOS, builds listing details, and applies the configured pickup rules. Category, format, location, handling time, price, returns, shipping service, package dimensions, and weight can participate in the rules. The result is true if any PUDO program is eligible; configured filtered sites return false.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The GraphQL path is a request-time evaluation and does not write the Sale PUDO bit. Other event-driven listing flows can update that legacy Sale.Flags12 bit and emit an asynchronous ULP ITEM_REVISED event when eligibility changes. ULOS uses Oracle records with an optional asynchronous NuDoc comparison, but this does not establish CLS NuDoc lineage. No provider-local TTL is present. Despite the schema documenting null for service failure, the loader maps many conversion and calculation failures to false; downstream consumers must not equate false with a definitive business ineligibility without error context.

Evidence. PickupEligibilityService/upcsService/.../schema/pickupeligibility.graphqls, graphql/datafetcher/EligibleForPudoDataFetcher.java, EligibleForPudoDataLoader.java, UPCSProcessor.java, PickUpServiceListingOfferPlugin.java, PickupListingServiceClient.java, PickUpRuleEngineImp.java, CacheRefreshEventGenerator.java, and ULOSDalUtilProxy.java.

docs.title: egdsellermgmt
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. egdsellermgmt adds eBay Guaranteed Delivery policy and regional eligibility type to the federated ShippingProgramEligibility entity. A present object has a policy; a missing eligibility type represents an ineligible regional result.

Core logic and lifecycle. The entity resolver validates the listing ID, then its DGS loader reads the provider's EbayGuaranteedDelivery document through a strong-consistency Monstor/NuData GET. The result is mapped to policy and US/Australia eligibility type. Separate listing-logistics operations create, merge, and delete these provider records; successful writes synchronously send an ITEM_REVISED ULP refresh.

Storage, errors, and boundary. A missing document produces a null ebayGuaranteedDelivery object, while async loader failures also collapse to null. Write requests can enable Monstor retry and use a configured timeout; the source does not prove the active retry setting or count. Refresh-send failures are logged rather than rethrown, and no GraphQL-path cache or TTL is defined. This is provider-owned Monstor/NuData enrichment keyed by core listing ID, not a named CLS core NuDoc family.

Evidence. GuaranteedDeliverySellerManagement/egdsellermgmtService/.../schema/egd.graphqls, graphql/datafetcher/EbayGuaranteedDeliveryResolver.java, EbayGuaranteedDeliveryDataLoader.java, GuaranteedDeliveryLib/.../dao/EbayGuaranteedDeliveryMonstorDAO.java, listinglogistics/ListingLogisticsOperations.java, and util/ULPCacheRefresher.java.

docs.title: mdmlusvcio
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. mdmlusvcio supplies markdown-promotion start and end times on an item. Its additional seller-promotion reports and mutations support markdown management but are outside ULP's current-listing field selection.

Core logic and lifecycle. The item entity fetcher validates item and listing identity, batches listing IDs, and reads an ItemSellerDiscount record from NuKV. For a selected MSKU backfill, missing NuKV dates cause a SaleBo lookup and SME markdown-item-detail lookup; recovered promotion ID and dates are written back to NuKV. SSKU items with no usable NuKV data return null. Other report/summary paths read SME markdown database data.

Storage, errors, and boundary. Markdown detail/log/history data is provider-owned SME database state, while duration data is primarily NuKV; NuKV is not NuDoc. The ULP listing field has no local TTL. Per-item lookup or backfill failures become null. Markdown operations can publish ITEM_REVISED, but publication is feature-gated and disabled by the checked-in default. Listing Processing Service calls retry failed-system responses up to the configured limit. The SaleBo fallback is a legacy recovery path, not proof of CLS NuDoc ownership.

Evidence. mdmlusvcioLib/src/main/resources/schema/markdown.graphqls, graphql/datafetcher/PromoSaleDateDataFetcher.java, MarkdownDiscountOnItemDataLoader.java, accessor/db/NukvDataAccessor.java, ListingDBAccessor.java, SMEMarkdownDBAccessor.java, accessor/service/ListingProcessServiceAccessor.java, and mdmlusvcioApi/.../CacheRefreshEventGenerator.java.

docs.title: dalasproxysourcesvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. dalasproxysourcesvc starts the DALAS plugin evaluation stage. It owns the parent dalasEvaluation and source-phase container/base-GUID data. The nested UUID is passed through; the concrete listing UUID prerequisite is external and originates from dalasuuidprovidersvc.

Core logic and lifecycle. The SingleSkuListing and VariationListing entity resolvers batch a converted ULP listing and its UUID to DALAS /v3/plugin-orchestrations/{listingId}. The provider encodes the returned entity container and emits a DalasSourceEvaluation. Listings outside the configured traffic ramp return an empty source without the DALAS request. DataLoader caching is disabled, no local DAO/cache or TTL exists, and the result is request-time DALAS behavior. The implementation does not populate the schema's optional dalasEntityContainerPreExisting field on its successful source path.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The repository proves an external DALAS POST, not DALAS persistence, event delivery, or source freshness. HTTP 5xx and network failures are retryable; 4xx and validation failures are not. Per-listing batch failures retain status/error information and are mapped to typed GraphQL errors. It consumes ULP core listing context but has no CLS client or NuDoc DAO.

Evidence. dalasproxysourcesvc/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, resolver/DalasSourceEvaluationEntityResolver.java, loader/PluginOrchestrationsBatchLoader.java, service/PluginOrchestrationsService.java, util/DalasResponseBuilder.java, and error/DalasGraphQLExceptionHandler.java.

docs.title: dalasproxysinksvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. dalasproxysinksvc performs the second DALAS stage for a source evaluation. It owns the inaccessible sink container and the storage manifest; UUID and source-stage values are external prerequisites.

Core logic and lifecycle. The DalasEvaluation entity resolver batches the source container, base GUID, and UUID to DALAS /v3/immutable-append/{listingId}. It encodes the response as a storage manifest. An empty source short-circuits to empty sink/manifest values. DataLoader caching is disabled and no provider-local persistence, TTL, or domain-event path is implemented. The checked-in response builder assigns the incoming source container to dalasEntityContainerSink, despite the schema describing the field as the final container.

Storage, errors, and boundary. This is a request-time DALAS pipeline stage, not a CLS/NuDoc owner. It classifies HTTP 5xx and network failures as retryable and 4xx or malformed input as non-retryable, then surfaces typed GraphQL errors with per-listing status. The generated ULP branches for both DALAS groups intentionally include the composed nested { dalasStorageManifest listingId } selection: aliases control generated query inclusion, not field ownership. dalasproxysourcesvc owns the listing-level parent, dalasproxysinksvc owns the manifest, listingId is the federation key, and dalasuuidprovidersvc owns the UUID.

Evidence. dalasproxysinksvc/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, resolver/DalasEvaluationEntityResolver.java, loader/ImmutableAppendBatchLoader.java, service/ImmutableAppendService.java, util/DalasResponseBuilder.java, and error/DalasGraphQLExceptionHandler.java.

docs.title: dalasuuidprovidersvc
docs.text:
Purpose and fields. dalasuuidprovidersvc owns and generates the internal dalasUuid listing field used by the DALAS source and sink stages. It is excluded from publicapi.

Core logic and lifecycle. The listing entity fetchers batch listing IDs through a non-caching DataLoader and submit one task per listing to EvaluationUuidService, which calls GuidGenerator.nextGuid(). A missing DataLoader falls back to direct UUID generation. The value is built into the single-SKU or variation entity response; it is not read from a database or external service.

Storage, errors, and boundary. The service has no writes, event flow, provider-local cache, TTL, persistence, or retryable downstream request. It generates at resolution time, so the source does not establish UUID stability across separate ULP requests. Validation failures are non-retryable bad-input errors; generic runtime errors become structured internal errors. It uses only listing ID and has no CLS/NuDoc data lineage.

Evidence. dalasuuidprovidersvc/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls, README.md, resolver/DalasUuidEvaluationEntityResolver.java, loader/EvaluationUuidBatchLoader.java, service/EvaluationUuidService.java, util/DalasUuidProviderSvcResponseBuilder.java, and error/DalasGraphQLExceptionHandler.java.

docs.title: Provider-to-NuDoc relationship summary
docs.text:
Provider repositories show that "post-listing" does not imply a single storage technology. The matrix below narrows the data-gap statement to what the inspected source proves.

Provider group Provider-local source Relationship to CLS core NuDoc BASICLISTINGDATA Provider-owned NuData/Monstor document. Separate application attributes layered on listing/item keys. CMPLREGULATORYSVC CountryOfOrigin NuDoc, vendor calls, and vector search. Separate compliance enrichment. CONNECTEDPRODUCTSULP Provider-owned NuDocument under connectedProduct.*. Separate connected-product modules keyed by item/listing. DEALSGRAPH DealsULP NuDoc __ROOT__, or a configured fake fetcher. Separate deal state keyed by listing ID. DEFAULTULPPROVIDER Static example resolver only. No core or provider data relationship is established. EBAYPLUSELIGIBILITY Precomputed NuKV eligibility entity. Separate shipping-program result. ITMVZBLIT NuData plus SaleBo; Caty remains source of truth during dual-write. ULP-enriched visibility, without a CLS docset identified. LCLISTINGPROVIDER NuKV EbayLive JSON cache. Separate eventually consistent live-commerce state. LOCNMAPPINGSVC NuData ListingLocations documents. Separate inventory-topology data keyed by listing/SKU/seller. MPLS GlobalShippingProgram Monstor/NuData records. Separate shipping-program result keyed by listing ID. PURCHASEVIEWGRAPHSVC Request-time COMS/Cosmos aggregation. Separate purchase-view computation; no CLS/NuDoc path shown. SAPSVC SAP classifier results read through Monstor. Separate derived product/aspect enrichment. SELLERPORTALSVC Provider item-group/item DAO and external inventory/catalog clients. Core-field or physical-store lineage is not established. SELLERRISKENTITYSVC DelayedItem NuDocument in DELAYED_ITEM_KEYSPACE. Separate risk/searchability state. SEOCORELABSVC NuKV SEO cache. Separate derived image-alt-text lookup. SLRINVSVC Seller-inventory SKUStatusDAO read-through. Separate inventory flags; no CLS/NuDoc path shown. SVLS Request-time CLS read through the SVLS CLS client. Direct CLS core-listing reconstruction; no field-level NuDoc document lineage is established by SVLS. ITEMCOMPATIBILITYSVC Provider-owned ItemCompatibility Monstor/NuData keyspace. Separate compatibility enrichment keyed by listing ID and core marketplace/category context. VEHENTSVC Provider MotorsVehicleHistoryReport and verification NuDocuments, with a CATY fallback for history data. Separate vehicle-history and verification data, using core listing data to obtain VIN and seller context. PICKUPELIGIBILITY Request-time ULP/Sale conversion and ULOS seller intent/eligibility data; optional ULOS NuDoc comparison. Computed pickup-program result, not CLS core-listing NuDoc state. EGDSELLERMGMT Provider-owned EbayGuaranteedDelivery Monstor/NuData document. Separate shipping-program enrichment keyed by listing ID. MDMLUSVCIO NuKV item discounts, SME markdown database data, and optional SaleBo backfill. Separate promotion state; NuKV and SaleBo fallback do not establish CLS NuDoc ownership. DALASPROXYSOURCESVC Request-time external DALAS plugin-orchestration response. Pipeline enrichment consuming a federated core-listing representation; no provider NuDoc or CLS client. DALASPROXYSINKSVC Request-time external DALAS immutable-append response. Pipeline enrichment consuming DALAS source/UUID state; no provider NuDoc or CLS client. DALASUUIDPROVIDERSVC Locally generated UUID at federation-resolution time. Internal DALAS pipeline identity; no persisted source or CLS/NuDoc lineage.

docs.title: Provider-data consumer rules
docs.text: Situation Required interpretation A requested provider field is absent or null It can reflect authorization, disabled configuration, environment exclusion, a cache miss, asynchronous calculation, an unavailable provider, or a genuine empty value. Inspect GraphQL errors and the field contract. A core listing is revised Do not assume all provider groups immediately refresh. Provider data can have an independent event and cache lifecycle. A visibility, risk, availability, or shipping-program field is returned Use it only for its documented domain use. It is not a universal buyer-eligibility or checkout decision. A provider group appears in schema Verify the active gateway, provider enablement, generated query template, and source owner before depending on it. A consumer needs provider freshness Confirm the owning provider's freshness and event contract. The local repositories establish grouping and refresh mechanics, not an end-to-end latency or delivery SLO.

docs.title: The comparison in one view
docs.text:
ULP is a consumer-facing, federated current-listing surface. NuDoc is a producer-side CLS persistence model. A data gap is therefore often a difference in purpose rather than a missing field.

Difference class What exists Gap or migration implication Shared core-state projection CLS persists core listing state across NuDoc document families; ULP exposes listing and item concepts through GraphQL. Assemble the right NuDoc families when using raw data, or use ULP when the GraphQL current-state contract fits. Do not assume one ULP field has one NuDoc storage field. NuDoc-only producer operations Drafts, history, locks, UUID maps, document keys, compression, archival paths, and targeted write/read boundaries exist in CLS. Use CLS/NuDoc-oriented interfaces for operational workflows. These states are not established as normal ULP current-listing fields. ULP-only enrichment Provider groups add derived, domain-owned, and extended data to the ULP response. Core NuDoc alone cannot reproduce these fields. Locate the mapped provider and confirm its source/freshness contract. Contract and access GraphQL authorization, gateway tags, group selection, configuration, cache state, and response errors affect ULP availability. A stored NuDoc value does not imply an API caller can read an equivalent ULP field. Representation and freshness NuDoc has documents, document IDs, compressed payloads, nested models, and current/history splits; ULP has graph projections and provider caches. Normalize shape deliberately and handle eventual consistency or delayed enrichment.

docs.title: NuDoc coverage matrix
docs.text:
CLS declares 22 logical document families across current, draft, index, and revision-history data. The following matrix makes the resulting ULP gaps explicit.

NuDoc family ULP equivalent established by source Coverage Reason or constraint ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__ ListingV2/Item identity, seller-product, listing-term, and lifecycle families Family correspondence ULP may transform, restrict, or assemble fields; exact leaf lineage varies. ItemKeyspace.ItemQtyPrice Item price, quantity, sold quantity, and commercial fields Directly mapped at document purpose Monetary nesting and consumer representation can differ. ItemKeyspace.ItemDescription Seller-product/listing description fields Directly mapped at document purpose ULP does not expose NuDoc compression as a consumer contract. ItemKeyspace.ItemCompatibility Listing/item compatibility fields Family correspondence Optional fields can be excluded from default cache reads until selected. ItemKeyspace.BusinessPolicies Listing/item terms and policy objects Family correspondence Field authorization and group/shared ownership can differ. ItemKeyspace.ItemDetails Specialized listing/item details when exposed Family correspondence No source proof of complete leaf coverage. ItemKeyspace.ItemLock No normal ULP field established NuDoc-only Reservation and lock lifecycle is an operational model. ItemKeyspace.UuidMap No normal ULP field established NuDoc-only Seller/UUID lookup is an operational index. ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__ MSKU listing/item/variation relationship and shared seller-product state Family correspondence Group and variation remain separate business grains. ItemGroupKeyspace.GroupDescription Shared MSKU description Directly mapped at document purpose Must not be treated as a duplicated variation description. ItemGroupKeyspace.GroupBusinessPolicies Shared MSKU term/policy state Family correspondence Exact ULP field and access depend on the selected contract. ListingDraft.__ROOT__ A live ListingV2 can expose a related draftId, but no full draft read is established NuDoc-only for draft state A draft is working state, not published current listing data. ListingDraft.ItemDraft No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Draft SSKU/variation content precedes or differs from live item state. ListingDraft.ItemDraftCompatibility No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Draft compatibility is not proof of live compatibility. ListingDraft.ItemGroupDraft No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Draft group structure is not a published MSKU group. ListingDraft.ItemGroupDraftCompatibility No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Draft-only specialized payload. ListingDraft.ItemGroupDraftDesc No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Draft-only shared description. UserListingDraft.UserItemDraftMap No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only User-scoped active-draft discovery index. ListingRevisionKeyspace.__ROOT__ No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Revision retention state differs from current state. ListingRevisionKeyspace.ListingRevision No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Historical summary must not be merged into latest fields without business rules. ListingRevisionKeyspace.ListingRevisionDetail No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Historical non-variation property detail. ListingRevisionKeyspace.VariationRevisionDetail No normal ULP current-listing equivalent established NuDoc-only Historical variation property detail.

docs.title: ULP enrichment absent from CLS core NuDoc evidence
docs.text:
The groups below are ULP-only relative to the CLS core NuDoc source. This does not imply the data is absent from eBay systems; it means the supplied CLS repository does not establish it as core listing document state.

ULP enrichment family Examples Data-gap conclusion Search and visibility Visible/suppressed sites, searchability times/reasons, risk holds, search hiding. Requires the visibility/risk provider path; a live NuDoc listing does not establish search visibility. Deals and engagement Daily-deal data, watch counts, purchase-view metrics. Requires deal, basic-listing-data, and purchase-view providers. Inventory topology Warehouse merchant-location keys, consignment, hub fulfillment, pre-authentication. Requires location-mapping and seller-portal providers. Shipping-program enrichment eBay Plus and Global Shipping Program eligibility, restricted countries, tariffs, shipment estimation metadata. Requires eBay Plus and MPLS providers; not a substitute for fulfillment execution. Product and SEO enrichment Search tagging/aspects, image alt text, derived image metadata. Requires SAP and SEO providers; do not assume it was seller-authored core content. Compliance and live-commerce enrichment Country-of-origin confidence and eBay Live event/eligibility state. Requires regulatory and live-commerce providers.

docs.title: Semantic and operational gaps
docs.text:
Even where ULP and NuDoc represent the same business concept, consumers need to account for the following differences.

Topic NuDoc behavior ULP behavior Consumer action Storage shape Separate docsets with service-specific keys and retrieval boundaries. Nested GraphQL types selected by the client. Model a consumer entity intentionally; do not expose raw document keys as business fields. SSKU/MSKU Group data and member variation state are separate. Listing/item graph can present both concepts. Preserve group-versus-variation grain in joins, aggregations, and metrics. Optional large data Description and compatibility can be isolated or compressed. Fields can be selectively requested and may be excluded from default cached reads. Request needed fields explicitly and define null/absence handling. History and drafts Independent families with different identities and lifecycles. Normal listing reads establish current-state access, not a history/draft API. Do not replace current listing values with draft or revision data. Provider state CLS source does not own provider enrichments. Field groups may be asynchronous, conditional, cached, or unavailable. Confirm owner, configuration, freshness, and error behavior for each provider field. Authorization CLS service operations have their own authorization and operational paths. Schema fields can be gateway- or principal-restricted. Validate the caller context and inspect GraphQL errors instead of interpreting absence as data loss. Freshness Core state is written through CLS operational flows. Cached current-state and provider refresh behavior can be eventually consistent. Use an owning transactional service for checkout, buyer eligibility, payment, fulfillment, or settlement decisions.

docs.title: Migration guidance
docs.text:
1. Start from the business question. Use ULP for a buyer-context-independent current listing view plus requested enrichments. Use CLS/NuDoc-oriented interfaces for producer operations, drafts, revision history, locks, and raw lineage.
  2. Request provider fields deliberately. Identify the field group and mapped provider; then verify the caller's gateway/authorization, enabled configuration, and freshness requirements.
  3. Treat a ULP event as a state-change signal. Retrieve needed current fields after an event; do not assume any event carries a complete listing snapshot or has legacy BES1 payload parity.
  4. Keep grain and time explicit. Distinguish listing, sellable item, variation group, draft, current state, and revision history. Avoid joins that multiply shared MSKU values across sellable variations.
  5. Record unknown lineage as unknown. An exact ULP-to-NuDoc field map requires a field path, relevant CLS converter/reconstructor, ULP mapping or response conversion, and any provider evidence. Do not promote a name-based guess to documentation.

docs.title: Tracing a specific field
docs.text:
Use this sequence when a field needs an exact source or gap classification:

  1. Find its federated contract. Locate the field in fgql/ext/superSchema and inspect its @join__field(graph: ...) ownership. UNILISTINGSVC means ULP exposes the field; it does not by itself identify the underlying provider or NuDoc docset.
  2. Inspect the ULP schema. Read the matching type and directives in unilistingsvc/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls or the FGQL ext/unilistingsvc.graphqls snapshot. Record deprecation, gateway exclusion, authorization, and field documentation.
  3. Resolve a ULP provider group. Search FieldToFieldGroupMapping.json for the field path and FieldGroupToSubgraphMapping.json for the service. Then inspect the production ListingV2ById-onDemandFieldGroup.graphql template to confirm the selected field block and @include guard.
  4. Trace core state in CLS. Search the V2 entity, its use in DocumentConverter or ItemGroupDocumentConverter, and the matching reconstruction code such as GetItemDocumentConverter. Record the NuDoc docset and any transformations such as compression.
  5. Classify the result. Mark it directly mapped only when the above evidence proves the path. Otherwise choose family correspondence, ULP-only, NuDoc-only, conditional, or unverified and state what repository/configuration is still required.

docs.title: Evidence references and limits
docs.text:
Evidence area Source artifacts CLS core writes and reads crlstngsvService/.../processor/DocumentConverter.java, ItemGroupDocumentConverter.java, GetItemDocumentConverter.java, CoreItemProcessor.java, CoreItemGroupProcessor.java, and nudata/Docset.java. CLS lifecycle and NuDoc families crlstngsv/doc/repository-business-process-walkthrough.md; NuData write-flow research; Listing NuData Design. ULP schema and provider grouping unilistingsvc/src/main/resources/schema/schema.graphqls; onDemand/FieldGroups.json; FieldToFieldGroupMapping.json; FieldGroupToSubgraphMapping.json; and the production on-demand query template. ULP selection, caching, and refresh FieldOnDemandFieldGroupLookup.java, ListingGraphQLQueryBuilder.java, MonstorFieldMapper.java, FGQLListingDataSource.java, and ULPProviderEventConsumer.java. Federation contract and routing fgql/ext/unilistingsvc.graphqls, fgql/ext/superSchema, src/gateway.ts, src/authenticatedDataSource.ts, and src/plugin/queryPlanHandler.ts. Provider output contracts and local behavior The provider-specific schema, resolver, service, source-client, persistence, and event paths listed in each provider implementation analysis. Oracle migration and event boundary Oracle Caty Item Tables Migration Guide, together with the FGQL schema and gateway source artifacts above.

The original NuDoc schema inputs, deployed supergraph, active provider configuration, physical provider stores, external provider dependencies, event delivery guarantees, and end-to-end freshness guarantees are outside the checked-out sources. The linked provider repositories establish their local implementation behavior, but they do not prove those external or deployment-time conditions. Confirm them with the owning service before making an operational, availability, or field-level lineage commitment.

docs.title: Item - Attribute Value Mapping
docs.text: ← Back to Home

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Mapping LDM Name: item_common_attribute_value_mapping

Description: Many-to-many relationship between Items and Attribute Values using the EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value) pattern for basic item attributes.

Primary Keys: item_id, attr_id, value_id

docs.title: Schema Structure
docs.text:
item_id        BIGINT      FK to Item
attr_id        BIGINT      Attribute identifier
attr_name      VARCHAR     Attribute name (denormalized)
value_id       BIGINT      Value identifier
value_desc     VARCHAR     Attribute value (denormalized)

docs.title: Get All Attributes for an Item
docs.text:
SELECT 
    item_id,
    attr_name,
    value_desc
FROM gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping
WHERE item_id = 123456789;

docs.title: Filter by Specific Attribute
docs.text:
-- Get brand information for items
SELECT 
    item_id,
    attr_name,
    value_desc
FROM gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping
WHERE item_id IN (123456789, 987654321)
  AND attr_name = 'Brand';

docs.title: Join with Item Entity
docs.text:
-- Get items with specific attribute value
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.item_title,
    i.item_price,
    m.attr_name,
    m.value_desc
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_name = 'Brand'
  AND m.value_desc = 'Apple'
LIMIT 100;

docs.title:
-- Get items matching multiple attribute criteria
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.item_title,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Brand' THEN m.value_desc END) AS brand,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Model' THEN m.value_desc END) AS model,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Color' THEN m.value_desc END) AS color
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_common_attribute_value_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_name IN ('Brand', 'Model', 'Color')
GROUP BY i.item_id, i.item_title
HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Brand' THEN m.value_desc END) = 'Apple'
LIMIT 100;
Physical Source
