docs.title: Scope and answer
docs.text:
This is a repository-scoped walkthrough of crlstngsv. In this document, “NuDoc” means the NuData/MonStor document classes and docsets represented by this repository. The repository does not use SQL DDL for these stores; it builds JSON documents and sends MonStor RequestFactory insert, upsert, update, and delete mutations.

There are 22 declared logical docsets in the source:

Keyspace family Domain purpose Logical docsets Count ItemKeyspace Current-state identity and operational data for one listing item or variation __ROOT__, ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDetails, BusinessPolicies, UuidMap, ItemLock 8 ItemGroupKeyspace Shared current-state data for an MSKU item group __ROOT__, GroupDescription, GroupBusinessPolicies 3 ListingDraft Working content and session state before or during listing publication __ROOT__, ItemDraft, ItemGroupDraft, ItemDraftCompatibility, ItemGroupDraftCompatibility, ItemGroupDraftDesc 6 UserListingDraft User-scoped index of active listing drafts UserItemDraftMap 1 ListingRevisionKeyspace Historical listing and variation changes, separate from current state __ROOT__, ListingRevision, ListingRevisionDetail, VariationRevisionDetail 4 Total 22

For ordinary live data writes, the item create/replace family writes six docsets, item-group create/replace writes three, an SSKU draft writes two or three documents and an MSKU draft writes three plus one ItemDraft per variation, or four plus one when group compatibility is present, active user-draft indexing writes one, and a revision insert writes one to three document types. UuidMap and ItemLock are auxiliary item docsets. Archive hold/version fallback writes the root docset in an archive keyspace. Therefore, “22 tables” is the schema declaration count, not the number of documents written by every request.

If a keyspace-qualified sink is counted only when a write is proven in code, there are 24 sink pairs:

  • 8 in live ItemKeyspace;
  • 3 in live ItemGroupKeyspace;
  • 6 in ListingDraft;
  • 1 in UserListingDraft;
  • 4 in ListingRevisionKeyspace;
  • 1 archive pair, ItemKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__;
  • 1 archive pair, ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__.

The archive keyspaces reuse the item and group schema classes, so they add two physical keyspace/docset sinks but no new logical docset class. The count does not claim that all 24 sinks are touched by one business operation.

The five rows above are the logical live keyspaces described by this document. ItemKeyspaceArchive and ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive are archive variants that reuse the root schemas; they are physical write targets, not additional logical keyspace families.

docs.title: Keyspace and docset purpose catalog
docs.text: This catalog explains what each keyspace represents and why each docset exists. The hierarchy role describes the document's relationship to its ancestor; it does not imply that every docset is written by every operation.

docs.title: ItemKeyspace
docs.text:
ItemKeyspace is the current-state family for one individual listing item or one variation of an MSKU listing. The item root is the identity anchor. Compatibility, description, quantity/price, details, and business-policy payloads are separated so they can be read and updated independently. UuidMap and ItemLock are auxiliary operational trees in the same keyspace, not additional parts of the normal six-docset item create/replace payload.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ItemRoot) Broad current-state item document: listing identity, seller/location, lifecycle, category, policy references, flags, identifiers, media references, and other item-level state. Root of the item ancestor tree; persisted primary key PK, normally equal to itemId. ItemCompatibility Fitment and compatibility payload for the item, with expanded or compressed representation. Child of the item ancestor; ItemCompID, normally COMPAT_<itemId>. ItemDescription Seller/item description payload and its revision timestamp, with expanded or compressed representation. Child of the item ancestor; ItemDescID, normally DESC_<itemId>. ItemQtyPrice Commercial and inventory state: available quantity, sold quantity, remnant quantity, and price variants. Child of the item ancestor; ItemQtyPriceID, normally QTY_PRICE_<itemId>. ItemDetails Additional item-level details such as high-precision prices, relaxed rules, source listing, and supporting documents. Child of the item ancestor; itemDetailsID, normally ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId>. BusinessPolicies Item-level return, payment, and shipping policy content and identifiers. Child of the item ancestor; plcsId, normally BIZ_POL_<itemId>. UuidMap (ItemUUIDMapping) Auxiliary seller-and-UUID lookup that resolves listingId and listingAppId for UUID-specific operations. Separate UUID ancestor tree in the same keyspace; composite key is seller ID plus UUID, with UUID_MAP child semantics. ItemLock Inventory reservation lifecycle state for active, committed, cancelled, and extended locks, including the aggregate summary lock. Auxiliary child under the item ancestor; persisted key pk, normally LOCK_<lockId>; summary key is LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$.

docs.title: ItemGroupKeyspace
docs.text:
ItemGroupKeyspace stores shared current-state data for an MSKU group. It identifies group membership and variation context while keeping variation-specific price, quantity, lifecycle, and other sellable state in the individual ItemKeyspace families. The group root references member item IDs; this is a logical relationship across keyspaces, not a cross-keyspace parent-child key.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ItemGroupRoot) Group identity, member item IDs, shared title/images, variation traits, group identifiers, version, and group lifecycle data. Root of the group ancestor tree; persisted primary key PK, normally equal to groupId. GroupDescription Shared description for the group, optionally compressed, with its revision timestamp. Child of the group ancestor; groupDescId, normally GROUP_DESC_<groupId>. GroupBusinessPolicies Shared group-level return, payment, and shipping policy content. Child of the group ancestor; plcsId, normally BIZ_POL_<groupId>. It inherits the policy field shape but has a distinct collection.

docs.title: ListingDraft
docs.text:
ListingDraft is the working-state family used while a listing is being constructed or revised before publication. A single draftId ancestor can contain SSKU item content, MSKU group content, compatibility content, group description content, and one ItemDraft per active MSKU variation. These docsets are storage children of the same draft ancestor even when one docset is logically associated with the item or group portion.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ListingDraftRoot) Draft session state, flags, scratch values, progress metadata, dates, and the list of variation item IDs. Root of the draft ancestor tree; persisted primary key PK, normally equal to draftId. ItemDraft Draft content for an SSKU item or one MSKU variation, including title, description, price, quantity, seller, terms, categories, media, and revision metadata. Direct child of the draft ancestor; PK, normally ITEM_<draftId> for SSKU or ITEM_<draftId>_<variationId> for an MSKU variation. ItemDraftCompatibility Optional SSKU compatibility payload for the draft item. Direct storage child of the draft ancestor, logically associated with ItemDraft; DraftCompID, normally COMPAT_<draftId>. ItemGroupDraft Shared MSKU draft-group content: group title, images, variation traits, seller group key, policies, and group ID. Direct child of the draft ancestor; PK, normally GROUP_<draftId>. ItemGroupDraftDesc Optional shared MSKU group description and description revision metadata. Direct storage child of the draft ancestor, logically associated with ItemGroupDraft; PK, normally GROUPDESC_<draftId>. ItemGroupDraftCompatibility Optional MSKU group-level compatibility payload. Direct storage child of the draft ancestor, logically associated with ItemGroupDraft; DraftCompID, normally GROUPCOMPAT_<draftId>.

docs.title: UserListingDraft
docs.text:
UserListingDraft is an index family for finding active listing drafts by user. It stores summary and lookup metadata rather than the full draft payload. It is intentionally separate from ListingDraft, so a user-index mutation does not automatically mutate the draft content tree.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context UserItemDraftMap (UserListingDraftMap) User-scoped summary of an active draft, including draftId, user, title, marketplace/application, category, images, creation mode, and timestamps. User-and-draft composite ancestor key; the schema class has no persisted primary-key field. Conceptually UserListingDraft/<userId>/<draftId>.

docs.title: ListingRevisionKeyspace
docs.text:
ListingRevisionKeyspace stores historical changes rather than the latest listing state. A listing ancestor can have an optional retention root, one or more generated revision documents, and detail children describing the non-variation and variation properties changed by each revision.

Docset Description and purpose Hierarchy and key context __ROOT__ (ListingRevisionRoot) Conditional retention state for a listing's revision history, including the listing identifier and TTL-maintenance fields. Optional sibling under the listing ancestor; lstgId identifies the listing. Normal revision inserts do not create it. ListingRevision Revision summary: changed property groups, revision/version identifiers, application, significant revision count, creation flag, and revision timestamp. Generated child of the listing ancestor; the schema has no persisted key field. ListingRevisionDetail Non-variation property-level change record with property group, property, change type, old value, new value, and display label. Generated child of a particular ListingRevision; the schema has no persisted key field. VariationRevisionDetail Variation-specific property-level change record with variation ID, changed variation property, trait values, change type, and old/new values. Generated child of a particular ListingRevision; the schema has no persisted key field.

docs.title: 1. End-to-end producer flow
docs.text:
The common path is:

REST resource or V1 dual-write trigger
  -> validation and processor selection
  -> V2 model-to-NuData document converter
  -> ancestor/child key construction
  -> transactional MonStor mutation
  -> later multi-docset get/query response

The V2 resources call processors directly. V1 listing and draft resources first pass through DualWriteProcessor or DraftDualWriteProcessor; those processors convert legacy payloads to V2 models and decide whether the NuData write is asynchronous, synchronous, parallel, or disabled by a ramp/config gate. A successful V2 write is not evidence that Oracle/Caty was or was not also written; those systems are outside this document's count.

The persistence boundary is a set of documents under an item, group, draft, user, or listing-revision ancestor. DocumentConverter, ItemGroupDocumentConverter, and DraftDocumentConverter construct the content. The processors then use MonStor InsertRequest, BatchMutateRequest, UpdateRequest, or DeleteRequest, generally with transactional options for multi-document operations. Consumers read current item and group state with multi-docset gets, read drafts through draft queries/gets, read active drafts through UserItemDraftMap, and read revision history through ancestor queries.

docs.title: 1.1. From request input to Java entity
docs.text:
There are two main producer entry paths:

  1. Direct V2 client input. A caller sends a JSON request to a V2 resource. The web framework binds the request body to the Java parameter declared by the resource: Item, ItemGroup, PriceAndQuantity, ListingDraft, or another operation-specific request type. The resource performs authorization and passes that typed object to the corresponding processor. For example, CoreItemResource.createItem(Item) passes an Item to CoreItemProcessor.insertItem(Item, ...), while CoreItemGroupResource.createItemGroup(ItemGroup) passes an ItemGroup to CoreItemGroupProcessor.insertItemGroup(ItemGroup, ...).

  2. Legacy V1 dual-write input. A legacy listing request is first represented by V1 Java entities such as Listing, ListingDetails, and SaleBo. DualWriteProcessor invokes ListingConverter, which builds one or more V2 Item objects and, only for an MSKU listing, an ItemGroup. The V1 listing ID, variation data, seller SKU, pricing, quantity, lifecycle, policies, and other source values are normalized into the V2 model before any NuData document is built. Runtime ramps can make this conversion/write synchronous, asynchronous, parallel, or disabled.

The important boundary is that NuData writers do not normally serialize the incoming HTTP JSON directly into storage. The request is first represented as a Java domain/request object, then passed through the processor and converter logic that applies the path's validation and normalization. The Java object is the source of truth for the document-building step described below.

docs.title: 1.2. Item producer path
docs.text:
For a direct V2 item create or replace, the flow is:

JSON request body
  -> Java Item
  -> CoreItemProcessor.insertItem/upsertItem
  -> DocumentConverter
  -> six ItemKeyspace Documents
  -> ancestor/child Keys
  -> transactional MonStor InsertRequest

CoreItemProcessor derives stable child identifiers from itemId, such as COMPAT_<itemId>, DESC_<itemId>, QTY_PRICE_<itemId>, ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId>, and BIZ_POL_<itemId>. It then asks DocumentConverter to build:

Java source object Converter method NuData document Item getRoot(item) ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__ Item getItemCompatibility(item, compatibilityId) ItemKeyspace/ItemCompatibility Item getDescription(item, descriptionId) ItemKeyspace/ItemDescription Item getQtyPrice(item, qtyPriceId) ItemKeyspace/ItemQtyPrice Item getItemDetails(item, itemDetailsId) ItemKeyspace/ItemDetails Item.businessPolicies getBusinessPolicies(..., bizPolId) ItemKeyspace/BusinessPolicies

Each converter creates a NuData schema object, copies or transforms Java properties, serializes that object through the configured Jackson ObjectMapper into an ObjectNode, and wraps it with DocumentFactory.createDocument(...). Examples of transformations include category and lifecycle construction, image conversion, amount conversion, expanded-versus-compressed descriptions and compatibilities, and conversion of return/payment/shipping terms.

The processor then builds the item ancestor key and child keys, adds the six documents to a transactional MonStor request, and executes it. A create path uses addForInsert; a replace/upsert path uses addForUpsert and can apply a core-listing-version filter to prevent an older update from overwriting newer state. A successful response means the accepted current item state has been written to the six logical docsets; it does not mean every possible auxiliary docset such as UuidMap or ItemLock was written.

docs.title: 1.3. ItemGroup producer path
docs.text:
For a direct V2 item-group create or the processor's upsert path, the flow is:

JSON request body
  -> Java ItemGroup
  -> CoreItemGroupProcessor.insertItemGroup/upsertItemGroup
  -> ItemGroupDocumentConverter + DocumentConverter
  -> three ItemGroupKeyspace Documents
  -> ancestor/child Keys
  -> transactional MonStor InsertRequest

CoreItemGroupProcessor derives GROUP_DESC_<groupId> and BIZ_POL_<groupId>, then builds:

Java source object Converter method NuData document ItemGroup ItemGroupDocumentConverter.getRoot(group, lastModifiedDate) ItemGroupKeyspace/__ROOT__ ItemGroup ItemGroupDocumentConverter.getDescription(group, descriptionId) ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupDescription ItemGroup.businessPolicies DocumentConverter.getBusinessPolicies(..., bizPolId) ItemGroupKeyspace/GroupBusinessPolicies

The group root contains group identity, member variation IDs, shared images, variation traits, group version, and group-level identifiers. The description and policy documents are separate child documents so they can be updated independently. The group processor adds all three documents to one transactional request; it does not write variation price or quantity into the group root.

The current CoreItemGroupResource replace methods are stubs that return null; the processor upsert path is nevertheless used by the V1 dual-write flow and is the code-proven group replacement implementation described here.

docs.title: 1.4. SSKU/MSKU conversion and write branching
docs.text:
The legacy conversion path determines whether a group exists before the NuData write:

V1 Listing + SaleBo
  -> ListingConverter.getItemsFromListing(...)
       -> one Item for SSKU
       -> one Item per active variation for MSKU
  -> ListingConverter.getItemGroupFromListing(...)
       -> null for SSKU
       -> one ItemGroup for MSKU
  -> group write (MSKU only)
  -> item write or batch item write

For an MSKU listing, ListingConverter creates the group ID from the parent listing ID, collects the active variation item IDs into ItemGroup.itemIds, and assigns that parent ID to each variation Item.groupId. Shared description, business policies, compatibilities, and some identifiers are stored on the group and cleared from the variation Item objects instead of being repeated. CoreItemProcessor.insertItems(...) then builds and inserts the complete six-document item family for each variation.

For an SSKU listing, the converter returns one ordinary Item and no ItemGroup; the processor writes only the item family. An MSKU with one active variation still takes the MSKU branch and writes an ItemGroup whose itemIds contains one variation ID.

docs.title: 1.5. Draft input follows the same boundary with a draft model
docs.text: For V2 listing drafts, the request body is bound to ListingDraft. The draft processor validates it and DraftDocumentConverter builds the draft root, item drafts, optional group draft, descriptions, and compatibility documents. The converter assigns or normalizes draft variation IDs, serializes each NuData schema object into a Document, and the processor writes the assembled documents transactionally. SSKU drafts have item content without a group draft; MSKU drafts have group content plus one item draft per variation.

docs.title: 1.6. Partial updates do not rebuild the whole Java entity
docs.text: Operation-specific requests such as price/quantity, category, product reference, hold status, business-policy reference, description, or item lock updates can bypass the full create/replace conversion. The processor converts only the changed request data or builds an update operation directly against the affected root or child docset. For example, price/quantity changes target ItemQtyPrice and related root state, a category change targets the root category fields, and a lock operation writes ItemLock plus its inventory side effect. Therefore, “one item write” may mean a six-docset replacement or a narrower mutation of one or two existing docsets.

docs.title: 2. Schema, key layout, field inventory, and model lineage
docs.text: Docset is the repository's schema abstraction: a Java class represents a NuData collection and getCollectionName() returns the collection name (crlstngsvService/src/main/java/com/ebay/app/cls/nudata/Docset.java). Nested helper classes such as Price, Lifecycle, TermsAndPolicies, and ShippingTerms are fields inside a document; they are not separate docsets.

docs.title: Item family: ItemKeyspace
docs.text:
The root key is KeyFactory.create(itemId). The child documents are descendants of that root:

itemId
├── ItemCompatibility / COMPAT_<itemId>
├── ItemDescription / DESC_<itemId>
├── ItemQtyPrice / QTY_PRICE_<itemId>
├── BusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<itemId>
├── ItemDetails / ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId>
└── ItemLock / LOCK_<lockId>

The lock-summary document uses the same ItemLock schema and reserved identifier LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$. Lock mutations also update ItemQtyPrice to reflect reserved inventory. UuidMap uses a different key shape: UUID_<sellerId>/<uuid> with a UUID_MAP child.

Docset Document role and representative fields __ROOT__ Core listing state: PK, title, category, lifecycle, seller/listing identifiers, location, images, policies/terms references, version/revision fields, onHold, endRsn, and other item-level state. DocumentConverter.getRoot() maps the V2 Item into this document. ItemCompatibility Fitment/compatibility payload: ItemCompID, compat or compressed cmpCompat, and ftExempt. ItemDescription Description payload: ItemDescID, desc or compressed compDesc, and descRevsnDt. ItemQtyPrice Inventory and commercial values: availQty, qtySold, price, and minRmntSet; price contains fixed, auction, marketing, original-retail, cost-of-goods, and price-guarantee data. ItemDetails Additional item details such as hasRlxdRls, high-precision fixed/start prices, source listing, and supporting documents. BusinessPolicies Policy content: policy identifiers plus return, payment, and shipping terms. UuidMap UUID/seller lookup value containing listingId and listingAppId; used to resolve or anonymize a listing mapping. ItemLock Reservation/lock documents with pk, status (A, C, X), quantity, expiration, timestamps, and UUID; the summary record stores aggregate reserved quantity.

The six-document item create/replace set is: __ROOT__, ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDetails, and BusinessPolicies. The UuidMap and ItemLock documents are not part of the normal item payload mutation.

docs.title: ItemKeyspace elaboration
docs.text: ItemKeyspace is the current-state store for one individual listing item. __ROOT__ holds the broad item state, while the child docsets isolate compatibility, description, quantity/price, details, and business-policy content that can be updated independently. UuidMap and ItemLock support lookup and reservation workflows rather than representing additional top-level item payloads. Consumers should use the item root as the identity anchor and treat child documents as parts of the same item state, not as independent listings.

docs.title: Relationship between ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace
docs.text:
These are separate keyspace families with separate ancestors and separate root documents. ItemKeyspace stores the individual item or variation records; ItemGroupKeyspace stores the multi-variation group identity, membership, shared traits, group description, and group-level policies. For an MSKU group, the group root's itemIds identifies its member item roots, and the item root's grpId points back to the group. This is a logical relationship, not a parent-child key relationship across keyspaces.

The two families therefore have different write responsibilities: item operations write variation/listing state such as quantity, price, lifecycle, description, and item compatibility, while group operations write membership, variation traits, group description, and group policies. A consumer must read both families to reconstruct a complete MSKU listing; a group document alone does not contain the full variation-level commercial state, and an item document alone does not establish the complete group membership.

docs.title: Single-SKU versus one-variation MSKU
docs.text:
The repository distinguishes SSKU versus MSKU by the listing's MSKU flag, not by counting variation records:

Listing condition ItemKeyspace result ItemGroupKeyspace result SSKU (saleBo.isMsku() is false) One ordinary item document family is created or updated. No ItemGroup record is created; getItemGroupFromListing(...) returns null. MSKU with one active/non-deleted variation One item record is created for that variation. Its groupId points to the parent listing/group ID. The MSKU group is still created with __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies; the group root's itemIds contains exactly that one variation item ID. MSKU with multiple active/non-deleted variations One item record is created per active variation. The same group docsets are created, and itemIds contains all active variation item IDs.

For the one-variation MSKU case, the group record is therefore not omitted or collapsed into the item record. The group ID is the parent listing ID, while the sole itemIds value is the separate variation item ID. A consumer should not infer “SSKU” merely because itemIds has length one; it must use the listing's MSKU classification and the presence of the group record.

docs.title: Item-group family: ItemGroupKeyspace
docs.text:
The group root is KeyFactory.create(groupId). Child keys are descendants:

groupId
├── GroupDescription / GROUP_DESC_<groupId>
└── GroupBusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<groupId>
Docset Document role and representative fields __ROOT__ Group identity and membership: PK, title, itemIds, seller/group key, variation traits, images, group version, group draft ID, and administrative/lifecycle fields. GroupDescription Group description, optionally compressed, with groupDescId and grpDescRevsnDt. GroupBusinessPolicies Group-level business policies. It extends the business-policy model but returns the group-specific collection name.

CoreItemGroupProcessor creates or upserts all three documents transactionally. Group shipping updates touch the root and GroupBusinessPolicies; description updates touch the root and GroupDescription.

docs.title: ItemGroupKeyspace elaboration
docs.text: ItemGroupKeyspace is the current-state store for an item group, most notably the shared structure of an MSKU listing. Its root describes the group and its member IDs; GroupDescription and GroupBusinessPolicies hold independently addressable group content. GroupBusinessPolicies uses the group collection name even though its fields inherit the item policy schema, so it must not be counted as the item BusinessPolicies docset. Group-level state also does not replace the item-level documents for the group's variations.

docs.title: Listing-draft family: ListingDraft
docs.text:
The draft root is keyed by draftId. The processor uses prefixes such as GROUP_, GROUPDESC_, GROUPCOMPAT_, ITEM_, and COMPAT_. The key relationship is:

draftId
├── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId>                 (SSKU)
├── ItemDraftCompatibility / COMPAT_<draftId>  (optional SSKU)
├── ItemGroupDraft / GROUP_<draftId>            (MSKU)
├── ItemGroupDraftDesc / GROUPDESC_<draftId>   (MSKU)
├── ItemGroupDraftCompatibility / GROUPCOMPAT_<draftId> (optional MSKU)
└── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId>_<variationId>   (MSKU variations)
Docset Document role and representative fields __ROOT__ Draft session, flags, scratch details, draft/creation/revision dates, and the list of MSKU variation IDs. ItemDraft SSKU or variation content including title, description, price, quantity, seller, listing terms, categories, images, and revision fields. ItemGroupDraft MSKU group title, images, variation traits, seller group key, business policies, and group ID. ItemDraftCompatibility Optional SSKU compatibility payload, compressed when configured. ItemGroupDraftCompatibility Optional MSKU group compatibility payload, compressed when configured. ItemGroupDraftDesc MSKU group description, optionally compressed, plus description revision date.

An SSKU draft normally writes two or three docsets: root, item, and optional item compatibility. An MSKU draft writes root, group, group description, optional group compatibility, and one or more ItemDraft variation documents. The variation count changes the number of documents, not the number of logical docsets.

docs.title: ListingDraft elaboration
docs.text: ListingDraft is a working-state store for listing construction before or during publication. SSKU drafts use item documents, while MSKU drafts add a group root, group description, optional group compatibility, and one item document per variation. Draft documents are not proof that a live ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace listing exists; they are a separate content model and lifecycle.

docs.title: User active-draft family: UserListingDraft
docs.text: UserItemDraftMap is keyed below a user root and draft identifier. Its representative fields are draftId, marketplace/application identifiers, category, title, image URLs, creation mode/date, user ID, and lastModifiedDate. It is a separate index/map from the content in ListingDraft; updating or deleting one does not imply that the other is automatically changed unless the caller invokes both flows.

docs.title: UserListingDraft elaboration
docs.text: UserListingDraft is an index for finding active drafts by user. Its UserItemDraftMap document contains summary metadata and lookup identifiers, not the complete draft payload. It can therefore be created, updated, or deleted independently of the corresponding ListingDraft content, subject to the caller's dual-write behavior.

docs.title: Revision-history family: ListingRevisionKeyspace
docs.text:
The listing ID is the ancestor. A normal insert creates a generated child key for ListingRevision, then generated child keys for optional details:

listingId
├── __ROOT__ / listingId [optional TTL-maintenance root]
└── ListingRevision / generated-guid
    ├── ListingRevisionDetail / generated-guid (zero or more)
    └── VariationRevisionDetail / generated-guid (zero or more)

The __ROOT__ document is an optional sibling under the listing ancestor. It is created or updated by expired-date maintenance, not by the normal revision insert. ListingRevision contains revised property groups, version/application identifiers, significant revision count, revised date, and updated core-listing version. Detail documents contain revised group/property, change type, old/new values, and (for variation details) variation traits/ID.

The declared revision root class exists as a schema class and is queried by the revision-history code, but RevisionHistoryNudataClient.addForInsert() explicitly does not create a root document in the normal insert path. A separate expired-date upsert path can create/update that root, so it remains a declared and conditional write target rather than a normal revision-insert target.

docs.title: ListingRevisionKeyspace elaboration
docs.text: ListingRevisionKeyspace is historical rather than current-state storage. ListingRevision records a revision summary under a listing ancestor, and detail children record property-level changes, including variation-specific changes. A revision document should be interpreted as an event/history record, not as a replacement for the latest ItemKeyspace or ItemGroupKeyspace state. The declared revision root is an exception: it participates in expired-date maintenance but is intentionally omitted from ordinary revision inserts.

docs.title: Detailed field schema and source-model lineage
docs.text: The following inventory lists the JSON properties declared directly on each docset class. Java types are included where they clarify whether a field is a scalar, list, enum, or embedded object. Fields inside embedded objects are not repeated as docsets: for example, ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__.category is a Category value containing category fields, but Category is not another NuData collection. The source classes use Jackson annotations, so the JSON property names below are the persisted names, not necessarily the Java member names. For item and item-group docsets, each table also includes the write-side source property or expression.

docs.title: Complete NuDoc hierarchies and primary keys
docs.text: NuData uses several independent ancestor trees. A keyspace is a storage namespace that can contain more than one tree; ItemKeyspace, for example, contains the normal item tree, the UUID lookup tree, and the item-lock subtree. A docset is a child of another docset only when its storage key is constructed beneath that ancestor. Sharing a keyspace does not by itself make two docsets parent and child.

docs.title: Item current-state and auxiliary lookup trees
docs.text:
ItemKeyspace
├── itemId [ItemRoot / PK]
│   ├── ItemCompatibility / COMPAT_<itemId> [ItemCompID]
│   ├── ItemDescription / DESC_<itemId> [ItemDescID]
│   ├── ItemQtyPrice / QTY_PRICE_<itemId> [ItemQtyPriceID]
│   ├── ItemDetails / ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId> [itemDetailsID]
│   ├── BusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<itemId> [plcsId]
│   └── ItemLock / LOCK_<lockId> [pk; summary: LOCK_$$$SUMMARY$$$]
└── UUID_<sellerId>/<uuid>
    └── UuidMap / UUID_MAP [seller ID + UUID]

UuidMap is an auxiliary lookup tree, not a child payload of ItemRoot. ItemLock uses the item ancestor and is operationally associated with the quantity/price document because lock mutations update reserved inventory there as a side effect.

docs.title: Item-group current-state tree
docs.text:
ItemGroupKeyspace
└── groupId [ItemGroupRoot / PK]
    ├── GroupDescription / GROUP_DESC_<groupId> [groupDescId]
    └── GroupBusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<groupId> [plcsId]

docs.title: Listing-draft tree
docs.text:
ListingDraft
└── draftId [ListingDraftRoot / PK]
    ├── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId> [PK]                         (SSKU)
    ├── ItemDraftCompatibility / COMPAT_<draftId> [DraftCompID] (optional SSKU)
    ├── ItemGroupDraft / GROUP_<draftId> [PK]                  (MSKU)
    ├── ItemGroupDraftDesc / GROUPDESC_<draftId> [PK]          (MSKU)
    ├── ItemGroupDraftCompatibility / GROUPCOMPAT_<draftId> [DraftCompID] (optional MSKU)
    └── ItemDraft / ITEM_<draftId>_<variationId> [PK]           (MSKU variation)

All six logical docsets are storage children of the same draftId ancestor. The compatibility and group-description documents are logically associated with the item or group portion of the draft, but they are not nested beneath those documents in the storage key path. An MSKU draft can contain multiple ItemDraft documents, one for each active variation.

docs.title: Active-user draft index tree
docs.text:
UserListingDraft
└── userId
    └── UserItemDraftMap / draftId [composite key: userId + draftId]

UserItemDraftMap has no persisted key field in its schema class; its key is the composite user-and-draft ancestor shape. The repository documents the two-part key but does not expose a serialized delimiter or additional prefix. It is separate from the full ListingDraft content tree.

docs.title: Listing-revision history tree
docs.text:
ListingRevisionKeyspace
└── listingId [revision ancestor]
    ├── __ROOT__ / listingId [lstgId; optional TTL-maintenance root]
    └── ListingRevision / <generated-guid> [no persisted key field]
        ├── ListingRevisionDetail / <generated-guid> [no persisted key field]
        └── VariationRevisionDetail / <generated-guid> [no persisted key field]

The revision root is conditional: TTL maintenance can upsert it, but the normal revision-insert path starts at ListingRevision. Detail documents are children of a particular generated revision key.
