docs.title: Field-schema interpretation
docs.text:
• The lists above are top-level persisted properties from the repository's Java schema classes. They are not a promise that every property is present on every document; converters may omit null values, and update paths may set or unset only a subset.
  • compat/cmpCompat and desc/compDesc show the repository's expanded versus compressed representation choice.
  • BusinessPolicies is reused by item, group, and draft models as an embedded object, while GroupBusinessPolicies is the separate group docset that inherits the same four top-level policy fields.
  • The four classes named __ROOT__ are different schemas in different packages. Their matching class names do not make them one shared collection across keyspaces.
  • getCollectionName() is the authoritative logical collection name in the source. The revision classes return their fully qualified Java class name, while the revision constants and mutation code use the short docset names ListingRevision, ListingRevisionDetail, and VariationRevisionDetail.

docs.title: Write-side lineage notes
docs.text:
The mappings in these tables follow the write-side converters, not just matching names by convention. A derived mapping means the JSON field is assembled from multiple model properties or converted to a NuData-specific embedded type. An update-only mapping is not populated by the standard create/replace converter; it is changed by a separate processor mutation.

The item root also has direct update methods that bypass full model conversion. For example, category updates set the nested category fields, price/quantity updates set selected root and child fields, and media updates set images/prdGallryFallbckURL-related root state. Therefore, the tables describe the full-document source model while partial operations may update only a subset.

The group root and child documents also have partial update paths that can change selected fields without reconstructing the entire ItemGroup payload.

docs.title: 3. Operation-to-docset write matrix
docs.text:
The matrix describes docset families, not individual documents. “Optional” means the request shape or operation determines whether the mutation is included.

Business operation NuData mutation and docsets Create/replace V2 item Insert or upsert six item docsets: __ROOT__, ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDetails, BusinessPolicies. Reconcile variants can omit ItemDetails or gate compatibility updates. Bulk replace items Calls the same item upsert path independently/asynchronously per item, so the same six-docset family is possible for each item. Item compatibility update Upsert ItemCompatibility only. Item description/revision update Update item __ROOT__ revision/version fields and ItemDescription. Item price/quantity/inventory update Update ItemQtyPrice and usually __ROOT__; may also update BusinessPolicies for payment fields and upsert ItemDetails for high-precision/detail state. Quantity/lifecycle inventory update Update ItemQtyPrice and __ROOT__ for quantities, scheduled/end dates, end reason, and core-listing version. Shipping/policy update Update item __ROOT__ and BusinessPolicies; group equivalent updates touch group __ROOT__ and GroupBusinessPolicies. Category/media/version/administrative item update Usually update item __ROOT__; category, media, hold, duplicate, relist, HTTPS, and related fields are root fields. MSKU variants use batch root updates. Item lock create/reactivate/commit/cancel/extend Write/update/delete ItemLock, plus update the item ItemQtyPrice quantities and the ItemLock summary. A lock operation therefore can touch two logical docsets, with ItemQtyPrice as the inventory side effect. UUID mapping create/delete/anonymize Insert/delete UuidMap. PII deletion anonymizes the UUID mapping and clears supported PII fields in item root/business-policy documents. Delete item variations Delete item root, compatibility, description, quantity/price, business-policy, details, and lock-summary keys. Individual lock children are handled by lock lifecycle operations; this delete list is not a blanket delete of every descendant. Create/replace item group Insert or upsert group __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies. Delete item group Delete group __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies. Create SSKU listing draft Insert root and ItemDraft; insert ItemDraftCompatibility only when compatibility exists. Create MSKU listing draft Insert root, ItemGroupDraft, ItemGroupDraftDesc, optional ItemGroupDraftCompatibility, and one ItemDraft per variation. Update listing draft Batch upsert root and current item documents, delete removed variation items, upsert/delete the applicable compatibility docset, and upsert/delete group/group-description documents as the draft changes between MSKU and SSKU. Delete listing draft Delete root, group/group-description/group-compatibility, item compatibility, and all descendant ItemDraft documents found by ancestor query. Create/update active user draft Insert, update, or upsert one UserItemDraftMap document. Delete active user drafts Delete the selected UserItemDraftMap documents. Insert revision history Insert one ListingRevision plus zero or more ListingRevisionDetail and VariationRevisionDetail children. Bulk backfill uses the same three docsets in one accumulated request. Revision expired-date maintenance Upsert the revision-history __ROOT__ document when that maintenance path is invoked. Archive hold update ArchiveItemProcessor inherits item update logic but overrides the hold-update keyspace; the proven archive write is ItemKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__. Archive group version update ArchiveItemGroupProcessor overrides the group-version keyspace; the proven archive write is ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive/__ROOT__.

docs.title: 4. V1 dual-write and feature-gated behavior
docs.text:
V1 listing operations do not have a second, independent NuData schema. They flow through DualWriteProcessor, which dispatches operations such as add, relist, revise inventory, end, finalize, description, shipping, media, markdown-sale, second-chance, hold, and HTTPS updates to the V2 item/group processors. The resulting docsets are therefore the same item and group families described above.

DraftDualWriteProcessor similarly converts V1 drafts into V2 ListingDraft content and can maintain the active UserItemDraftMap index. These writes may be asynchronous fire-and-forget tasks, and reconciliation or failure events can cause retries or alternate paths.

Whether a V1 request writes NuData depends on runtime configuration and ramps. The code contains controls for disabling NuData, V2-primary migration, parallel update, create/update/end dual-write, and draft dual-write behavior. Consequently, the matrix describes code-proven targets, not a guarantee that every production request reaches every target.

docs.title: Counts
docs.text: Count type Result Meaning Declared logical docsets 22 Distinct docset classes/collection names represented in the live schema packages. Nested Java value objects are excluded. Normal item create/replace targets 6 The six item documents built by CoreItemProcessor for the standard payload path. Normal item-group create/replace targets 3 Group root, group description, and group business policies. Listing-draft logical targets 6 Six declared draft docsets; one SSKU request writes root plus item and optional compatibility (2–3 documents), while an MSKU request writes root, group, description, optional compatibility, and one item document per variation (3+N or 4+N documents). User active-draft target 1 UserItemDraftMap. Normal revision insert targets 1–3 Revision plus optional listing and variation detail children; the revision root is not in this normal insert. Proven keyspace-qualified write sinks 24 The 22 live logical pairs plus two archive root pairs.

docs.title: Important boundaries
docs.text:
• The counts are for NuData/MonStor structures visible in this repository. They exclude Oracle, Caty, SaleBO, and any downstream physical stores.
  • A docset count is not a row/document count. MSKU drafts and revisions can create many documents in one logical docset.
  • A class in the package is not proof that every path writes it. For example, revision __ROOT__ is declared and read but omitted from the ordinary revision insert; UuidMap and ItemLock are auxiliary flows.
  • Archive processors mostly read archive keyspaces. Only the overridden hold and group-version methods prove archive writes in this repository.
  • Deletes are key-specific. A delete request may remove a known set of child keys and may use an ancestor query for variation documents; it should not be interpreted as a schema drop or a physical table drop.
  • The document classes expose JSON property names, but this repository does not show a complete MonStor index/partition/replication DDL. The inventory therefore describes document shape and key ancestry, not every physical storage-engine index.
  • Dual-write order, async execution, retry, rollback, and ramps affect when a write is observed and whether it is attempted. They do not create additional logical NuData docsets.

docs.title: 6. Q&A for Item and ItemGroup readers
docs.text: This section answers questions a reader familiar with eBay shopping concepts may ask when first encountering the Java entities and NuData docsets. The answers are limited to behavior shown by this repository.

docs.title: What is an Item in this service?
docs.text: Item is the Java V2 entity for one listing-level or variation-level sellable record. For an SSKU listing, it represents the single sellable item. For an MSKU listing, the service creates one Item for each active variation, with variation-specific quantity, price, identifiers, and other item state.

docs.title: What is an ItemGroup?
docs.text: ItemGroup is the Java V2 entity for the shared parent of an MSKU listing. It stores the group identity, title, membership, variation traits, shared images, group description, and group-level business policies. It is not a second copy of every variation's commercial state.

docs.title: Does every Item have an ItemGroup?
docs.text: No. An SSKU item has an ItemKeyspace record family and no corresponding ItemGroupKeyspace record. An MSKU item has an ItemGroupKeyspace group, and its item root contains grpId pointing to that group.

docs.title: If an MSKU has only one active variation, is the ItemGroup still created?
docs.text: Yes. The repository uses the MSKU classification flag, not the number of active variations, to decide whether a group exists. An MSKU with one active variation has one item record and an item-group root whose itemIds list contains exactly that one variation item ID.

docs.title: Is a one-item itemIds list evidence that the listing is SSKU?
docs.text: No. A one-entry itemIds list can be a valid one-variation MSKU group. To classify the listing, use the MSKU/SSKU behavior and the presence of the ItemGroupKeyspace group, not the list length alone.

docs.title: Is the eBay seller SKU the same as the NuData item ID?
docs.text: No. The NuData item ID (Item.itemId, persisted as PK) identifies the service record. The seller-provided SKU is represented separately by Item.sellerItemKey and persisted as slrItemKey. For a group, the seller's group key is stored on ItemGroup.sellerGroupKey.

docs.title: Does one Java Item object map to one NuData document?
docs.text: No. The Java Item is converted into an item document family. The root ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__ contains broad item state, while child docsets hold compatibility, description, quantity/price, details, and business-policy state. A full create/replace can therefore write six item docsets for one Java Item.

docs.title: Does one Java ItemGroup object map to one NuData document?
docs.text: No. A full group write creates or upserts three documents under the group ancestor: __ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies. ItemGroup is the source entity; the docsets are the persistence representation.

docs.title: Are ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace SQL tables?
docs.text: They are logical NuData/MonStor keyspace families, not SQL tables shown by this repository. Each docset class defines a persisted document shape and each ancestor/child key defines where that document belongs. The counts in this document are logical docset and proven sink counts, not relational table DDL counts.

docs.title: Which fields belong to the item and which belong to the group?
docs.text: Variation-specific commercial state belongs to Item, especially quantity and price in ItemQtyPrice, along with variation identifiers and lifecycle state. Shared MSKU state belongs to ItemGroup, including membership, variation traits, group description, shared images, and group policies. The converter explicitly clears description, business policies, compatibilities, and global identifiers from MSKU variation Item objects when those values are stored at group level.

docs.title: Where is the description stored for SSKU versus MSKU?
docs.text: For SSKU, the description is written to the item's ItemDescription docset. For MSKU, the shared description is written to the group's GroupDescription docset rather than repeated on every variation item.

docs.title: Where are business policies stored for SSKU versus MSKU?
docs.text: For SSKU, return, payment, and shipping terms are written to the item's BusinessPolicies docset and related root policy fields. For MSKU, the shared terms are written to GroupBusinessPolicies; the group collection name is different even though the policy field schema is inherited from the item business-policy model.

docs.title: Where are price and quantity stored?
docs.text: Price and quantity are variation/item-level state. They are primarily written to ItemQtyPrice, whose price object contains fixed, auction, marketing, original-retail, cost-of-goods, and price-guarantee values, while availQty, qtySold, and minRmntSet hold inventory-related values. They are not represented by the group root merely because the item belongs to an MSKU group.

docs.title: Are Price, Lifecycle, and BusinessPolicies separate docsets?
docs.text: No. In the item root, Price and Lifecycle are embedded Java value objects. The policy terms inside the item root are also embedded. BusinessPolicies is a separate docset only when referring to the item policy document; the group equivalent is the separate GroupBusinessPolicies docset.

docs.title: Why do several keyspaces have a __ROOT__ class?
docs.text: The class name is reused across different Java packages, but the schemas and collections are different. ItemKeyspace/__ROOT__ is an item root, ItemGroupKeyspace/__ROOT__ is a group root, and the draft and revision roots have their own meanings. They must be identified by keyspace and docset, not by the class name alone.

docs.title: Can a consumer reconstruct a complete MSKU listing from the group alone?
docs.text: No. The group provides shared structure and the list of variation item IDs. The consumer must fetch the corresponding ItemKeyspace item families to obtain each variation's price, quantity, lifecycle, and other item-level state. Conversely, an item alone does not establish the complete group membership.

docs.title: 7. Evidence map
docs.text:
The primary source locations for the walkthrough are:

  • Docset.java - document-set schema abstraction.
  • CoreItemProcessor.java - item keys, six-document insert/upsert, partial mutations, locks, UUID map, PII, and delete paths.
  • DocumentConverter.java - item root and child document construction.
  • ListingConverter.java - SSKU/MSKU classification, variation item creation, and group itemIds construction.
  • CoreItemGroupProcessor.java - group keys and three-document mutations.
  • ItemGroupDocumentConverter.java - group document construction.
  • CoreListingDraftProcessor.java - SSKU/MSKU draft insert, upsert, and delete behavior.
  • DraftDocumentConverter.java - draft root, item, group, description, and compatibility documents.
  • UserListingDraftProcessor.java - active-draft map insert/update/delete.
  • RevisionHistoryNudataClient.java - revision and optional child inserts.
  • RevisionHistoryConstants.java - revision keyspace and docset names.
  • DualWriteProcessor.java and DraftDualWriteProcessor.java - V1-to-V2 routing and asynchronous/ramped behavior.
  • ArchiveItemProcessor.java and ArchiveItemGroupProcessor.java - archive keyspace overrides.

docs.title: Why Selling's NuData Schema Is a Producer Model
Executive conclusion
docs.text:
Core Listing Service stores listing data in NuData to operate the Selling workflow: create and revise listings, update price and quantity, manage variation groups, find active drafts, reserve inventory, and retain revision history. It is a producer-side operational model, not a consumer-ready record for analytics, reporting, or general self-service use.

The five live logical keyspaces and 22 declared docsets preserve the producer's identity, lifecycle, ownership, payload, and mutation boundaries. As a result, a downstream consumer does not receive one complete, flat listing record. To create an easy-to-read data product, downstream processing must assemble the necessary documents, choose the intended lifecycle state, decode alternative representations, normalize nested or repeated values, and publish governed consumer entities.

This is not a criticism of the NuData design. The design is appropriate for the service that owns and changes listing state. The conclusion is that its storage shape should not be exposed as the default consumption shape.

docs.title: Scope and terminology
docs.text:
This analysis covers the five active logical keyspace families:

  1. ItemKeyspace
  2. ItemGroupKeyspace
  3. ListingDraft
  4. UserListingDraft
  5. ListingRevisionKeyspace

A keyspace is an operational storage family. A docset is a named stored-document type within that family. Neither is automatically a consumer-facing entity or relational table.

ItemKeyspaceArchive and ItemGroupKeyspaceArchive are physical archive write targets that reuse live item or group root schemas. They are not additional live logical families and are out of scope here.

docs.title: Why Selling uses five keyspaces
docs.text:
The split is primarily about business identity and lifecycle, not about creating five alternative copies of the same listing.

Keyspace Identity and lifecycle Producer-side purpose Consumer implication ItemKeyspace One current sellable item: an SSKU listing or one MSKU variation, keyed by item ID. Holds state that is changed and read at an individual sellable-item level. It is not always the complete customer-visible listing; an MSKU item needs group context. ItemGroupKeyspace One current MSKU group, keyed by group ID. Holds state shared by a variation set and the links to its member items. Consumers must assemble group and variation records deliberately. ListingDraft One working draft, keyed by draft ID, before or during publication. Separates editable, incomplete work from published state. Draft data is not proof that a live item or group exists. UserListingDraft A user-and-draft active-draft index. Finds a user's active draft summaries without reading complete draft content. It is a discovery index, not a duplicate of the draft payload. ListingRevisionKeyspace History for an item or group listing, keyed by listing ID. Retains revision summaries and changed-property details separately from latest state. It must not be mixed with current-state fields when producing a current listing view.

The lifecycle is therefore:

UserListingDraft (find active draft)
          |
          v
ListingDraft (working state) ---- publish ----> ItemKeyspace (current item state)
                                                     ^
                                                     |
                                   ItemGroupKeyspace (shared MSKU state)

ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace changes ----> ListingRevisionKeyspace (history)

The arrows describe business relationships and service flows. They are not relational joins supplied by NuData.

docs.title: The five families and 22 declared logical docsets
docs.text:
Keyspace Logical docsets Count ItemKeyspace __ROOT__, ItemCompatibility, ItemDescription, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDetails, BusinessPolicies, UuidMap, ItemLock 8 ItemGroupKeyspace __ROOT__, GroupDescription, GroupBusinessPolicies 3 ListingDraft __ROOT__, ItemDraft, ItemDraftCompatibility, ItemGroupDraft, ItemGroupDraftCompatibility, ItemGroupDraftDesc 6 UserListingDraft UserItemDraftMap 1 ListingRevisionKeyspace __ROOT__, ListingRevision, ListingRevisionDetail, VariationRevisionDetail 4 Total 22

This is a schema-declaration count. A single producer operation writes only the docsets needed for that operation; it does not write all 22 documents.

docs.title: Why Item and Item Group are separate
docs.text: The distinction is clearest for SSKU and MSKU listings.

docs.title: SSKU: one sellable item
docs.text:
An SSKU has no variation parent. Its current state is held in one ItemKeyspace document family.

ItemKeyspace / itemId
├── __ROOT__                 broad current item state
├── ItemQtyPrice             sellable price and quantity
├── ItemDescription          seller description
└── other optional or operational item docsets

docs.title: MSKU: one shared group and many sellable variations
docs.text:
An MSKU has data with two different ownership boundaries:

ItemGroupKeyspace / groupId
├── __ROOT__                 group title, itemIds, variation dimensions, shared images
├── GroupDescription         shared description
└── GroupBusinessPolicies    shared policies

ItemKeyspace / itemId-1      first sellable variation
ItemKeyspace / itemId-2      second sellable variation
...
ItemKeyspace / itemId-N      Nth sellable variation

The ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__.itemIds value identifies the member variations. Each member item has isVariation=true, but it remains its own sellable item with an item-level lifecycle and price/quantity state.

Concern MSKU group owns it once Variation item owns it per sellable SKU Listing structure Group identity, member item IDs, variation traits, trait-driven images The variation's selected trait values Shared seller content Group title, description, business policies, shared images Item-specific content when applicable Commercial operations Not the price or inventory counter for every variation Price, available quantity, sold quantity, locks, and item lifecycle

Storing shared data once avoids copying group-owned content to every variation. Storing commercial state per variation allows a price or inventory change to address only the sellable SKU that changed. This is a producer ownership and mutation design, not a ready-made parent/child reporting table.

docs.title: Why ItemKeyspace has many docsets
docs.text:
ItemKeyspace is the current-state family with the broadest set of Selling operations. Its docsets split state by update behavior, payload character, specialization, and lookup or reservation purpose.

Docset Producer boundary Why it is separate __ROOT__ Broad item identity, seller/location, category, lifecycle, flags, media references, and other item state. A price update or description-only read should not require rebuilding or fetching the broad item payload. ItemQtyPrice Available quantity, quantity sold, remnant rules, and price variants. This is the focused commercial state used by price and inventory operations. ItemDescription Seller description and description revision time. Description can be large, has its own revision, and can be stored expanded or compressed. ItemCompatibility Parts fitment or compatibility content. This is specialized, potentially large content that common item reads need not carry. BusinessPolicies Return, payment, and shipping policy content. Policies are a cohesive policy payload with a different access and update boundary from core item identity. ItemDetails High-precision prices, relaxed-rule state, and supporting seller documents. Specialized details do not belong on every common item path. ItemLock Inventory reservation and lock-summary state. Lock flows have a dedicated operational lifecycle and should not rewrite broad item state. UuidMap Seller-and-UUID lookup to listing and application identifiers. UUID-specific lookup avoids treating a broad item document as a lookup index.

The first six are the normal current-item document family. ItemLock and UuidMap are auxiliary operational branches in the same keyspace, not fields that every item create or full-item read must use.

docs.title: Design principle: partition by producer access pattern
docs.text:
Selling does not start with the question, “What fields should a consumer see in one listing record?” It starts with, “Which part of listing state does this service own, change, or need for this operation?” A docset is created when that part of the item has a meaningfully different mutation, retrieval, payload, or operational-identity boundary.

Producer question Docset design response ItemKeyspace example Does this state change on a focused commercial operation? Keep it independently addressable from broad listing state. Purchases and price updates address hot ItemQtyPrice, rather than rewriting category, media, lifecycle, and other root fields. Is this content large, irregular, or unnecessary for many reads? Put it in an optional payload that readers request only when needed. ItemDescription and ItemCompatibility hold seller text and fitment; each can use an expanded or compressed representation. Does the operation have specialized or infrequent behavior? Keep its data out of the common item path. ItemDetails holds high-precision prices and seller documents; ItemCompatibility supports fitment-specific behavior. Does the operation need its own key and lifecycle? Use a purpose-specific document shape instead of overloading the item root. ItemLock manages reservations and a lock summary; UuidMap supports seller-and-UUID lookup.

This principle makes docsets selective retrieval and targeted-update boundaries. The performance consequence is that a known operation can avoid unrelated payload and a consumer-like full-item assembly when it is not needed. It does not, by itself, guarantee a particular latency, throughput, storage, or concurrency result; those depend on the NuData implementation, payload sizes, request composition, caching, and service behavior.

docs.title: Item hierarchy is a storage and mutation hierarchy
docs.text:
The conceptual key layout is:

ItemKeyspace
├── itemId
│   ├── __ROOT__ / itemId
│   ├── ItemQtyPrice / QTY_PRICE_<itemId>
│   ├── ItemDescription / DESC_<itemId>
│   ├── ItemCompatibility / COMPAT_<itemId>
│   ├── BusinessPolicies / BIZ_POL_<itemId>
│   ├── ItemDetails / ITEM_DETAILS_<itemId>
│   └── ItemLock / LOCK_<lockId> or lock-summary key
└── sellerId + uuid
    └── UuidMap

The hierarchy tells the service which document it can read, update, or create for an item operation. It does not mean every item reader must traverse every branch, nor that every child is a relational row to join without business rules.

docs.title: Examples: price/quantity and description
docs.text:
ItemQtyPrice is intentionally narrower than the item root. It groups available and sold quantity with the listing's price variants. A price update can address this commercial branch rather than rebuilding category, media, seller, lifecycle, and policy-reference fields in __ROOT__.

ItemDescription is intentionally separated because seller-authored content can be large and irregular. The service writes either desc or compressed compDesc, together with descRevsnDt, and can read the description without requesting the full item. A downstream consumer must therefore decide whether to decompress content and must not treat the two representations as two independent descriptions.

docs.title: Hierarchical POJOs are different from docset hierarchy
docs.text:
Two kinds of hierarchy exist in this design, and they solve different problems.

Hierarchy Example What it preserves Document hierarchy itemId ancestor with ItemQtyPrice and ItemDescription child docsets. Separate producer access, mutation, payload, and lifecycle boundaries. Embedded object hierarchy price.fixedPrice.currency, lifecycle.startDate, category.primaryCategoryId, aspects[]. Cohesive Selling concepts and their internal cardinality.

The producer POJOs are composed objects, not a single flat bag of fields. For example, BaseItem uses Amount for price values, lists for aspects, images, identifiers, and compatibility, and objects such as BusinessPolicies, Lifecycle, Format, and TermsAndPolicies.

The document converter preserves that cohesion while deciding which document owns each producer concern:

Item / BaseItem POJO
├── broad identity, lifecycle, category, images  -> ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__
├── available quantity and Amount price variants -> ItemQtyPrice
├── seller description                            -> ItemDescription
├── compatibility list                            -> ItemCompatibility
├── return, payment, and shipping policies        -> BusinessPolicies
└── precision prices and seller documents         -> ItemDetails

Within a docset, nesting prevents related values from being separated. For example, each price amount keeps its value and currency together, and price groups fixed-price, auction, marketing, and reference-price concepts. Not every listing format uses every price variant.

A flat raw schema would instead create many nullable, format-specific fields, such as fixed_price_value, fixed_price_currency, auction_reserve_value, and auction_reserve_currency. It would also force the schema to grow when a producer object gains another optional nested concept. Flattening may be appropriate in a downstream model, but it is a consumer transformation decision, not evidence that the producer document shape is incorrect.

docs.title: Code evidence: crlstngsv POJOs to NuDocs
docs.text:
The source code makes the producer orientation explicit. The Selling-domain objects in crlstngsvLib are converted into NuData-specific classes in the service layer; the mapping is not a direct persistence of a universal consumer record.

Producer aggregate or payload Write-side mapper NuData target Read-side reconstruction Item and its BaseItem composition DocumentConverter.getRoot, getQtyPrice, getDescription, getItemCompatibility, getBusinessPolicies, and getItemDetails ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__ and the corresponding item child docsets GetItemDocumentConverter offers status, summary, description-only, full-without-description, and full assembly methods. NormalizedLockRequest and UUID-specific lookup flows DocumentConverter.getItemLock and dedicated lookup processing ItemLock and UuidMap in ItemKeyspace Locks and UUID mappings are operational lookups, not a projection of every Item field. ItemGroup with member item IDs and variation attributes ItemGroupDocumentConverter.getRoot and getDescription; shared policies use DocumentConverter.getBusinessPolicies ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__, GroupDescription, and GroupBusinessPolicies ItemGroupDocumentConverter reconstructs status, summary, full-without-description, full, and description-only group payloads. ListingDraft, DraftSession, ItemDraft, and GroupDraft DraftDocumentConverter.getRoot, getGroup, getGroupDescription, compatibility creation, and getItems ListingDraft.__ROOT__, item-draft, group-draft, compatibility, and group-description docsets GetDraftDocumentConverter.getListingDraft combines root, group, description, compatibility, and item documents into a ListingDraft. ActiveListingDraft plus user ID UserListingDraftDocumentConverter.getUserListingDraftDoc UserListingDraft.UserItemDraftMap getActiveListingDraft recreates the active-draft summary, not the full ListingDraft. RevisionHistoryDataContainer and derived revision records RevisionHistoryProcessor delegates to listing, property-detail, and variation-detail processors before the NuData client insert ListingRevisionKeyspace.ListingRevision, ListingRevisionDetail, and VariationRevisionDetail; __ROOT__ is conditional retention state Revision records are generated history payloads, intentionally separate from reconstruction of the latest Item or ItemGroup.

Two concrete examples demonstrate why this matters:

  • DocumentConverter.getQtyPrice(Item, ...) creates a NuData Price object from several Item Amount values, while description and compatibility converters choose a compressed representation only when compression produces a value.
  • CoreItemProcessor explicitly creates root, description, quantity/price, details, policies, and compatibility documents for item writes. Conversely, GetItemDocumentConverter selects and assembles only the documents needed by the requested status, summary, description-only, or full read.

The converter layer is therefore a producer-owned persistence mapping layer. It encodes how Core Listing Service operates on NuData; it does not remove the need for a consumer-oriented contract.

docs.title: What downstream consumers need
docs.text:
A consumer-ready listing model should be produced from NuData rather than using raw docsets as if they were complete business tables.

Downstream responsibility Why the raw producer model does not do it automatically Select the intended state Current item/group state, draft state, user draft index, and revision history have different business meanings. Discover and assemble source documents An MSKU requires a group plus selected member items; an item can require selected child docsets. Decode and canonicalize content Description and compatibility may be expanded or compressed; optional variants and abbreviated fields need common rules. Normalize nested and repeated data Price envelopes, aspects, images, compatibility, policies, and variation traits need a deliberate entity, column, or child-record design. Define consumer business keys and grain Storage keys and generated child keys do not by themselves define a reporting, analytical, or ML entity grain. Apply quality rules and retain lineage Consumers need rules for nulls, duplicates, lifecycle filters, type conversion, and traceability back to keyspace/docset/field.

For the Item domain, the existing governed item and variation LDMs are the right direction: they provide a consumer-facing logical interface above the raw document families. The required ETL or rearrangement is the boundary that turns producer-operational data into readable, stable downstream data.

docs.title: Evidence and limits
docs.text:
• NuData write-flow research documents the five live keyspaces, all 22 declared docsets, their key shapes, and observed write behavior.
  • Listing NuData Design documents live, draft, revision, and archive storage categories and the SSKU/MSKU split.
  • Core Listing Service NuData V2 database schema documents docset roles and frequency tiers.
  • The crlstngsv source evidence comes from the V2 entity POJOs and the service converter and processor classes named in the mapping table. Those classes show the producer-to-NuDoc transformation and selected read reconstruction paths.

The original schema-design ADR is not present in this documentation set. Accordingly, this page explains the design from observed key hierarchy, payload shape, and service conversion/read-write behavior. It does not assert undocumented latency targets, cross-document transaction guarantees, or historical intent.

docs.title: Core Listing Service - NuData V2 Database Schema
docs.text: Source wiki: https://wiki.corp.ebay.com/spaces/LS/pages/2269021212/Core+Listing+Service+-+NuData+V2+Database+Schema

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This page documents the NuData (NoSQL) database schema used by the Core Listing Service V2 APIs. The service uses four primary keyspaces to store item data, item groups (MSKU/variations), listing drafts, and revision history.

Note

This documentation covers V2 API entities only. V1 legacy entities are not included.

docs.title: High-Level Keyspace Relationships
docs.text:
The four keyspaces and their interactions:

  • listingdraftkeyspace (PK: draftId) - Contains draft data before publishing
    • __ROOT__ - Draft metadata
    • ItemDraft (N) - Individual item drafts
    • ItemGroupDraft - MSKU group drafts
    • Referenced by: itemkeyspace.__ROOT__.drftId and itemgroupkeyspace.__ROOT__.grpDrftId
  • itemkeyspace (PK: itemId) - Stores individual items (both single SKU and MSKU variations)
    • __ROOT__ - Core item data (isVariation=false for single SKU, true for MSKU child)
    • ItemQtyPrice - Quantity and pricing (HOT path)
    • ItemDescription - Item description text
    • BusinessPolicies, ItemCompatibility, ItemLock, UuidMap, ItemDetailsDoc
  • itemgroupkeyspace (PK: groupId) - Stores MSKU parent/group information
    • __ROOT__ - Group metadata with itemIds[] array referencing variations in itemkeyspace
    • GroupDescription - Group-level description
    • Contains itmsVryBy[] defining variation structure (e.g., Color, Size)
  • listingrevisionhistorykeyspace (PK: lstgId) - Revision tracking
    • __ROOT__ - Container (lstgId can be itemId or groupId)
    • ListingRevision (N) - High-level revision info
    • ListingRevisionDetail (N) - Field-level changes
    • VariationRevisionDetail (N) - MSKU variation changes

docs.title: Single SKU Listing Flow
docs.text:
• Create draft: POST /v2/listing_draft -> listingdraftkeyspace (__ROOT__ + ItemDraft)
  • Publish listing: POST /v2/item -> itemkeyspace (__ROOT__ + ItemQtyPrice + ItemDescription + BusinessPolicies)
  • Revise listing: PUT /v2/item/{itemId} -> itemkeyspace (update __ROOT__, increment vrsnId) + listingrevisionhistorykeyspace (ListingRevision + ListingRevisionDetail)

docs.title: MSKU/Multi-Variation Listing Flow
docs.text:
• Create MSKU draft: POST /v2/listing_draft (with variations) -> listingdraftkeyspace (__ROOT__ + ItemGroupDraft + N ItemDrafts)
  • Publish MSKU: POST /v2/item_group -> itemgroupkeyspace (__ROOT__ + GroupDescription) + itemkeyspace (N variation documents, each with isVariation=true)
  • Revise MSKU: PUT /v2/item_group/{groupId} -> updates group and/or specific variations + records revision history (ListingRevision + ListingRevisionDetail + VariationRevisionDetail)

docs.title: Example: T-Shirt MSKU with 2 Colors x 3 Sizes = 6 Variations
docs.text:
• 1 document in itemgroupkeyspace: groupId="G100", itemIds=["200001","200002","200003","200004","200005","200006"], itmsVryBy=[{name:"Color", values:["Red","Blue"]}, {name:"Size", values:["S","M","L"]}]
  • 6 documents in itemkeyspace: itemIds 200001-200006, each with isVariation=true and specific aspect values (e.g., Color=Red, Size=S)

docs.title: Access Patterns by Frequency
docs.text:
High Frequency (Hot Path):

  • ItemQtyPrice - Read/Write on every purchase, price update
  • Item __ROOT__ - Read for item display, write for revisions
  • ItemGroup __ROOT__ - Read for MSKU display

Medium Frequency:

  • ItemDescription - Read for item display (cached), rarely updated
  • GroupDescription - Read for MSKU display (cached), rarely updated
  • BusinessPolicies - Read when policies referenced, updated occasionally

Low Frequency (Cold Path):

  • ItemCompatibility - Read only for parts fitment, rarely updated
  • ListingRevision* - Write on every revision, read only for history queries
  • ItemLock - Read/Write only during concurrent update conflicts
  • UuidMap - Read only during draft validation
  • ItemDetailsDoc - Read only when seller documents attached

docs.title: Keyspace Architecture
docs.text:
The Core Listing Service uses the following NuData keyspaces:

  • itemkeyspace - Stores individual item/listing data (single SKU and variations)
  • itemgroupkeyspace - Stores item group data for MSKU/multi-variation listings
  • listingdraftkeyspace - Stores listing draft data before publishing
  • listingrevisionhistorykeyspace - Stores revision history for listing changes

docs.title: 1. Item Keyspace (itemkeyspace)
docs.text:
The itemkeyspace stores all individual item data. Each item is stored as a document family with multiple document types (collections) for different aspects of the item.

Primary Key: PK = itemId (eBay item ID)

docs.title: __ROOT__ Collection [HOT - Read/Write]
docs.text:
• Core item data (static/slowly changing): itemId (PK), sellerId, uuid, vrsnId, drftId, title, category, epid, conditionId, format, lifecycle
  • Media and classification: aspects[], images[], videos[], location, policies
  • isVariation flag: false = single SKU, true = MSKU child variation
  • Foreign keys: drftId -> listingdraftkeyspace.__ROOT__.draftId
  • Implicitly referenced by: itemgroupkeyspace.__ROOT__.itemIds[] (if isVariation=true)

Child Collections:

  • ItemQtyPrice [HOT - Read/Write]: Frequently updated data - availQty, qtySold, fixedPrice, mrktngPrc
  • ItemDescription [WARM - Read]: Large text data - desc, compDesc, descRevsnDt
  • BusinessPolicies [WARM - Read]: Policy details - retTrms, pmtTrms, shipTrms
  • ItemCompatibility [COLD - Read]: Parts fitment - compat[], cmpCompat
  • ItemLock [COLD - Read/Write]: Concurrency control
  • UuidMap [COLD - Read]: UUID to ItemId mapping
  • ItemDetailsDoc [COLD - Read]: Seller documents

Read Patterns:

  • Get Item by ID: PK lookup on __ROOT__ + parallel fetch ItemQtyPrice, ItemDescription
  • Get MSKU Variations: Batch PK lookup for all itemIds from ItemGroup.itemIds[]
  • Update Price/Qty: Direct write to ItemQtyPrice collection

Write Patterns:

  • Create Item: Write __ROOT__, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDescription, BusinessPolicies atomically
  • Update Item: Write __ROOT__ (increment vrsnId), update specific collections
  • End Item: Update __ROOT__.endRsn, __ROOT__.admEndDt

docs.title: 2. Item Group Keyspace (itemgroupkeyspace)
docs.text:
The itemgroupkeyspace stores multi-variation listings (MSKU). Each item group contains metadata about the variation structure and references to individual variation items.

Primary Key: PK = groupID

docs.title: __ROOT__ Collection [HOT - Read/Write]
docs.text:
• Group metadata: groupId (PK), groupTitle, groupType, owner, grpVrs, grpDrftId
  • itemIds[]: Array of variation item IDs (references to itemkeyspace documents where isVariation=true)
  • itmsVryBy[]: Variation structure definition - Example: [{name:"Color", values:["Red","Blue"]}, {name:"Size", values:["S","M","L"]}]
  • Image rules: imgVryBy (which traits control images), images[] (group-level images)
  • Seller references: sellerGroupKey (seller's custom group SKU)
  • Foreign keys: grpDrftId -> listingdraftkeyspace.__ROOT__.draftId

Child Collections:

  • GroupDescription [WARM - Read]: Large text data - groupDesc, compDesc, grpDescRevsnDt

MSKU Variation Relationship:

ItemGroup.__ROOT__ with groupId="G100" and itemIds=["200001","200002","200003"] references 3 variation documents in itemkeyspace, each with isVariation=true. The itmsVryBy[] field defines the variation structure (e.g., Color, Size), and each variation's aspects[] field contains the specific trait values (e.g., Color=Red, Size=S).

Read Patterns:

  • Get MSKU:
    1. PK lookup on ItemGroup __ROOT__ to get itemIds[] and itmsVryBy[]
    2. Batch PK lookup on itemkeyspace for all itemIds[]
    3. Fetch GroupDescription
  • Display Variation Matrix: Parse itmsVryBy[] and match aspects[] from each variation

Write Patterns:

  • Create MSKU:
    1. Write ItemGroup __ROOT__ + GroupDescription
    2. Write N variation documents in itemkeyspace (all with isVariation=true)
  • Add Variation:
    1. Create new item in itemkeyspace
    2. Append itemId to ItemGroup.itemIds[]
  • Update Group Title: Update ItemGroup.__ROOT__.groupTitle
  • Update Variation Price: Update specific item's ItemQtyPrice in itemkeyspace

docs.title: Relationship: Item Group -> Items
docs.text:
Parent-Child Relationship:

  • ItemGroup __ROOT__ contains itemIds array with all variation item IDs
  • Each variation is stored as a separate document in itemkeyspace
  • Variations have isVariation=true flag in their item __ROOT__ document
  • The itmsVryBy field defines variation traits (e.g., Color, Size)
  • Individual variations store their specific trait values in their aspects field

Example MSKU Structure:

A t-shirt with Color (Red, Blue) and Size (S, M, L) variations:

  • 1 ItemGroup document with groupId="100001"
  • itemIds = ["200001", "200002", "200003", "200004", "200005", "200006"]
  • itmsVryBy = [{"name":"Color","values":["Red","Blue"]}, {"name":"Size","values":["S","M","L"]}]
  • 6 Item documents in itemkeyspace (one per variation combination)

docs.title: 3. Listing Draft Keyspace (listingdraftkeyspace)
docs.text:
The listingdraftkeyspace stores draft listings before publication. Drafts can be for single items or item groups (MSKU).

Primary Key: PK = draftId

docs.title: __ROOT__ Collection [WARM - Read/Write]
docs.text:
• Draft metadata: draftId (PK), itmId[] (published item IDs after publish), lstdItmId (published listing ID), origItmId (original item ID for relist/revise)
  • Lifecycle: crtDate, lastModDate, prgDt (purge date), lstgTm (listing time)
  • Referenced by: itemkeyspace.__ROOT__.drftId and itemgroupkeyspace.__ROOT__.grpDrftId

Child Collections:

  • ItemDraft (N) [WARM - Read/Write]: Individual item drafts - Similar structure to Item __ROOT__, with desc inline (not separate). For Single SKU: 1 ItemDraft. For MSKU: N ItemDrafts (one per variation)
  • ItemGroupDraft [WARM - Read/Write]: MSKU group draft - grpTtl, itmsVryBy[], imgsVryBy, slrGrpKey, bizPol
  • ItemGroupDraftDesc [WARM - Read]: Group description for draft

Draft to Published Item Flow:

  • Single SKU: listingdraftkeyspace (__ROOT__ + ItemDraft) -> itemkeyspace (__ROOT__ + collections)
  • MSKU: listingdraftkeyspace (__ROOT__ + ItemGroupDraft + N ItemDrafts) -> itemgroupkeyspace (__ROOT__) + itemkeyspace (N variations)

docs.title: 3.1. __ROOT__ Collection
docs.text:
The main draft document containing draft session metadata and flags.

  • PK: String - Draft ID (Primary Key)
  • itmId: List<String> - Item IDs if draft was published
  • lstgTm: Long - Listing time
  • origItmId: String - Original item ID for relist/revise
  • lstdItmId: String - Published listing ID
  • prgDt: Long - Purge date
  • totCumLstgs: Long - Total cumulative listings
  • crtDate: Long - Creation date
  • lastModDate: Long - Last modified date
  • qtySold: Integer - Quantity sold
  • itmRevsnDt: Long - Item revision date

  • descRevsnDt: Long - Description revision date

  • Draft Session Flags: lstgTmpltFls, mnMxFls, ryiStat, scrtchFl (1-4)

  • Item Flags (Bitmap): fl (1-12), pwdEx, props, saleStat, visitCnt, shipRgn

  • Scratch Details: Various legacy fields for draft management

docs.title: 3.2. ItemDraft Collection
docs.text:
Stores draft data for individual items or variations.

PK: itemDraftId

Contains similar fields to Item ROOT collection plus:

  • currPrc: Amount - Current price (for auction items)
  • fl01: Long - Variation-specific flags
  • prodDtls: Boolean - Product details selection
  • brnd: String - Brand
  • desc: String - Description (inline in draft)
  • cmpDesc: byte[] - Compressed description

docs.title: 3.3. ItemGroupDraft Collection
docs.text:
Stores draft data for item groups (MSKU).

  • PK: String - Group draft primary key
  • grpId: String - Published group ID if exists
  • grpTtl: String - Group title
  • itmsVryBy: List<NameValuesPair> - Items vary by traits
  • imgsVryBy: ImagesVaryBy - Images vary by
  • img: List<ImageMap> - Group images
  • slrGrpKey: String - Seller group key
  • bizPol: BusinessPolicies - Business policies

docs.title: 3.4. ItemGroupDraftDesc Collection
docs.text: Stores group description for draft item groups.

docs.title: 4. Listing Revision History Keyspace (listingrevisionhistorykeyspace)
docs.text:
The listingrevisionhistorykeyspace stores revision history tracking for listing changes.

Primary Key: lstgId (Listing ID - can be itemId or groupId)

docs.title: __ROOT__ Collection [COLD - Read/Write]
docs.text:
• Container: lstgId (PK) - Can be itemId (single SKU) or groupId (MSKU)
  • Referenced by: itemkeyspace.__ROOT__.itemId and itemgroupkeyspace.__ROOT__.groupId

Child Collections:

  • ListingRevision (N) [COLD - Read/Write]: High-level revision info - vrsnId (version number), rvsdDate (revision timestamp), rvsdPrptyGrps[] (changed property groups like PRICE_QUANTITY, DESCRIPTION, TITLE), appId, sigRevCnt, vrsnCrtd
  • ListingRevisionDetail (N) [COLD - Read/Write]: Field-level change details - rvsdPrptyGrp, rvsdPrpty (specific field like TITLE, FIXED_PRICE), chgTp (ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED), newVal, oldVal. One record per changed field in the revision
  • VariationRevisionDetail (N) [COLD - Read/Write]: Variation-specific changes (MSKU only) - varId (variation item ID), rvsdVarPrpty (VAR_FIXED_PRICE, VAR_AVAILABLE_QUANTITY, etc.), chgTp, newVal, oldVal, varTraitVals (e.g., "Color=Red,Size=Large"). One record per variation per changed field

Revision History Examples:

Single SKU Revision (Change title and price):

ListingRevision: vrsnId=2, rvsdPrptyGrps=[TITLE, PRICE_QUANTITY]
ListingRevisionDetail #1: rvsdPrpty=TITLE, chgTp=MODIFIED, oldVal="Nike Shoes Size 10", newVal="Nike Air Max Shoes Size 10"
ListingRevisionDetail #2: rvsdPrpty=FIXED_PRICE, chgTp=MODIFIED, oldVal="99.99 USD", newVal="89.99 USD"

MSKU Revision (Change group title + Red-Large variation price):

ListingRevision: vrsnId=3, rvsdPrptyGrps=[GROUP_TITLE, PRICE_QUANTITY]
ListingRevisionDetail: rvsdPrpty=GROUP_TITLE, chgTp=MODIFIED, oldVal="T-Shirt Collection", newVal="Premium T-Shirt Collection"
VariationRevisionDetail: varId="200006", rvsdVarPrpty=VAR_FIXED_PRICE, chgTp=MODIFIED, oldVal="19.99 USD", newVal="17.99 USD", varTraitVals="Color=Red,Size=Large"

docs.title: 4.1. __ROOT__ Collection
docs.text: • lstgId: String - Listing ID (Primary Key)

docs.title: 4.2. ListingRevision Collection
docs.text:
Stores high-level revision information.

  • vrsnId: Long - Version ID
  • rvsdDate: Long - Revised date timestamp
  • rvsdPrptyGrps: List<RevisedPropertyGroupEnum> - Revised property groups
  • Examples: PRICE_QUANTITY, DESCRIPTION, TITLE, CATEGORY, etc.
  • appId: Long - Application ID that made the revision
  • sigRevCnt: Integer - Significant revision count
  • vrsnCrtd: Boolean - Version created flag
  • updCrLstgVrs: String - Updated core listing version

docs.title: 4.3. ListingRevisionDetail Collection
docs.text:
Stores detailed field-level changes for each revision.

  • rvsdPrptyGrp: RevisedPropertyGroupEnum - Property group
  • rvsdPrpty: RevisedPropertyEnum - Specific property changed
  • Examples: TITLE, FIXED_PRICE, AVAILABLE_QUANTITY, DESCRIPTION, etc.
  • chgTp: ChangeTypeEnum - Type of change: ADDED, MODIFIED, DELETED
  • newVal: String - New value
  • oldVal: String - Old value
  • lbl: String - Label/display name

docs.title: 4.4. VariationRevisionDetail Collection
docs.text:
Stores detailed variation-level changes for MSKU revisions.

  • varId: String - Variation ID (the item ID of the variation)
  • rvsdPrptyGrp: RevisedPropertyGroupEnum - Property group
  • rvsdVarPrpty: RevisedVariationPropertyEnum - Variation property changed
  • Examples: VAR_FIXED_PRICE, VAR_AVAILABLE_QUANTITY, VAR_SKU, etc.
  • chgTp: ChangeTypeEnum - Type of change
  • newVal: String - New value
  • oldVal: String - Old value
  • varTraitVals: String - Variation trait values for identification
  • Example: "Color=Red,Size=Large"

docs.title: Single SKU Listing Flow
docs.text:
• Draft created -> Document in listingdraftkeyspace with ItemDraft collection
  • Draft published -> Document in itemkeyspace with __ROOT__, ItemQtyPrice, ItemDescription collections
  • Item revised -> New ListingRevision and ListingRevisionDetail documents in listingrevisionhistorykeyspace

docs.title: MSKU/Multi-Variation Listing Flow
docs.text:
• Draft created -> Document in listingdraftkeyspace with ItemGroupDraft + multiple ItemDraft collections
  • Draft published:
    • One document in itemgroupkeyspace (__ROOT__, GroupDescription)
    • N documents in itemkeyspace (one per variation, each with isVariation=true)
  • MSKU revised -> ListingRevision + ListingRevisionDetail (for group changes) + VariationRevisionDetail (for variation changes)

docs.title: Foreign Key Relationships
docs.text:
• Item -> Draft: Item.drftId references ListingDraft.draftId
  • ItemGroup -> Draft: ItemGroup.grpDrftId references ListingDraft.draftId
  • ItemGroup -> Items: ItemGroup.itemIds contains array of Item.itemId
  • Item -> Variation Flag: Item.isVariation=true indicates this item belongs to an ItemGroup
  • Revision History -> Item: ListingRevision.lstgId can be either Item.itemId or ItemGroup.groupId
  • VariationRevisionDetail -> Item: VariationRevisionDetail.varId references Item.itemId

docs.title: Compression Strategy
docs.text:
Large text fields are often stored in compressed format:

  • ItemDescription.compDesc - Compressed description
  • ItemCompatibility.cmpCompat - Compressed compatibility data
  • GroupDescription.compDesc - Compressed group description

docs.title: Separation of Concerns
docs.text:
The schema separates frequently-updated data from static data:

  • Static data: __ROOT__ collections (title, category, creation info)
  • Dynamic data: ItemQtyPrice (quantity, price changes)
  • Large data: ItemDescription, GroupDescription (separated for performance)
  • Complex data: ItemCompatibility, BusinessPolicies (policy details)

docs.title: Denormalization
docs.text:
Some data is intentionally denormalized for query performance:

  • Core item fields are stored in __ROOT__ even though they could be references
  • Draft data duplicates published item structure for independent draft management
  • Revision history stores both old and new values for complete audit trail

docs.title: Query Patterns
docs.text:
• Get Item by ID: Primary key lookup in itemkeyspace using itemId
  • Get Item Group (MSKU) by ID: Primary key lookup in itemgroupkeyspace using groupId, then batch fetch all variations from itemkeyspace using itemIds array
  • Get Revision History: Primary key lookup in listingrevisionhistorykeyspace using itemId or groupId
  • UUID Uniqueness Check: Lookup in itemkeyspace UuidMap collection

docs.title: Field Name Abbreviations
docs.text:
NuData field names use abbreviations to reduce storage size. Examples:

  • aspct = aspects
  • avlQty = availableQuantity
  • bizPol = businessPolicies
  • cndDesc = conditionDescription
  • itmLocn = itemLocation
  • lstgAppId = listingApplicationId

docs.title: Type Definitions
docs.text: Complex types (Amount, Duration, Format, etc.) are defined in the sellingDomainCommonLib module and shared across the application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This page describes the document collections in the ItemKeyspace, including their fields, data types, and descriptions. Each section represents a distinct document/collection in the keyspace.

Production keyspace: https://cloud.ebay.com/cloud-data/databases/nudocument/keyspaces/ItemKeyspace?tab=overview&environment=production

docs.title: Documents in ItemKeyspace

docs.title: 2. ItemQtyPrice
docs.text:
Stores quantity and pricing information (frequently updated data).

Field Type Description ItemQtyPriceID String Collection document ID availQty Integer Available quantity qtySold Integer Quantity sold qtySldByPickpStre Integer Quantity sold by pickup store minRmntSet Integer Minimum remnant set price Price Container for all pricing fields price.fixedPrice Amount Fixed/BIN price price.auctnRsrvPrc Amount Auction reserve price price.strtBidPrice Amount Starting bid price price.mrktngPrc MarketingPrice Marketing/original price price.orgnRetailPrice Amount Original retail price price.COGs Amount Cost of goods sold price.prcGuarantee Boolean Enrolled in price guarantee

docs.title: 3. ItemDescription
docs.text:
Stores the item description (separated for performance).

Field Type Description ItemDescID String Collection document ID desc String Item description text/HTML compDesc byte[] Compressed description descRevsnDt Long Description revision date

docs.title: 4. ItemCompatibility
docs.text:
Stores parts compatibility/fitment data.

Field Type Description ItemCompID String Collection document ID compat List<ItemCompatibility> Compatibility entries cmpCompat byte[] Compressed compatibilities ftExempt Integer Fitment threshold exempt

docs.title: 5. BusinessPolicies
docs.text:
Stores detailed business policy information.

Field Type Description plcsId String Policies document ID retTrms ReturnTerms Return policy details pmtTrms PaymentTerms Payment terms shipTrms ShippingTerms Shipping terms

docs.title: 6. ItemDetailsDoc
docs.text:
Additional listing details like relaxed rules and high precision prices.

Field Type Description itemDetailsID String Collection document ID hasRlxdRls Boolean Indicates if the listing has relaxed rules applied fixedPriceHP Amount Fixed price with high precision strtBidPriceHP Amount Starting bid price with high precision docs Documents Vehicle-related documents container docs.vhclTtlFrnt String Vehicle title front document reference docs.vhclTtlBck String Vehicle title back document reference docs.vin String Vehicle Identification Number document reference docs.odometer String Odometer reading document reference

docs.title: 7. UuidMap
docs.text:
Maps UUID to Item ID for uniqueness validation. The document is keyed by the UUID itself (primary key); the following fields are stored within the document.

Field Type Description listingId String Listing ID mapped to the UUID listingAppId String Listing application ID associated with the UUID

docs.title: 8. ItemLock
docs.text:
Provides locking mechanism for concurrent updates.

Field Type Description pk String Lock ID (Primary Key) st ItemLockStatus Lock status: A (ACTIVE), C (COMMITTED), X (CANCELLED) qty Long Quantity being locked expDt Long Lock expiration timestamp cmtDt Long Committed timestamp (nullable) cnclDt Long Cancelled timestamp (nullable) extDt Long Extended timestamp (nullable) extCnt Long Number of times the lock has been extended (nullable) crtDt Long Creation timestamp modDt Long Last modified timestamp (nullable) uuid String UUID associated with the lock

docs.title: Relational Data Flow Diagram: SSKU vs MSKU in NuData
docs.text: The following diagram illustrates how data is organized and stored for Single SKU (SSKU) vs Multi-SKU (MSKU) listings in NuData, across ItemKeyspace and ItemGroupKeyspace. Data is sourced from the crlstngsv (Core Listing Service) codebase.

docs.title: 1. SSKU (Single SKU) Listing - ItemKeyspace Only
docs.text:
A Single SKU listing has one item stored entirely within ItemKeyspace, keyed by itemId. No group is created. The isVariation flag is false or absent.

ItemKeyspace | Primary Key = itemId | isVariation = false / null

docs.title: Identity and Listing Data
docs.text:
• PK = itemId
  • sellerId
  • title
  • category
  • conditionId, conditionDescription
  • format (FixedPrice / Auction)
  • lotSize, lotId
  • sellerItemKey (seller's SKU)
  • aspects (item specifics)
  • images
  • lifecycle (startDate, endDate, duration)
  • marketplaceListedOn
  • tradingScope
  • inventoryTrackingMethod

docs.title: Item Metadata
docs.text:
• isVariation = false
  • creationDate, lastModifiedDate
  • draftId, uuid, epid
  • manageByInventory
  • coreListingDataVersion
  • regulatoryInfo, customPolicies
  • extendedProducerResponsibility

docs.title: SSKU Child Documents
docs.text: Document Fields ItemDescription description, compressedDescription, descriptionRevisionDate ItemQtyPrice availableQuantity, price (value + currency), quantitySold, minimumRemnantSet FulfillmentTerms shippingOptions, shippingTerms, packageSpec, weight, overrideShippingOptions BusinessPolicies payment policy ID, fulfillment policy ID, return policy ID, businessPolicyIdentifiers ReturnTerms / Tax / Others returnTerms (domestic/intl), tax (VAT, etc.), buyerRestrictions, lifecycle, paymentTerms

docs.title: 2. MSKU (Multi-SKU / Variation) Listing - ItemGroupKeyspace + ItemKeyspace
docs.text: A Multi-SKU listing stores group-level shared data in ItemGroupKeyspace and per-variation data in ItemKeyspace. Each variation item has isVariation = true. The group document references all variation item IDs via itemIds[].

docs.title: __ROOT__ Document (Group Root)
docs.text:
Identity and metadata:

  • PK = groupId
  • groupOwner (sellerId)
  • groupTitle (shared title)
  • groupType
  • sellerGroupKey (group SKU)
  • groupVersion
  • groupDraftId
  • createdDate, lastModifiedDate
  • adminEndedDate
  • httpsCompliant

Variation linking:

  • itemIds[] -> [itemId1, itemId2, ...]
  • itemsVaryBy (e.g., Color, Size)
  • imagesVaryBy (trait for images)
  • images (group product images)
  • compatibilities
  • globalIdentifiers (UPC, EAN)
  • managedFulfillmentSupported

docs.title: MSKU Group Child Documents
docs.text: Document Fields GroupDescription groupDescription (HTML), compressedGroupDescription, groupDescriptionRevisionDate; shared description for all variations GroupBusinessPolicies Payment policy ID, fulfillment policy ID, return policy ID; shared policies across variations TraitImages / ImagesVaryBy Images mapped per variation trait value (e.g., Color=Red -> image URL); imagesVaryBy -> trait name driving image variation

docs.title: Group to Variation Item Relationship
docs.text: itemIds[] links the group document to variation items in ItemKeyspace.

docs.title: __ROOT__ - Variation Item (repeated N times, one per SKU)
docs.text:
Identity:

  • PK = itemId (unique per variation)
  • isVariation = true
  • sellerId
  • title
  • category
  • conditionId
  • format
  • sellerItemKey (variation SKU)

Variation-specific data:

  • aspects (e.g., Color=Red, Size=M)
  • images (variation-level images)
  • lifecycle (start/end dates)
  • creationDate, lastModifiedDate
  • uuid, epid
  • draftId
  • inventoryTrackingMethod

docs.title: MSKU Variation Child Documents
docs.text:
Document Fields ItemQtyPrice (per variation) availableQuantity (per variation), price (per variation), quantitySold, minimumRemnantSet ItemDescription (variation) description (variation-specific), compressedDescription, descriptionRevisionDate

Note

Shared data (description, business policies, group title) is stored in ItemGroupKeyspace, not duplicated per variation item.

docs.title: 3. Key Differences: SSKU vs MSKU Storage Summary
docs.text: Attribute / Field SSKU (Single SKU) MSKU (Multi-SKU / Variation) Keyspaces Used ItemKeyspace only ItemGroupKeyspace + ItemKeyspace (one row per variation) Primary Key itemId (ItemKeyspace PK) groupId (ItemGroupKeyspace PK) + itemId per variation (ItemKeyspace PK) isVariation flag false / null true on each variation item in ItemKeyspace Number of ItemKeyspace records 1 (for the single item) N (one per variation, all with isVariation=true) Number of ItemGroupKeyspace records None 1 (one group document linking all N variations) Title Per item: ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.title Shared: ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__.groupTitle Description Per item: ItemKeyspace.ItemDescription Shared: ItemGroupKeyspace.GroupDescription Price and Quantity Per item: ItemKeyspace.ItemQtyPrice Per variation: ItemKeyspace.ItemQtyPrice (one per itemId) Aspects / Variation Traits ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.aspects (item specifics) ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.aspects (specific trait values per variation) + ItemGroupKeyspace.itemsVaryBy (trait names) Business Policies ItemKeyspace.BusinessPolicies (per item) ItemGroupKeyspace.GroupBusinessPolicies (shared across all variations) Images ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.images Group-level: ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__.images + TraitImages; variation-level: ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.images Seller Item Key (SKU) ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.sellerItemKey ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__.sellerGroupKey (group) + ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.sellerItemKey (per variation) Item Linking No group linkage ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__.itemIds[] -> list of variation itemIds Seller ID ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.sellerId ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__.groupOwner (sellerId) + ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.sellerId per variation Global Identifiers (UPC/EAN) ItemKeyspace.__ROOT__.gblIdentifiers ItemGroupKeyspace.__ROOT__.globalIdentifiers (shared at group level)

docs.title: Oracle Caty Item Tables Migration Guide
Summary
docs.text:
The Selling team is phasing out / decommissioning the Oracle UserItemHost (CatyHost) item family due to scalability challenges, high Oracle licensing costs, performance bottlenecks, and complex maintenance requirements.

The migration to a NuDocument-based solution will be executed in phases.

In the initial phase, the primary data reads/writes for all selling listing applications from the following Oracle tables will be migrated to NuDocument. This includes migrating Selling View Listing Service(SVLS) to read data from NuDocument instead of Oracle.

  • EBAY_ITEMS
  • EBAY_SECONDARY_DATA
  • ITEM_ATTR_INFO
  • ITEM_VARIATION
  • EBAY_ITEM_DESC
  • EBAY_ITEM_SHIPPING
  • EBAY_ITEM_REV_DETAIL
  • EBAY_ITEM_REVISIONS
  • ITEM_VARIATION_REV
  • ITEM_ATTR_INFO_VERSION
  • ITEM_DESC_VERSION
  • ITEM_DESC_VERSION_NEW
  • ITEM_FEATURES_VERSION
  • ITEM_SECONDARY_DATA_VERSION
  • ITEM_SHIPPING_VERSION
  • ITEM_VARIATION_VERSION
  • ITEM_VERSION
  • ITEM_SHIPPING_VERSION
  • ITEM_VARIATION_VERSION
  • ITEM_VERSION
  • EBAY_SCHEDULED_ITEM
  • ITEM_LOCK
  • ENTITY_PROFILE_LOCK

In the initial phase, Domain teams have been asked to identify their usage of data from these tables. This sheet gives insights into how different applications are using data in these tables.

In the next phase, domain teams will need to migrate their data reads and writes out of these Oracle tables completely. They can leverage ULP to phase out these Oracle tables. Also, consumers of the item life cycle BES1 events needs to be migrated

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Historically, these item tables were established long ago, and over time, numerous fields have been added without clear data ownership.

The Selling team conducted a thorough analysis of all data stored within these tables and devised a strategy to segregate seller-provided data as part of the listing flow (Core Selling data) from derived or computed data or data provided post Listing(Domain Data), which is managed by various domain teams such as Shipping, Trust, and Seller standards. A summary of the various fields and classifications of core selling and computed data can be found in this sheet

The earlier strategy for this Oracle migration involves the Selling Team owning only over core selling data or seller-provided data in listing flows, while domain teams take responsibility for domain data (derived or computed or post listing data).

The core selling data, identified and modeled as Listing documents in NuData, are concurrently dual written into both NuData and Oracle. This core selling data is then made accessible through SVLS for client applications, with over 200 clients currently retrieving core selling data via SVLS.

Domain teams were similarly tasked with establishing their own data stores to manage their respective data and transitioning client applications away from Oracle.

Despite these efforts, the transition has not significantly reduced Oracle data access. Applications such as Search and View Item (VI), Search, Checkout require access to more than just core selling data. They have adopted a model that involves accessing core selling data via SVLS and directly accessing the database for all other domain or derived data.

Key learnings from this initial migration strategy include:

  • Many applications require access to more than just Core Selling data.
  • Domain teams need a simplified method to manage their data with minimal effort.
  • It is challenging for each domain team to coordinate with every consumer of their data, especially large consumers like Search and View Item, to access data from different sources.

To address these challenges, the Selling team has developed a new platform, Unified Listing Platform (ULP).

Unified Listing Platform (ULP) is designed to serve all consumers of buyer-context independent listing data, including both core listing data as well as extended listing information. ULP provides data with low latency, high throughput, supporting both single and bulk listing data retrieval, single and multi-sku via GraphQL endpoint. ULP also broadcasts different kinds of listing change events, including CDC event stream for caller convenience. For more information about ULP, visit https://go/ulp

In H1 2024, the Selling Listing team did an exercise with all the domain teams to find the data usage of different applications from these tables. This sheet gives insights into how different applications are using data in these tables.

docs.title: What is the current migration strategy for the Selling Listing Platform team?
docs.text:
The Selling team is currently dual-writing core selling data into both NuData and Oracle, with Oracle still serving as the primary data source for read and write operations. Our goal is to make NuData the primary source for all selling read use cases. Currently, SVLS, our service for data retrieval, reads data from Oracle, but we are transitioning all data reads from Oracle to NuData, making NuData the primary source for all SVLS use cases. This change will alleviate significant pressure on Oracle..

We have identified certain domains, such as checkout, that still directly write data to Oracle (e.g., quantity updates during checkout) for the Core Selling data. We are collaborating with these teams to migrate their data writing to use our service, CAS (Central Availability Service). This migration is a prerequisite for making NuData the primary source for SVLS for Core Selling data.

The Selling team will continue dual-writing until all domains have fully migrated away from Oracle. Additionally, we are actively enhancing the ULP to provide the necessary support for readers and writers to easily transition their use cases to ULP.

docs.title: What is the current migration strategy for domain teams?
docs.text:
Domain teams responsible for writing data to Oracle should manage their data and make it accessible through services. These teams can integrate with ULP as data providers, allowing their data to be available to all ULP clients. ULP also provides support for Domain teams that store few data points like flags, counts etc for easier migration.

Domain teams that retrieve data directly from Oracle should transition away from using Oracle. They can integrate with ULP to meet most of their data requirements. If their data has not yet been migrated to ULP, temporary adapters may be available to retrieve data from Oracle(Only flags from ebay_items and variation_item are targeted). These adapters will be phased out once the domain teams have migrated their data and registered with ULP as providers. Please refer to ULP documentation for more information.

docs.title: How can I determine which tables/columns my application is using?
docs.text:
Option 1: Visit the Sherlock Pool page (of your production pool) under the DAL tab to find the list of oracle queries used in your application. You can refer to the following sample link: Sherlock Pool Page - DAL Tab.

Option 2: Use the DBinaBox tool to retrieve the list of queries used in your application or pool. You can refer to the following link: DBinaBox Tool.

docs.title: How can I migrate my application that is using SaleBOF / SaleAggregator to fetch item information?
docs.text:
The V3 DAL libraries, such as SaleAggregator and SaleBOF, consolidate data from multiple tables, including those beyond item tables, and retrieve most columns entirely from these sources. For instance, over 400 item attributes are consolidated into a single XML CLOB within the item item attributes table, requiring applications to fetch and parse this column to read/write specific attributes. Additionally, a single flag column in these item tables may contain up to 32 flags, with more than 500 such flags in total.

The existing DAL libraries, like SaleBOF, load all these columns completely, which complicates pinpointing the precise data needed for specific applications. Out of approximately 1200 data points stored in these 6 tables, only about 300 are provided by the seller, with the remainder often going unused. Our goal is to migrate only the necessary data and phase out what is not used.

Given these complexities, updating these libraries to automatically fetch the required data is not feasible. To facilitate a smoother transition for applications, we have introduced the Unified Listing Platform (ULP). This service provides centralized access to all Listing/Item-related information, streamlining the data retrieval process for applications transitioning from older DAL libraries.

docs.title: Mapping of SaleBo fields to ULP/SVLS fields
docs.text: We are currently working on this mapping. In the meantime, you can refer to the following wiki for more information: Mapping Wiki.

docs.title: My application needs item data in realtime. How can I get the real time data ?
docs.text: ULP currently uses cached data and is eventually consistent. We are working on enabling real-time retrieval of item data based on specific needs. Please share your use case with us so we can assess how ULP can support it.

docs.title: My Application listens to Item BES events and fetches item data, can I get the data from ULP?
docs.text:
We recommend migrating to the ULP events from the legacy BES item events. For more details, please refer to this link.

Please note that ULP currently uses cached data and is eventually consistent.

docs.title: We currently use Oracle GoldenGate events to capture item changes. How can I migrate this process??
docs.text: ULP generates NuData CDC streams(WIP/POC), which are equivalent to Oracle GoldenGate events and can be utilized in your application.

docs.text: We are working on creating DW tables, will be available soon

docs.title: What are recommended migration paths for consumers of legacy listing BES 1 events?
docs.text: List of all Caty BES events: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FrvVsiH2D_3JV7zguvEqdxPiWz0q9BUcnMgi2_5sIcI/edit?gid=0#gid=0 ( For non ULP BES, if you have more questions reach out to Souhaila Moalla- NuData)

docs.title: The Listing Platform currently generates the following events using the legacy BES 1 framework, which relies on Oracle transactional PL/SQL
docs.text:
• ITEM
  • ITEM.NEW
  • ITEM.REVISED
  • ITEM.EXTENDED
  • ITEM.CLOSURE
  • ITEM.SOLD
  • ITEM.SCHED.TOACTIVE
  • ITEM.CATEGORY.UPDATED
  • ITEM.HOLDSTATUS.UPDATED
  • DRAFT
  • DRAFT.CREATE
  • DRAFT.UPDATE

These events are accessible to BES 2 consumers through the BES 2 event bridge or Event Type BES2 Replication

docs.title: Unified listing platform is generating following BES 2 events
docs.text:
• ULP.LISTING.NEW
  • ULP.LISTING.UPDATED
  • ULP.LISTING.ENDED
  • ULP.LISTING.HOLDSTATUS.UPDATED
  • ULP.LISTING.CATEGORY.UPDATED

With the ongoing deprecation of the corresponding Oracle tables, it is necessary for consumers of these BES 1 events to transition to alternative solutions.

There are three options:

docs.title: Option 1( Recommended )
docs.text: Consumers of the legacy Listing BES1 events are advised to migrate to the corresponding ULP BES2 events. This migration requires integrating with the ULP to access item details as needed, involving changes to the consumer to accommodate the new BES2 event format. Please note that while Listing BES1 and ULP BES2 are distinct events with different payloads, they are generated for the same use cases. Consumers must manage the transition carefully to ensure a smooth switch and avoid any data duplication or loss during the process.

docs.title: Option 2
docs.text: For consumers where the transition demands minimal changes, the BES platform offers support that facilitates a straightforward migration to BES 2. However, once the underlying Oracle tables and BES 1 events are phased out, our application will generate these events in a non-transactional manner, which may lead to potential availability issues. This option should be chosen only if your application can tolerate such availability concerns.

docs.title: Option 3
docs.text: For consumers requiring more real-time event handling of item updates where no direct BES 2 equivalent exists, the Listing Platform will create new events leveraging NuData's Transactional BES capabilities. These will be new BES 2 events, and consumers will need to migrate to consume these new events.
